member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.BarcodeGenerator.QRCodeLogo
member.summary: The QRCodeLogo class represents a logo image that can be used in a QR code. It can be initialized with an image size and image path, a base64-encoded image, an online image URL, or an icon.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to use the QRCodeLogo component in Razor syntax:
<SfQRCodeGenerator Width="150px" Height="150px" Value="Syncfusion"> <QRCodeLogo Width="50" Height="50" ImageSource="images/syncfusion.png"></QRCodeLogo> </SfQRCodeGenerator>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.BarcodeGenerator.QRCodeLogo.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the image displayed in the center of the QR code.
member.value: The default value is one-third of the QR code width.
member.remarks: The image size should be equal to or less than 30% of the QR code's width. If the specified width exceeds 30%, the QR code may not be scanned properly. Therefore, the lesser value between 30% of the QR code's width and the specified width will be used for rendering.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the image width for the QR code in Razor syntax:
<SfQRCodeGenerator Width="150px" Height="150px" Value="Syncfusion"> <QRCodeLogo Width="50" Height="50" ImageSource="images/syncfusion.png"></QRCodeLogo> </SfQRCodeGenerator>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.BarcodeGenerator.QRCodeLogo.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the image displayed in the center of the QR code.
member.value: The default value is one-third of the QR code height.
member.remarks: The image size should be equal to or less than 30% of the QR code's height. If the specified height exceeds 30%, the QR code may not be scanned properly. Therefore, the lesser value between 30% of the QR code's height and the specified height will be used for rendering.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the image height for the QR code in Razor syntax:
<SfQRCodeGenerator Width="150px" Height="150px" Value="Syncfusion"> <QRCodeLogo Width="50" Height="50" ImageSource="images/syncfusion.png"></QRCodeLogo> </SfQRCodeGenerator>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.BarcodeGenerator.QRCodeLogo.ImageSource
member.summary: Gets or sets the image source that will be displayed in the center of the QR code.
member.value: A string representing the image source. The default value is string.Empty.
member.remarks: The logo can be specified as an image path, a base64-encoded image, an online image URL, or an icon.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the image source for the QR code in Razor syntax:
<SfQRCodeGenerator Width="150px" Height="150px" Value="Syncfusion"> <QRCodeLogo ImageSource="images/syncfusion.png"></QRCodeLogo> </SfQRCodeGenerator>

             <QRMargin Left = "10" Top="10" Right="10" Bottom="10"></QRMargin>

             }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.SfMediaQuery
member.summary: The Blazor Media Query component allows developers to create responsive layouts. The component tracks changes in the browser size and notifies when the browser size matches the specified media query. The class is used to store information about each media query breakpoint, including the Breakpoint name and the MediaQuery itself. The property returns the Breakpoint of the MediaBreakpoint in the MediaBreakpoints collection that matches the current browser size. This allows developers to easily create responsive layouts that adapt to different screen sizes and device types.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.GlobalOptions.Animation

member.value: Default, if the animation works in all the Syncfusion Blazor components based on its animation property value. Enable/Disable, to control the animation in all the Syncfusion Blazor components. The default value is 'Default'.

For example, If GlobalOptions.Animation is �Enable� and Blazor Chart animation is false, the animation applies to the Blazor Chart component. If GlobalOptions.Animation is �Disable� and Blazor Chart animation is true, the animation doesn't applies to the Chart component.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfCheckBox`1
member.summary: Represents a configurable CheckBox component which allows the user to select, deselect, or display an indeterminate state. This component supports checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states, and can be used in forms or as a standalone UI input to collect binary or triple-state responses.
member.remarks: The component supports checked, unchecked, and indeterminate states. It provides support for two-state and tristate selection patterns with flexible property configuration, including custom label positioning, enable/disable tri-state, RTL support, and accessibility options. The checkbox state can be two or three states based on the property and is intended for both standalone use and within forms.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to instantiate a basic checkbox that is initially checked.
<SfCheckBox Checked="true"> </SfCheckBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfCheckBox`1.Label
member.summary: Gets or sets the label text that is displayed next to the checkbox.
member.value: A string representing the label content for the checkbox. The default value is String.Empty.
member.remarks: This property specifies the descriptive text shown beside the checkbox element. Assign a value to visually describe the purpose of the checkbox to users.

example.code: <SfCheckBox Label="Accept Terms"> </SfCheckBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfCheckBox`1.LabelPosition
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that determines the placement of the label in relation to the checkbox.
member.value: One of the enumeration values which can be or . The default value is .
member.remarks: If set to , the label appears to the left side of the checkbox; if set to , the label appears to the right side. Use this property to customize the layout and improve accessibility.

example.code: <SfCheckBox Label="I agree" LabelPosition="LabelPosition.After"> </SfCheckBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfCheckBox`1.Indeterminate
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether the checkbox is in the indeterminate state.
member.value: true if the checkbox state is indeterminate; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Setting places the checkbox in the indeterminate state, which overrides the Checked property during the initial render. Use this state when the selection is partial or undefined.

example.code: <SfCheckBox Indeterminate="true"> </SfCheckBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfCheckBox`1.EnableTriState
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the checkbox supports tristate (checked, unchecked, and indeterminate).
member.value: true if the tristate mode is enabled. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If enabled, the checkbox can display three states: checked, unchecked, and indeterminate. This state depends on the combination of the Checked and properties. Tristate mode is useful for representing partial selections, such as in select-all scenarios.

example.code: <SfCheckBox EnableTriState="true"> </SfCheckBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfCheckBox`1.ValueChange
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is invoked when the checked, unchecked, or indeterminate state of the checkbox changes due to a UI interaction.
member.value: An EventCallback<ChangeEventArgs<TChecked>> that is triggered whenever the state of the checkbox is altered by the user. The callback argument contains the updated checked state and the UI event.
member.remarks: This event is only raised from UI-based interactions (such as mouse/touch clicks), and not from programmatic changes. Handle this event to react to state changes for form submission, validation, or other logic.

example.code:
<SfCheckBox ValueChange="@Changed">
            </SfCheckBox>
            @code {
                private void Changed(ChangeEventArgs<bool> args)
                {
                    // Handle checkbox value change.
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1
member.summary: Provides a base class for form input components in Syncfusion Blazor, encapsulating common functionality and API contracts for input controls with checked/value states.
member.remarks: This abstract class defines core implementation for form-oriented input elements—such as checkboxes and radio buttons—offering consistent property contracts for Checked/Value/CssClass/Name, support for form integration, RTL rendering, persistence, and extensible rendering. Component developers should inherit this base to ensure seamless interop, accessibility, and persistence with Syncfusion’s form controls.
member.example: See SfCheckBox or SfRadioButton for real-world usage and parameter pattern derived from .

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content to be rendered inside this input component, typically containing HTML elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS class string(s) used for customizing the visual appearance of this input component.
member.value: Accepts a CSS class string or whitespace-separated classes to apply appearance customization. The default value is String.Empty.
member.remarks: The property allows custom styling of the input container to match application theming or branding needs.

example.code: <SfCheckBox CssClass="e-custom" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the HTML name attribute of the input element, used for form submission scenarios.
member.value: A string representing the input's form field name. The default value is String.Empty.
member.remarks: Set the property to identify this component's value when the surrounding form is submitted. This is essential for integration with HTML forms and server-side model binding.

example.code: <SfRadioButton Name="myRadioValue" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the value to submit for the input control when included in form data.
member.value: A string representing the value assigned to the input. The default value is String.Empty.
member.remarks: The property allows setting or retrieving the value sent to the server during a form submission.

example.code: <SfCheckBox Value="mycheckboxValue" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.Checked
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether this input component is checked/selected.
member.value: A value of type TChecked (such as bool for Checkbox or string for RadioButton). The default is false for checkboxes.
member.remarks: The property controls the selection state and determines whether the control is rendered as checked (or selected) in the UI. Changing this value updates the state and triggers form events.

example.code: <SfCheckBox Checked="true" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.Disabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a boolean value indicating whether this component is disabled and non-interactive.
member.value: true if the control should be disabled (unresponsive to user input); otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When is set to true, the component is not interactive and visually appears disabled on the UI.

example.code: <SfRadioButton Disabled="true" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to render the component in right-to-left (RTL) layout.
member.value: true enables RTL layout for languages such as Arabic or Hebrew; otherwise, false. The default is false.
member.remarks: Use to align the directionality of the component with right-to-left language application support.

example.code: <SfCheckBox EnableRtl="true" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether component's checked state should be persisted across browser reloads.
member.value: true to enable client persistence using browser local storage, otherwise false. Default is false.
member.remarks: This stores the property value in the user's local storage, enabling the control to remember its state between page reloads.

example.code: <SfRadioButton EnablePersistence="true" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfInputBase`1.HtmlAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets the collection of additional HTML attributes applied to the input container element.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab
member.summary: Represents the Blazor Floating Action Button (FAB), which is an extension of the component that floats above page content and enables quick access to the primary action.
member.remarks: The Floating Action Button (FAB) is positioned above all page content and is primarily used for the most frequent action on a page. This component supports various visual and positional customizations and can be integrated flexibly with other Syncfusion components.
member.example:
A simple FAB with text content.
<SfFab Content="Click" />
FAB with icon.
<SfFab IconCss="e-icons e-search" />
FAB with icon and text.
<SfFab IconCss="e-icons e-search" Content="Search" />
FAB with info button style.
<SfFab CssClass="e-info" IconCss="e-icons e-search" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.IsPrimary
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that determines whether the primary style is applied to the Floating Action Button (FAB).
member.value: true if the primary style is applied to the FAB component; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: Use this property to visually emphasize the main action by rendering the FAB in a primary style. The primary style is meant to highlight the most important action on the page.
member.example:
Set a FAB as secondary style.
<SfFab IsPrimary="false" Content="Secondary" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.Target
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS selector that identifies an element on the page in which the FAB will be positioned.
member.value: A string value representing the selector of the target element. The default value is null, in which case the FAB is positioned relative to the browser viewport.
member.remarks: The specified target element must have a CSS position of relative or absolute to ensure the FAB is positioned within it. If not, the FAB will be placed relative to the next closest ancestor with a relative position.
member.example: A simple FAB targeting a sibling element.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.Visible
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the FAB is visible.
member.value: true if the FAB is visible; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: Set this property to false to programmatically hide the Floating Action Button. When true, the FAB is rendered and visible on the page.
member.example:
Hide the FAB conditionally.
<SfFab Visible="false" Content="Hidden FAB" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.Position
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the FAB relative to its element or the viewport.
member.value: One of the enumeration values that specifies the location of the FAB. The default value is .
member.remarks: Set this property to position the FAB at various locations within the target container or viewport. To manually refresh the FAB position after the is resized, use the method. The FAB position will automatically update when the browser is resized.
member.example:
Set the FAB to appear in the top right corner of its target container.
<SfFab Target="#myContainer" Position="FabPosition.TopRight" />

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.RenderBase
member.summary: Returns the render fragment for the base button element, allowing the Floating Action Button (FAB) to reuse all visual and accessibility logic from .
member.remarks: This fragment is used internally to ensure the FAB leverages the full feature set and templating system of the parent button component.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.OnInitializedAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously initializes state for the component, setting up element ID, position tracking, and required scripts.
member.remarks: This method ensures the FAB is properly registered for use in Blazor component trees, including setup for client interop scripts and internal state for position/target.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous operation.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.OnParametersSetAsync
member.summary: Handles updated parameter values for the FAB when property bindings change, ensuring correct position and visibility.
member.remarks: This lifecycle override keeps FAB UI in sync with component state, propagating property changes and revalidating required client-side configuration.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous operation.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.OnAfterScriptRendered
member.summary: Invoked after required scripts for the FAB are rendered. Completes initialization and synchronizes client state with server.
member.remarks: This method ensures correct interop setup and applies initial properties such as position and visibility to the FAB element once scripts are loaded client-side.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous operation.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.ComponentDispose
member.summary: Cleans up resources used by the FAB, unregistering client interop and removing window event hooks.
member.remarks: This override safely tears down all client-side objects created by the FAB and its JavaScript modules to prevent memory leaks.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfFab.RefreshPositionAsync
member.summary: Refreshes the FAB's position. Call this method to recalculate and reapply the FAB's coordinates when its is resized or repositioned.
member.remarks: Use this after dynamic layout changes, or after updating the property, to guarantee visual accuracy for the FAB.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous repositioning operation.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfIcon.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content to be rendered inside the component.
member.value: A representing the content to be rendered within the icon. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to provide custom or additional content inside the element, such as labels or accessible elements alongside the icon glyph.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfIcon.HtmlAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of additional HTML attributes that will be applied to the icon element.
member.value: A Dictionary of and containing additional attributes for the icon element. The default value is an empty dictionary.
member.remarks: Additional attributes can be added by specifying them as inline attributes or by specifying the @attributes directive. These attributes allow further customization such as styles, ARIA labels, or data attributes. If the class attribute is specified, its value will be merged into the icon's CSS class attribute.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfIcon.IconCss
member.summary: Gets or sets a CSS class string that can be used to display a custom icon or apply custom styles to icons rendered by this component.
member.value: A string containing one or more CSS class names, separated by spaces. The default value is string.Empty.
member.remarks: The property is used to append custom classes to the icon element, allowing the use of custom font icons such as FontAwesome, Open Iconic, or applying targeted custom styling. If this property is set while using built-in icon names, both classes will be applied.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfIcon.Name
member.summary: Gets or sets the name of a predefined Syncfusion icon to render in the component.
member.value: An enum value specifying the icon glyph to display. The default is determined by the consuming markup.
member.remarks: Set the property to a value from the enumeration to render a built-in Syncfusion icon glyph. To use a custom or third-party icon, use the property instead. When both and are specified, both glyph classes will be applied.

example.code: <SfIcon Name="IconName.Bold"></SfIcon>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfIcon.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the size of the icon in the component.
member.value: An enumeration value that specifies the size of the icon. The default value is .
member.remarks: The property is only effective when using a built-in icon via the property. If a custom icon is used via , the icon's size is determined by the applied custom CSS. Use this property to visually scale Syncfusion predefined icons.

example.code: <SfIcon Name="IconName.Paste" Size="IconSize.Large"></SfIcon>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfIcon.Title
member.summary: Gets or sets the title attribute for the icon, used to display tooltips and improve accessibility of the .
member.value: A string representing the title attribute value. The default is string.Empty.
member.remarks: The property provides a tooltip on mouse-over and assists screen readers to describe the icon content, which helps to enhance accessibility for users with assistive technologies.

example.code: <SfIcon Name="IconName.Cut" Title="Cut"></SfIcon>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfRadioButton`1
member.summary: Represents a RadioButton component, which is a graphical interface element that allows users to select a single option from a group. It supports checked and unchecked states for user interaction and custom logic.
member.remarks: This generic component allows flexible data binding to various types for checked state tracking. The RadioButton supports RTL, persistence, label positioning, and can be easily customized via its component parameters. This class should be used when you want to offer a mutually exclusive choice selection within a UI form or group.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to initialize a basic radio button using the Checked property.
<SfRadioButton Checked="true"> </SfRadioButton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfRadioButton`1.Label
member.summary: Gets or sets the label displayed next to the radio button.
member.value: A string that specifies the display label of the radio button. The default is String.Empty.
member.remarks: Use this property to assign custom text to the radio button's label, allowing users to distinguish between radio button options. Leaving this value empty will hide the label from the rendered output.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfRadioButton`1.LabelPosition
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the label in relation to the radio button.
member.value: One of the enumeration values. The default is .
member.remarks: If the is , the label appears to the left of the radio button. If set to , the label appears to the right of the radio button. This property helps control the element flow for better localization and accessibility.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SfRadioButton`1.ValueChange
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is invoked when the state of the radio button changes due to user interaction.
member.value: An EventCallback<ChangeArgs<TChecked>> that is triggered when the state of the radio button is changed by the user. The callback receives a ChangeArgs<TChecked> argument.
member.remarks: This event is raised only in response to user-based click actions on the radio button. You can use it to perform custom logic or UI updates whenever the checked state is modified by end-users.

<SfSpeedDial Mode="SpeedDialMode.Linear"> <SpeedDialItems> <!-- Action items here --> </SpeedDialItems> </SfSpeedDial>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SpeedDialMode.Linear
member.summary: Renders the speed dial items as a linear list either vertically or horizontally, based on the linear direction.
member.value: The option presents the speed dial actions as a traditional stacked or row layout.
member.remarks: When set to linear mode, the displays all action items in a straight line (either column or row based on ).

example.code: <SfSpeedDial Mode="SpeedDialMode.Linear"> <SpeedDialItems> <!-- Items --> </SpeedDialItems> </SfSpeedDial>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SpeedDialMode.Radial
member.summary: Renders the speed dial items in a radial (circular) layout, similar to a radial menu.
member.value: The option displays the speed dial actions as a circle around the main button.
member.remarks: Selecting radial mode arranges the speed dial action buttons around the main dial button, forming a circular pattern.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SpeedDialRadialSettings
member.summary: Provides configuration options to precisely customize the placement, spacing, and direction of speed dial action buttons when the Mode is set to . This class enables advanced control over the radial layout of action items linked to the component.
member.remarks: Use the to refine the spatial arrangement of floating action items displayed in radial mode, including controlling the arc span, distance of menu items from the main button, angular origin, and orientation of the radial layout. This property is applicable when the is set to .

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Buttons.SpeedDialRadialSettings.EndAngle
member.summary: Gets or sets the end angle, in degrees, used to determine the final position of speed dial action items relative to the main button along the radial arc.
member.value: An int value between 0 and 360, specifying the end angle for the radial arrangement of the speed dial items. The default value is -1, which means the angle is determined automatically.
member.remarks: If the property value is set outside the valid range (0–360), it will be ignored, and the end angle will be calculated automatically based on the . Use this property to control where the last speed dial menu item appears along the arc.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateRangePicker`1.InputFormats
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of input formats to be used for parsing date values in the component.
member.value: An array of strings representing the acceptable input formats for date values. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows the to interpret typed date values using a specified array of formats. The formats can include both standard and custom formats supported in C#. When both and properties are specified, the property takes priority. If only is specified, parsing will be attempted using the formats provided in the array. If neither property is specified, the default behavior remains unchanged. The parsing logic prioritizes the formats in the order they are specified in the array. If a successful parsing occurs, the updates its value accordingly. Error handling is controlled by the property, allowing for different user experiences in case of invalid input.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the InputFormats property to accept multiple date formats:
<SfDateRangePicker InputFormats='new string[] { "dd/MM/yyyy", "MM/dd/yyyy", "yyyy-MM-dd" }' TValue="DateTime?" />

member.summary: The DateTimePicker is a graphical user interface component that allows users to select both date and time values through an interactive popup interface.
member.remarks: The SfDateTimePicker component extends the functionality of a standard DatePicker by providing additional time selection capabilities. It supports features like time step intervals, minimum and maximum time constraints, Islamic calendar mode, and various formatting options. The component provides separate popups for date and time selection, making it easy for users to specify precise date-time values.
member.example:
Basic usage of the DateTimePicker component:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime" Value="DateTime.Now" Format="dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm"> </SfDateTimePicker>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateTimePicker`1.ScrollTo
member.summary: Gets or sets the scroll bar position in the time popup list when no value is selected or the given value is not present in the DateTimePicker popup list.
member.value: A value that represents the scroll position in the time popup list. The default value is null.
member.remarks: The property determines the initial scroll position of the time popup list. When set, the time popup will scroll to the specified time value, making it visible in the dropdown. If the specified time is not available in the popup list or if no value is provided, the component will use this property to set the scroll position.

example.code:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" ScrollTo="@ScrollPosition">
            </SfDateTimePicker>
            
            @code {
                DateTime? ScrollPosition = new DateTime(2024, 1, 1, 14, 30, 0);
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateTimePicker`1.Max
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum date and time value that can be selected in the component.
member.value: A value that represents the maximum date and time that can be selected. The default value is December 31, 2099 at 23:59:59.
member.remarks:
The property defines the latest date and time that can be selected in the DateTimePicker component. When combined with the property, the following behaviors apply:
If is greater than the current property's time, the component will prioritize the property.
If is less than the current property's time, the component will prioritize the property.
Users will not be able to select any date and time beyond this maximum value.

example.code:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" Max="@MaxDateTime">
            </SfDateTimePicker>
            
            @code {
                DateTime MaxDateTime = new DateTime(2024, 12, 31, 23, 59, 59);
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateTimePicker`1.Min
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum date and time value that can be selected in the component.
member.value: A value that represents the minimum date and time that can be selected. The default value is January 1, 1900 at 00:00:00.
member.remarks:
The property defines the earliest date and time that can be selected in the DateTimePicker component. When combined with the property, the following behaviors apply:
If is less than the current property's time, the component will prioritize the property.
If is greater than the current property's time, the component will prioritize the property.
Users will not be able to select any date and time before this minimum value.

example.code:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" Min="@MinDateTime">
            </SfDateTimePicker>
            
            @code {
                DateTime MinDateTime = new DateTime(2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0);
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateTimePicker`1.MaxTime
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum time that can be selected in the time popup of the component.
member.value: A value representing the maximum selectable time. The default value is December 31, 2099 at 23:59:59.
member.remarks:
The property restricts the time selection for all dates except the specific date defined by the property. The following behaviors apply when both and are configured:
If is greater than the current property's time component, the component will prioritize the property.
If is less than the current property's time component, the component will prioritize the property.
This property is particularly useful for setting business hours or operational time limits across all selectable dates.

example.code:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" MinTime="@MinTime" MaxTime="@MaxTime">
            </SfDateTimePicker>
            
            @code {
                DateTime MinTime = new DateTime(2024, 8, 6, 9, 0, 0);
                DateTime MaxTime = new DateTime(2024, 8, 6, 18, 0, 0);
            }

member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum time that can be selected in the time popup of the component.
member.value: A value representing the minimum selectable time. The default value is January 1, 1900 at 00:00:00.

This property is particularly useful for setting business hours or operational time limits across all selectable dates.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateTimePicker`1.Step
member.summary: Gets or sets the time interval between adjacent time values in the time popup list of the component.
member.value: An int value that specifies the time interval in minutes between two adjacent time values in the time popup list. The default value is 30 minutes.
member.remarks: The property controls the granularity of time selection in the dropdown list. For example, if set to 30 minutes, the time options will appear as 00:00, 00:30, 01:00, 01:30, and so on. Smaller values provide finer time selection granularity, while larger values reduce the number of available options in the dropdown. The step value must be a positive integer representing minutes.

example.code:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" Step="15"> </SfDateTimePicker>
<!-- This creates time intervals of 15 minutes: 00:00, 00:15, 00:30, 00:45, etc. -->

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.SfDateTimePicker`1.TimeFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the format of the time value to be displayed in the time popup list of the component.
member.value: A string value that specifies the time format pattern for the time popup list. The default value is null.
member.remarks: The property allows you to customize how time values appear in the dropdown list. You can use standard .NET DateTime format strings such as "HH:mm", "hh:mm tt", "H:mm", etc. If not specified, the component will use the default time format based on the current culture. This property only affects the display format in the time popup list and does not change the actual value format.

example.code:
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" TimeFormat="HH:mm"> </SfDateTimePicker>
<!-- Displays time in 24-hour format: 09:30, 14:45, etc. -->
<SfDateTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" TimeFormat="hh:mm tt"> </SfDateTimePicker>
<!-- Displays time in 12-hour format with AM/PM: 09:30 AM, 02:45 PM, etc. -->

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarView
member.summary: Specifies the different view levels available for calendar components.
member.remarks: The enum defines the hierarchical view levels that can be displayed in calendar components such as SfCalendar, SfDatePicker, and SfDateTimePicker. Users can navigate between these views to select dates at different levels of granularity.
member.example:
Setting the calendar view:
<SfCalendar TValue="DateTime" View="CalendarView.Year"></SfCalendar>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarView.Month
member.summary: Displays the calendar in month view, showing individual days of a specific month.
member.remarks: This is the default and most detailed view level, allowing users to select specific dates within a month. The month view displays all days in a grid format with day names as headers.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarView.Year
member.summary: Displays the calendar in year view, showing all months of a specific year.
member.remarks: In year view, users can select entire months rather than individual dates. This view is useful when month-level selection is required or when navigating to different months quickly.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarView.Decade
member.summary: Displays the calendar in decade view, showing a range of years within a decade.
member.remarks: The decade view provides the highest level of navigation, allowing users to select entire years. This view is typically used for quick navigation across multiple years or when year-level selection is needed.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarType
member.summary: Specifies the calendar system to be used in calendar components.
member.remarks: The enum allows selecting between different calendar systems such as Gregorian and Islamic (Hijri). It determines how dates are calculated, displayed, and handled in components such as SfCalendar, SfDatePicker, and SfDateTimePicker. The calendar type affects date calculations, month names, and cultural formatting.
member.example:
Setting the calendar type to Islamic:
<SfCalendar TValue="DateTime" CalendarMode="CalendarType.Islamic"></SfCalendar>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarType.Gregorian
member.summary: Represents the Gregorian calendar system, which is the internationally accepted civil calendar.
member.remarks: This is the default calendar type used worldwide. The Gregorian calendar has 12 months with varying day counts, and includes leap years every four years (with some exceptions). It starts from January 1st as the new year.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.CalendarType.Islamic
member.summary: Represents the Islamic (Hijri) calendar system used in Islamic cultures.
member.remarks: The Islamic calendar is a lunar calendar consisting of 12 months with approximately 354 or 355 days in a year. It starts from the year of Prophet Muhammad's migration to Medina (622 CE in the Gregorian calendar). Each month begins with the sighting of the new moon.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DayHeaderFormats
member.summary: Specifies the display format for day names in the calendar header.
member.remarks: The enum controls how day names are displayed in the header row of calendar components. This affects the visual appearance and space utilization of the calendar, allowing customization based on available space and user preferences. Different formats provide varying levels of detail for day identification.
member.example:
Setting the day header format:
<SfCalendar TValue="DateTime" DayHeaderFormat="DayHeaderFormats.Abbreviated"></SfCalendar>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DayHeaderFormats.Short
member.summary: Displays day names in short format, typically showing two characters (e.g., "Su", "Mo", "Tu").
member.remarks: This format provides a compact representation while still being easily recognizable. It's suitable for calendars where space is moderately constrained but readability remains important.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DayHeaderFormats.Narrow
member.summary: Displays day names as single characters (e.g., "S", "M", "T").
member.remarks: This is the most compact format, using only the first letter of each day name. It's ideal for mobile interfaces or very small calendar displays where space is at a premium. Note that some days may share the same initial letter in certain locales.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DayHeaderFormats.Abbreviated
member.summary: Displays day names in abbreviated format, typically showing three characters (e.g., "Sun", "Mon", "Tue").
member.remarks: This format provides a good balance between space efficiency and clarity. It's commonly used in many calendar applications as it's easily readable while not taking up excessive space.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DayHeaderFormats.Wide
member.summary: Displays day names in full format, showing complete day names (e.g., "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday").
member.remarks: This format provides the clearest representation of day names but requires the most space. It's suitable for large calendar displays where readability is prioritized over space conservation.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.BlurEventArgs

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.RangePopupEventArgs
member.summary: Provides event arguments for DateRangePicker popup events including open and close operations.
member.remarks: This class contains information about popup state changes in date range picker components. It provides control over popup behavior, including the ability to cancel the action, specify where the popup should be appended, and access the current date range value.

example.code:
<SfDateRangePicker TValue="DateTime?">
                <DateRangePickerEvents TValue="DateTime?" OnOpen="OnPopupOpen" OnClose="OnPopupClose"></DateRangePickerEvents>
            </SfDateRangePicker>
            
            @code {
                void OnPopupOpen(RangePopupEventArgs args)
                {
                    // Append popup to a specific container
                    args.AppendTo = "#custom-container";
                }
                
                void OnPopupClose(RangePopupEventArgs args)
                {
                    // Optionally cancel the popup closing
                    // args.Cancel = true;
                    Console.WriteLine($"Current range: {args.Date}");
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.RangePopupEventArgs.AppendTo
member.summary: Gets or sets the target element where the popup will be appended.
member.value: A string containing a CSS selector specifying the target element. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property accepts CSS selectors to specify where the popup should be rendered in the DOM. Use "#" for element IDs and "." for CSS classes. If not specified, the popup will be appended to the body element or the modal element if one is provided. This is useful for controlling the popup's position and z-index context within complex layouts.

example.code: @code { void PopupOpen(RangePopupEventArgs args) { args.AppendTo = "#target"; // Append to specific element // args.AppendTo = ".popup-container"; // Or append to element with class } }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.RangePopupEventArgs.Cancel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the popup action should be canceled.
member.value: true if the popup action should be canceled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: This property allows you to prevent the popup from opening or closing by setting it to true. This is useful for implementing conditional popup behavior based on application state, validation rules, or user permissions. When canceled, the popup action will be prevented and the popup state will remain unchanged.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.RangePopupEventArgs.Date

member.value: A string containing the current date range text. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property contains the human-readable string representation of the current date range selection, formatted according to the component's format settings and culture. It represents the text that is currently displayed in the date range picker's input field.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.RangePopupEventArgs.Event
member.summary: Gets or sets the original browser event that triggered the popup action.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ChangeEventArgs`1
member.summary: Provides strongly-typed event arguments for change events in calendar and time picker components.
member.typeparam: The type of the component's value (typically or nullable ).
member.remarks: This generic class provides comprehensive information about value changes in date/time picker components.                 {

                    {

                        Console.WriteLine($"Formatted text: {args.Text}");
                    }
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ItemEventArgs`1
member.summary: Provides strongly-typed event arguments for item rendering events in list-based components.
member.typeparam: The type of the item value being rendered (typically for time picker items).
member.remarks: This class contains information about individual list items as they are rendered in dropdown components such as time pickers. It allows customization of item appearance, disabling specific items, and accessing item-specific data during the rendering process. This event is fired for each item in the dropdown list.

example.code:
<SfTimePicker TValue="DateTime?">
                <TimePickerEvents TValue="DateTime?" ItemRender="OnItemRender"></TimePickerEvents>
            </SfTimePicker>
            
            @code {
                void OnItemRender(ItemEventArgs<DateTime?> args)
                {
                    // Disable lunch hour (12:00 PM)
                    if (args.Value?.Hour == 12 && args.Value?.Minute == 0)
                    {
                        args.IsDisabled = true;
                    }
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DateRangePickerModel`1
member.summary: Represents a comprehensive model for DateRangePicker component configuration and event handling.
member.typeparam: The type of the date range values (typically or nullable ).
member.remarks: This class serves as a complete configuration model for DateRangePicker components, encapsulating all properties related to appearance, behavior, validation, localization, and event handling. It provides strongly-typed access to all DateRangePicker features including range selection, popup behavior, formatting, and accessibility. The model supports both programmatic configuration and data binding scenarios.

example.code:
<SfDateRangePicker TValue="DateTime?" @bind-StartDate="Model.StartDate" @bind-EndDate="Model.EndDate"
                              AllowEdit="@Model.AllowEdit" Format="@Model.Format" 
                              ShowClearButton="@Model.ShowClearButton">
                <DateRangePickerEvents TValue="DateTime?" 
                                      ValueChange="@Model.Change"
                                      OnOpen="@OnPopupOpen"
                                      RangeSelected="@OnRangeSelected">
                </DateRangePickerEvents>
            </SfDateRangePicker>
            
            @code {
                DateRangePickerModel<DateTime?> Model = new DateRangePickerModel<DateTime?>
                {
                    AllowEdit = true,
                    Format = "dd/MM/yyyy",
                    ShowClearButton = true,
                    Placeholder = "Select date range..."
                };
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.PresetsModel
member.summary: Represents a predefined date range preset for DateRangePicker components.
member.remarks: This class defines a preset date range option that users can quickly select from a predefined list. Presets are commonly used to provide convenient shortcuts for frequently selected date ranges such as "Last 7 Days", "This Month", "Last Quarter", etc. Each preset contains a start date, end date, and a display label for user interface presentation.

example.code:
<SfDateRangePicker TValue="DateTime?" Presets="@DatePresets">
            </SfDateRangePicker>
            
            @code {
                List<PresetsModel> DatePresets = new List<PresetsModel>
                {
                    new PresetsModel { Label = "Today", Start = DateTime.Today, End = DateTime.Today },
                    new PresetsModel { Label = "Last 7 Days", Start = DateTime.Today.AddDays(-6), End = DateTime.Today },
                    new PresetsModel { Label = "Last 30 Days", Start = DateTime.Today.AddDays(-29), End = DateTime.Today },
                    new PresetsModel { Label = "This Month", Start = new DateTime(DateTime.Today.Year, DateTime.Today.Month, 1), End = DateTime.Today }
                };
            }

                {
                    Format = "dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm",
                    Step = 15, // 15-minute intervals
                    ShowTodayButton = true,
                    AllowEdit = true
                };
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.DatePickerModel
member.summary: Represents a comprehensive model for DatePicker component configuration.
member.remarks: This class serves as a complete configuration model for DatePicker components, encapsulating all properties related to appearance, behavior, validation, localization, and accessibility. It provides strongly-typed access to all DatePicker features including date selection, formatting options, input validation, and user interface customization. The model supports both programmatic configuration and data binding scenarios for comprehensive date input functionality.

example.code:
<SfDatePicker TValue="DateTime?" @bind-Value="@SelectedDate"
                         AllowEdit="@Model.AllowEdit" Format="@Model.Format"
                         ShowClearButton="@Model.ShowClearButton" Placeholder="@Model.Placeholder">
            </SfDatePicker>
            
            @code {
                DateTime? SelectedDate = DateTime.Today;
                
                DatePickerModel Model = new DatePickerModel
                {
                    AllowEdit = true,
                    Format = "dd/MM/yyyy",
                    ShowClearButton = true,
                    Placeholder = "Select a date...",
                    StrictMode = false
                };
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.TimePickerModel`1
member.summary: Represents a comprehensive model for TimePicker component configuration and event handling.
member.typeparam: The type of the time values (typically or nullable ).
member.remarks: This class serves as a complete configuration model for TimePicker components, encapsulating all properties related to appearance, behavior, validation, time selection, and event handling. It provides strongly-typed access to all TimePicker features including time interval settings, format customization, popup behavior, and accessibility features. The model supports both programmatic configuration and data binding scenarios for comprehensive time input functionality.

example.code:
<SfTimePicker TValue="DateTime?" @bind-Value="@Model.Value"
                         Format="@Model.Format" Step="@Model.Step"
                         ShowClearButton="@Model.ShowClearButton">
                <TimePickerEvents TValue="DateTime?" 
                                 ValueChange="@Model.Change"
                                 ItemRender="@Model.ItemRender">
                </TimePickerEvents>
            </SfTimePicker>
            
            @code {
                TimePickerModel<DateTime?> Model = new TimePickerModel<DateTime?>
                {
                    Format = "HH:mm",
                    Step = 30, // 30-minute intervals
                    ShowClearButton = true,
                    AllowEdit = false // Picker-only mode
                };
                
                void OnItemRender(ItemEventArgs<DateTime?> args)
                {
                    // Custom item rendering logic
                    if (args.Value?.Hour < 9 || args.Value?.Hour > 17)
                    {
                        args.IsDisabled = true; // Disable outside business hours
                    }
                }
            }

member.summary: Defines the contract for DateRangePicker component operations and state management.

member.summary: Updates the child properties of the DateRangePicker component based on the specified preset configuration.

The preset value can contain date ranges, formatting options, or other configuration settings that should be propagated to child components.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.IDateRangePicker.CallStateHasChangedAsync
member.summary: Asynchronously invokes the StateHasChanged method to notify the component that its state has changed and requires re-rendering.

It ensures that any changes to the component's properties or internal state are reflected in the UI. The method should be called after making changes that affect the visual representation of the component.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker
member.summary: Defines the contract for TimePicker component interface that provides time selection functionality.
member.remarks: This interface extends and defines all the essential properties required for implementing a TimePicker component. It includes properties for time formatting, validation, localization, styling, and user interaction control.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.AllowEdit
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the user can edit the time value directly in the input field.
member.value: A bool value that determines if direct editing is allowed. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When set to false, the user can only select time values from the dropdown popup and cannot type directly into the input field. This property is useful for ensuring data integrity and preventing invalid time entries.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS class name that will be applied to the TimePicker component.
member.value: A string representing the CSS class name(s) to be applied to the component. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows for custom styling of the TimePicker component by applying additional CSS classes. Multiple classes can be specified by separating them with spaces.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the component's state should be persisted across browser sessions.
member.value: A bool value that determines if persistence is enabled. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the component will maintain its state (such as selected time value) even after the browser is closed and reopened. The component state is stored in the browser's local storage.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the component should be displayed in right-to-left (RTL) mode.
member.value: A bool value that determines if RTL mode is enabled. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the component layout and text direction will be adjusted to support right-to-left languages such as Arabic, Hebrew, etc. This property is particularly useful for internationalization and localization scenarios.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the TimePicker component is enabled and interactive.
member.value: A bool value that determines if the component is enabled. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When set to false, the component becomes non-interactive, cannot receive focus, and appears visually disabled. This property is useful for conditionally disabling the component based on application logic.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.FloatLabelType
member.summary: Gets or sets the floating label type for the TimePicker input field.
member.value: A enumeration value that determines the floating label behavior.
member.remarks: This property controls how the label text behaves in relation to the input field. Options include Auto, Always, and Never, which determine when and how the label floats above the input field.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the time format pattern used to display and parse time values.
member.value: A string representing the time format pattern. Common formats include "HH:mm", "hh:mm tt", "HH:mm:ss".
member.remarks: This property defines how time values are displayed in the input field and how user input is parsed. The format follows standard .NET DateTime format strings. For example, "HH:mm" displays 24-hour format, while "hh:mm tt" displays 12-hour format with AM/PM indicator.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.HtmlAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets additional HTML attributes that will be applied to the TimePicker input element.
member.value: An object containing key-value pairs of HTML attributes. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows for adding custom HTML attributes to the underlying input element. Common uses include adding data attributes, ARIA attributes for accessibility, or other custom attributes.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.KeyConfigs
member.summary: Gets or sets the keyboard shortcut configurations for the TimePicker component.
member.value: An object containing keyboard shortcut mappings. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows customization of keyboard shortcuts and key bindings for the component. It can be used to define custom key combinations for various component actions like opening the popup, navigating through time values, or confirming selections.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Locale
member.summary: Gets or sets the locale identifier for internationalization and localization of the TimePicker component.
member.value: A string representing the locale identifier (e.g., "en-US", "fr-FR", "de-DE"). The default value is based on the browser's locale.
member.remarks: This property determines the language and cultural conventions used for displaying time formats, text labels, and other localizable content. The locale affects time format patterns, AM/PM indicators, and other culture-specific display elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Max
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum selectable time value for the TimePicker component.
member.value: A representing the maximum allowed time value. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property restricts the time selection range by setting an upper limit. Users cannot select or enter time values that exceed this maximum value. Only the time portion of the DateTime value is considered; the date portion is ignored.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Min
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum selectable time value for the TimePicker component.
member.value: A representing the minimum allowed time value. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property restricts the time selection range by setting a lower limit. Users cannot select or enter time values that are below this minimum value. Only the time portion of the DateTime value is considered; the date portion is ignored.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Placeholder
member.summary: Gets or sets the placeholder text that appears in the TimePicker input field when no time is selected.
member.value: A string representing the placeholder text. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property provides a hint to users about the expected time format or selection. The placeholder text is displayed in a lighter color and disappears when the user focuses on the input field or selects a time.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Readonly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the TimePicker input field is read-only.
member.value: A bool value that determines if the input field is read-only. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, the input field cannot be edited directly, but users can still select time values from the dropdown popup. This property is useful when you want to restrict direct text input while still allowing time selection through the UI.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.ScrollTo
member.summary: Gets or sets the time value to scroll to when the TimePicker popup is opened.
member.value: A nullable representing the time to scroll to in the popup. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property determines the initial scroll position of the time list in the popup when it opens. If not specified, the popup will scroll to the currently selected time or the current system time. Only the time portion of the DateTime value is used; the date portion is ignored.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.ShowClearButton
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the clear button is displayed in the TimePicker input field.
member.value: A bool value that determines if the clear button is shown. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, a clear button (usually an 'X' icon) appears in the input field, allowing users to quickly clear the selected time value. The button is only visible when there is a selected time value in the component.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.Step
member.summary: Gets or sets the time interval step in minutes between consecutive time values in the popup list.
member.value: An int representing the step interval in minutes. The default value is typically 30 minutes.
member.remarks: This property controls the granularity of time values displayed in the dropdown popup. For example, a step of 15 would show times like 12:00, 12:15, 12:30, 12:45, etc. Smaller step values provide more precise time selection but result in longer dropdown lists.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Calendars.ITimePicker.StrictMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether strict mode is enabled for time value validation.
member.value: A bool value that determines if strict mode is enabled. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the component enforces strict validation of time input values. In strict mode, only exact time format matches are accepted, and invalid entries are automatically corrected or rejected. When both InputFormats and properties are specified, the InputFormats property takes priority for parsing. If only InputFormats is specified, parsing will be attempted using the formats provided in the array. The parsing logic prioritizes the formats in the order they are specified in the InputFormats array. If a successful parsing occurs, the updates its value accordingly. Error handling is controlled by the property.

member.summary: Gets or sets the font family for the text.

member.remarks: This property specifies the font face used in rendering the text, offering a wide variety of standard and custom fonts.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.Internal.IChartDefaultFont.FontStyle
member.summary: Gets or sets the font style for the text.
member.value: A string representing the font style for the text. The default value is "Normal".
member.remarks: The font style can be used to apply settings like Italic or Oblique to the text, affecting its emphasis and legibility.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.Internal.IChartDefaultFont.FontWeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the font weight for the text.
member.value: A string representing the font weight for the text. The default value is "Normal".
member.remarks: Use this property to define the thickness of the text characters, providing levels of boldness.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.Internal.IChartDefaultFont.Opacity
member.summary: Gets or sets the opacity for the text.
member.value: A double value representing the opacity for the text. The default value is 1.
member.remarks: The opacity determines the transparency level of the text, where 1 is completely opaque, and 0 is fully transparent.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.Internal.IChartDefaultFont.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the font size for the text.
member.value: A string representing the font size for the text. The default value is "16px".
member.remarks: This property determines the size of the text, impacting its readability within the chart component context.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.Internal.IChartDefaultFont.TextAlignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the text alignment.
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the alignment of the text. The options include: - Near - Center - Far
The default value is Alignment.Center.
member.remarks: Text alignment adjusts the horizontal placement of text within its container, affecting its position relative to other content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.Internal.IChartDefaultFont.TextOverflow
member.summary: Gets or sets the text overflow behavior to employ when the text exceeds the defined margins.
member.value:
One of the enumeration that specifies the text overflow options. The options include: - TextOverflow.Trim: Trims the text if it exceeds the defined margins. - TextOverflow.Wrap: Wraps the text if it exceeds the defined margins. - TextOverflow.None: Shows the text as it is.
The default value is TextOverflow.Trim.
member.remarks: This property manages how text should behave when it's too long for its allocated space, either by trimming, wrapping, or displaying fully.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartLegendSettings.Alignment
member.summary: Gets or sets the alignment of the legend in an .
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the legend alignment. Options include: - Near: Aligns the legend to the left or top based on the . - Center: Aligns the legend to the center of the chart. - Far: Aligns the legend to the right or bottom based on the .
The default value is Alignment.Center.
member.remarks: The alignment of the legend within the functions as follows: - Near: Aligns the legend to the top-left if is LegendPosition.Top and to the right-top if is LegendPosition.Right. - Center: Aligns the legend to the top center if is LegendPosition.Top and to the right center if is LegendPosition.Right. - Far: Aligns the legend to the top-right if is LegendPosition.Top and to the right-bottom if is LegendPosition.Right.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to set the legend alignment in an accumulation chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartLegendSettings Visible="true" Alignment="Alignment.Far"></AccumulationChartLegendSettings> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"></AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartLegendSettings.Background

member.value: A string value specifying the background color of the legend area. The default value is transparent.
member.remarks: The value can be specified in hex or rgba format, following valid CSS color string conventions.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to set the background color of the legend in an accumulation chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"></AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartLegendSettings Visible="true" Background="#4266f9"></AccumulationChartLegendSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartSeries.LegendShape
member.summary: Defines the shapes available for legends in charts.
member.value:
Specifies the legend shape for each series. The available shapes include: - Circle: Renders a circle. - Rectangle: Renders a rectangle. - Triangle: Renders a triangle. - Diamond: Renders a diamond. - Cross: Renders a cross. - HorizontalLine: Renders a horizontal line. - VerticalLine: Renders a vertical line. - Pentagon: Renders a pentagon. - InvertedTriangle: Renders an inverted triangle. - SeriesType: Renders a legend shape based on the series type.
The default value is LegendShape.SeriesType.
member.remarks: The enumeration allows you to select a specific shape for legend items in a chart. By default, it adapts to the shape being used in the series type.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.Enable
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the tooltip is enabled in the Accumulation Chart.
member.value: true if the tooltip is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Use this property to control the visibility of tooltips within the accumulation chart. Enabling the tooltip provides additional information when hovering over the chart's elements.

example.code: // The following code snippet demonstrates how to enable the tooltip in an Accumulation Chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.EnableAnimation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the tooltip will animate while moving from one point to another in the Accumulation Chart.
member.value: true if the tooltip animation is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: Using this property can be useful to eliminate animations for a simpler tooltip display.

example.code: // The following code snippet demonstrates how to disable tooltip animation in an Accumulation Chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" EnableAnimation="false"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.EnableHighlight
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable highlighting when hovered over the point element.
member.value: true if highlight options are enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If set to true, when hovered over the point element, the respective series will be highlighted using the property .

example.code: // The following code snippet demonstrates how to enable highlight in an Accumulation Chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" EnableHighlight="true"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.EnableMarker
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display a marker in the tooltip in the Accumulation Chart.
member.value: true if the marker should be displayed in the tooltip; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: If set to true, the marker shape assigned for the series associated with the hovered point is applied for the tooltip marker. If the marker is not enabled, a circle-shaped marker will be rendered by default.

example.code: // The following code snippet demonstrates how to configure an Accumulation Chart to disable the tooltip marker: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" EnableMarker="false"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.EnableTextWrap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to wrap the tooltip's long text based on the available space in the Accumulation Chart.
member.value: true if the tooltip text should be wrapped; otherwise, false. The default is typically false unless specified.
member.remarks: Using this property allows you to adjust the tooltip text to wrap automatically.

example.code: // This code snippet demonstrates how to enable text wrapping in the tooltip of an Accumulation Chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" EnableTextWrap="true"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.value: A string representing the fill color of the tooltip background. The default fill color is determined by the Accumulation Chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with a fill color of #020202.

example.code: // This example shows how to set a custom fill color for the tooltip of an Accumulation Chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" Fill="#d22253"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the format for the tooltip content in the Accumulation Chart.
member.value: A string that defines the format for the tooltip content. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks:
The property allows customization of the tooltip content. By default, the tooltip displays information for the x and y values of a point. Additional information can be included in the tooltip using a format string.
For example, the format "${point.x} : ${point.y}%" shows the point x value and a customized point y value in the tooltip.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.Header
member.summary: Gets or sets the header text for the tooltip in the Accumulation Chart.
member.value: A string representing the tooltip header text. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks: This property can provide additional context or information related to the data point being displayed. It allows you to set a custom header for the Accumulation Chart tooltip.

example.code: // This example shows how to set a custom header for the tooltip in an Accumulation Chart: <SfAccumulationChart> <AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartSeries DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" XName="Browser" YName="Users"> </AccumulationChartSeries> </AccumulationChartSeriesCollection> <AccumulationChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" Header="Sales"></AccumulationChartTooltipSettings> </SfAccumulationChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.AccumulationChartTooltipSettings.Shared

member.summary: Represents an annotation, a user-defined HTML element that can be added to a chart. This class provides options for customizing these annotations to enhance their visual appeal.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAnnotation.ContentTemplate
member.summary: Gets or sets the content template for the annotation. The content template can be any HTML element, allowing for a flexible and customizable way to display additional information or visuals on the chart.
member.value: The template content is applied for the chart annotation based on the custom template provided by the user that is being rendered. The default value is null.
member.remarks: The is used to define a custom template for the chart annotation.

example.code:
// The following code snippet shows how to set up chart with custom annotation templates:
Annotation in Pixel
 ...

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAnnotation.CoordinateUnits
member.summary: Gets or sets the annotation’s coordinate units, either in Pixel or Point.
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the coordinate units of an annotation. The options include: - Pixel: Annotation renders based on x and y pixel values. - Point: Annotation renders based on x and y axis values.
The default value is Units.Pixel.
member.remarks: Adjust the property to control how the annotation is positioned on the chart. Choosing Pixel makes the annotation placement more absolute relative to the control's boundaries, whereas Point allows it to respond dynamically to data changes and axis scaling.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAnnotation.Description
member.summary: Gets or sets information about the annotation for assistive technology.
member.value: A string providing additional details or context about the annotation that can be utilized by assistive technology.
member.remarks: Use the property to convey useful information to screen readers and other accessibility tools.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAnnotation.Region
member.summary: Gets or sets the regions to insert annotations in relation to a series or a chart.
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the regions of an annotation. The options include: - Chart: Annotation renders based on chart coordinates. - Series: Annotation renders based on series coordinates.
The default value is Regions.Chart.
member.remarks: Adjust the property to change where and how annotations are displayed on the chart.

example.code:
// This example demonstrates how to render a chart with an annotation placed within the chart region:
Highest Medal Count

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAnnotation.X
member.summary: Gets or sets the X-coordinate value for the annotation.
member.value: If the coordinate unit is set to , this property specifies the axis value. Otherwise, it specifies the pixel or percentage of the coordinate. The default value is zero.
member.remarks: This property determines the horizontal position of the annotation based on the defined coordinate units. When the is set to Units.Pixel, the X value represents the number of pixels from the chart's left boundary. If set to Units.Point, it corresponds to a value along the horizontal axis.

example.code:
// This example demonstrates how to render a chart with an annotation using only the X coordinate:
Highest Medal Count

member.summary: Gets or sets the name of the horizontal axis associated with the annotation.
member.value: The name of the horizontal axis.
member.remarks: This property requires the presence of the 'Axes' of the chart.

example.code:

Highest Medal Count

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAnnotation.Y
member.summary: Gets or sets the Y-coordinate value for the annotation.
member.value: If the coordinate unit is set to , this property specifies the axis value. Otherwise, it specifies the pixel or percentage of the coordinate. The default value is zero.

member.summary: Gets or sets the font size of the chart subtitle.
member.value: A string representing the font size of the chart subtitle. he default size is determined by the Chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with a subtitle text size of 14px.
member.remarks: Use the property to change the font size of subtitle text in the Chart. This property accepts standard CSS font-size specifications, such as values in 'px'.

member.summary: Gets or sets the font weight of the chart subtitle.
member.value: A string representing the font weight of the subtitle text. The default font weight is determined by the Chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with subtitle font weight of 400.
member.remarks: The font weight can be a number (100 to 900), or a keyword such as 'normal', 'bold', 'bolder', or 'lighter'.

example.code: // The following code demonstrates setting a custom font weight for the subtitle text: <SfChart Title="Sales Data" SubTitle="2023 Overview"> <ChartSubTitleStyle FontWeight="600" /> </SfChart>
