member.value: A double value representing the horizontal width of the rounded corner. The default value is 5.
member.remarks: This property affects the appearance of the corners of the data label's background. This property is applicable only when is enabled.

example.code: // The following example demonstrates setting a horizontal radius for the data label corners: <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@WeatherReports" XName="X" YName="Y"> <ChartMarker> <ChartDataLabel Visible="true" Rx="10"> <ChartDataLabelBorder Width="1" Color="black"></ChartDataLabelBorder> </ChartDataLabel> </ChartMarker> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartDataLabel.Ry

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartEmptyPointSettings.Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets the mode for handling empty points in the series.
member.value: An enumeration value that indicates how empty points are treated in the chart. Options include: - Gap: Leaves a gap for empty points. - Zero: Renders empty points as zero. - Average: Uses the average of adjacent points for empty points. - Drop: Drops empty points from the chart. The default value is .

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartLastDataLabel
member.summary: Defines the options for customizing and displaying the label of the last value in the series.
member.remarks: This property allows you to display a label for the last value in a series, with customizable appearance options such as background color, line color, and dash pattern.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartLastDataLabel.ShowLabel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the label and indicator for the last data point in the series are visible.
member.value: true to display the last value label and the corresponding grid line indicator; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <ChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.remarks: Use this property to toggle the visibility of the last data label in the chart series. This is particularly useful for highlighting trend endpoints or enhancing visual clarity in analytical charts.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartLastDataLabel.Background
member.summary: Gets or sets the background color of the last value label.
member.value: A string representing the background color (e.g., "#ffffff" or "transparent"). The default value is "transparent".

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <ChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" Background="red" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.remarks: Useful for enhancing label visibility, especially when the chart background contains multiple colors.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartLastDataLabel.DashArray
member.summary: Gets or sets the dash pattern for the grid line behind the last value label.
member.value: A string defining the dash array (e.g., "4,2" for dashed lines). The default value is an empty string, which results in a solid line.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <ChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" DashArray="2,5" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.remarks: This property is useful for distinguishing the indicator line from other grid lines or series lines.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartLastDataLabel.LineWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the line displayed behind the last value label.
member.value: A double value specifying the thickness of the grid line. The default value is 1.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <ChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" LineWidth="0.5" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.remarks: Thicker lines can improve visibility, especially when multiple series are present.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartLastDataLabel.LineColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the grid line displayed behind the last value label.
member.value: A string specifying the grid line color. The default value is an empty string, which means the series color will be used.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <ChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" LineColor="black" /> </ChartSeriesCollection> </ChartSeries> </SfChart>

member.remarks: This property helps provide a direct reference line across the chart to the last value, improving readability and data interpretation.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartSorting
member.summary: Configures the sorting option for the chart.
member.example:
This example shows how to sort a chart by the "Y" property in asscending order.
<SfChart @ref=”Chart” DataSource=”Data”> <ChartSorting PropertyName ="Y" Direction ="SortDirection.Descending"/> … </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartSorting.Parent
member.summary: Specifies the direction in which to sort the chart data.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartSorting.Direction
member.summary:
Get and set the sorting direction for the chart data. The available direction are,
Ascending Sort from smallest to largest. For example, from A to Z.
Descending Sort from largest to smallest. For example, from Z to A.
member.value:
An that specifies the sort order for the chart data. The possible values are:
Ascending: Sorts the chart data from smallest value to largest.
Descending: Sorts the chart data from largest value to smallest.
The default value is .
member.remarks: This property is essential for defining the sorting behavior of the chart data.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to sort the chart data in descending order based on the X axis values. <SfChart> <ChartSorting PropertyName="X" Direction="ListSortDirection.Descending"></ChartSorting> <ChartPrimaryXAxis ValueType="Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ValueType.Category" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@SalesReports" XName="X" YName="YValue" Type="ChartSeriesType.Column"></ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartSorting.PropertyName
member.summary: Gets or sets the property name being used as the sorting criterion.
member.value: A string specifying the property name for sorting, such as x, y, high, low, open, close, or size fields of the chart data source. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property determines the field by which the chart data should be sorted.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to sort the chart data in ascending order based on the X axis values. <SfChart> <ChartSorting PropertyName="X" Direction="ListSortDirection.Descending"></ChartSorting> <ChartPrimaryXAxis ValueType="Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ValueType.Category" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@SalesReports" XName="X" YName="YValue" Type="ChartSeriesType.Column"></ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

But this property allows you to provide dynamic information based on the data. For example, the format "${series.name} : ${point.x}" displays the series name and x-value of the point in the accessibility description.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to add a power trendline with an accessibility description format to a chart. <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartTrendlines> <ChartTrendline AccessibilityDescriptionFormat="Power trendline" /> </ChartTrendlines> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartStackLabelSettings

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartStackLabelSettings.Visible

member.value: true to make the stack labels visible; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

member.remarks: This property controls the visibility of the stack labels, allowing them to be toggled on or off.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartStackLabelSettings.Fill

member.remarks: This property sets the background color for the stack labels.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartStackLabelSettings.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the format used to display the stack labels.
member.value: A string that specifies the format used to display the stack labels.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartStackLabelSettings.Angle

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartDataEditSettings
member.summary: Provides options to customize the drag settings for chart series.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartDataEditSettings.Enable
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable data editing by dragging the point.
member.value: true if data editing is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, users can interactively edit data points by dragging them on the chart.

example.code: // This example shows how to enable data editing in a chart by setting the ChartDataEditSettings. <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartDataEditSettings Enable="true"></ChartDataEditSettings> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartDataEditSettings.Fill
member.summary: Gets or sets the color for the edited point.
member.value: A string representing the color of the edited point.
member.remarks:
The property specifies the color of the point interior which will be assigned while dragging and will remain for the edited point. This property accepts values in hex or rgba as a valid CSS color string.
Note: It is not applicable to line-based series types such as Line, Step Line, and Spline.

example.code: // This example demonstrates enabling data editing in a column chart and setting the fill color of edited points. <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue" Type="ChartSeriesType.Column"> <ChartDataEditSettings Enable="true" Fill="red"></ChartDataEditSettings> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartDataEditSettings.MaxY
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum Y value to which the point can be dragged for data editing.
member.value: Accepts double value. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property helps control the upper limit for the Y-axis when interactively editing data points on the chart.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable data editing in a column chart // and limit the maximum editable Y-value to 20 using MaxY property. <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue" Type="ChartSeriesType.Column"> <ChartDataEditSettings Enable="true" MaxY="20"></ChartDataEditSettings> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartDataEditSettings.MinY
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum Y value to which the point can be dragged for data editing.
member.value: Accepts double value. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property helps control the lower limit for the Y-axis when interactively editing data points on the chart.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable data editing in a column chart // and restrict the minimum editable Y-value to 30 using the MinY property. <SfChart> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue" Type="ChartSeriesType.Column"> <ChartDataEditSettings Enable="true" MinY="30"></ChartDataEditSettings> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings
member.summary: Provides options to customize the zoom settings of the chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.EnableDeferredZooming
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to update the chart with a delay while panning.
member.value: true if updating the chart with a delay while panning is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: Enabling this option can provide a smoother user experience during panning by introducing a delay before the chart is updated.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable selection zooming with deferred zooming in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings EnableDeferredZooming="true" EnableSelectionZooming="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.EnableMouseWheelZooming
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the chart can be zoomed using the mouse wheel.
member.value: true if the chart can be zoomed using the mouse wheel; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Enabling this option allows users to zoom in or out on the chart by using the mouse wheel.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable mouse wheel zooming in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings EnableMouseWheelZooming="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.EnablePan
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the chart can be panned when zoomed.
member.value: true if the chart can be panned when zoomed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Enabling this option allows users to pan across the zoomed-in chart area for better exploration of specific regions.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable pan functionality in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings EnablePan="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.EnablePinchZooming
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the chart can be zoomed through pinch gestures on touch-enabled devices.
member.value: true if the chart can be zoomed through pinch gestures; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Enabling this option allows users to zoom in or zoom out on the chart by performing pinch gestures on touch-enabled devices.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable pinch zooming in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings EnablePinchZooming="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.EnableScrollbar
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the axis should have a scrollbar when zoomed.
member.value: true if the axis should have a scrollbar when zoomed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Enabling this option allows users to navigate and visualize specific regions of the chart using scrollbar when zoomed.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the scrollbar in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings EnableScrollbar="true" ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.EnableSelectionZooming
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the chart can be zoomed by selecting a rectangular region on the plot area.
member.value: true if the chart can be zoomed by selecting a rectangular region on the plot area; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Enabling this option provides an interactive way for users to focus on specific areas of interest within the chart.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable selection zooming in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings EnableSelectionZooming="true" ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets the mode of zooming.
member.value:
One of the enumeration that specifies the mode of zooming. The options include: - XY: Chart can be zoomed both vertically and horizontally. - X: Chart can be zoomed horizontally. - Y: Chart can be zoomed vertically.
The default mode is ZoomMode.XY.
member.remarks: This property can be set to allow zooming both vertically and horizontally, only horizontally, or only vertically.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable zooming only along the Y-axis in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings Mode="ZoomMode.Y" ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.ToolbarDisplayMode
member.summary: Gets or sets the visibility mode for the zooming toolbar in the chart.
member.value:
One of the enumeration that specifies the visibility mode for the zooming toolbar. The options include: - OnDemand: The zooming toolbar is only visible while the chart has zoomed. - Always: The zooming toolbar is always visible even though the chart has not zoomed. - None: The zooming toolbar will not be visible even though the chart is zoomed.
The default value is ToolbarMode.OnDemand.
member.remarks: It determines whether the toolbar should be visible only when the chart is zoomed, always visible, or never visible.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to display the zoom toolbar always in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.ToolbarItems
member.summary: Gets or sets the list of items to be added in the toolbar for the chart.
member.value: The list of to be displayed in the chart toolbar. The available items include: - Zoom - ZoomIn - ZoomOut - Pan - Reset
member.remarks: The property allows customization of the items displayed in the chart toolbar. Users can choose from a set of predefined items, such as Zoom, ZoomIn, ZoomOut, Pan, and Reset, to be included in the toolbar.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to configure specific toolbar items in a chart's zoom settings. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" ToolbarItems="new List<ToolbarItems>() { ToolbarItems.Zoom, ToolbarItems.Reset, ToolbarItems.Pan }" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.AccessibilityDescriptionFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the format for the toolkit accessibility description of the chart zoom toolkit.
member.value: Accepts a string that defines the format for the toolkit accessibility description of the chart zoom toolkit. The default value is null.
member.remarks: Use this property to specify a format for the toolkit accessibility description of the chart zoom toolkit. The placeholder ${value} can be used to set the accessibility text for the zoom toolkit toolbar item name. For example, the format "Selected the ${value} option" will read as "Selected the ZoomIn option" for the button.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to configure the accessibility description format for the toolbar items in a chart's zoom settings. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" AccessibilityDescriptionFormat="Selected the ${value} option" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.AccessibilityRole
member.summary: Gets or sets the accessibility role for the chart zoom toolkit.
member.value: Accepts a string that defines the accessibility role for the chart zoom toolkit. The default value is null.
member.remarks: Use this property to provide an accessibility role for the chart zoom toolkit.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to configure the accessibility role for the toolbar items in a chart's zoom settings. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" AccessibilityRole="button" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.Focusable
member.summary: Gets or sets the accessibility keyboard navigation options for the chart zoom toolkit.
member.value: Accepts the boolean value to enable or disable the keyboard navigation for the chart zoom toolkit. The default value is true.
member.remarks: Use this property to toggle the keyboard navigation focus for the chart zoom toolkit.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to configure zoom settings to be focusable in the chart. <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" Focusable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" Name="England" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10" /> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomSettings.ToolbarPosition
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the zoom toolbar.
member.value: The position of the zoom toolbar, represented by a value. The default value is determined by the chart's default settings.
member.remarks: This property allows you to customize the position of the zoom toolbar in the chart. Changing this value will update the toolbar's position when the chart is rendered or updated.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomToolbarPosition
member.summary: Provides the options for customizing the toolbar position in the Chart.
member.value: Accepts the instance of class. The default value is instance of .

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomToolbarPosition.HorizontalAlign
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal alignment of the toolbar.
member.value:
Specifies the horizontal position of the toolbar. The available options are:
Left Aligns the toolbar to the left side of the chart.
Center Centers the toolbar horizontally within the chart.
Right Aligns the toolbar to the right side of the chart. This is the default value.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" Mode="ZoomMode.X"> <ChartZoomToolbarPosition HorizontalAlign="HorizontalAlign.Left"> </ChartZoomToolbarPosition> </ChartZoomSettings> </SfChart>

member.remarks: This property determines the horizontal placement of the toolbar relative to the chart's plotting area.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomToolbarPosition.VerticalAlign
member.summary: Gets or sets the vertical alignment of the toolbar.
member.value:
Specifies the vertical position of the toolbar. The available options are:
Top Positions the toolbar at the top of the chart. This is the default value.
Middle Vertically centers the toolbar within the chart.
Bottom Positions the toolbar at the bottom of the chart.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" Mode="ZoomMode.X"> <ChartZoomToolbarPosition VerticalAlign="VerticalAlign.Top"> </ChartZoomToolbarPosition> </ChartZoomSettings> </SfChart>

member.remarks: This property determines the vertical placement of the toolbar relative to the chart's plotting area.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomToolbarPosition.X
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal offset of the toolbar from its horizontal position.
member.value: A double value that specifies the horizontal distance, in pixels, from the toolbar's horizontal position. For example, if the horizontal alignment is set to Center and the offset is 30, the toolbar will shift 30 pixels to the right of the center. Negative values move the toolbar in the opposite direction. The default value is 0.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" Mode="ZoomMode.X"> <ChartZoomToolbarPosition X="30"> </ChartZoomToolbarPosition> </ChartZoomSettings> </SfChart>

member.remarks: Use this property to fine-tune the toolbar's horizontal placement beyond the predefined alignment options.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartZoomToolbarPosition.Y
member.summary: Gets or sets the vertical offset of the toolbar from its vertical position.

example.code: <SfChart> <ChartZoomSettings ToolbarDisplayMode="ToolbarMode.Always" Mode="ZoomMode.X"> <ChartZoomToolbarPosition Y="50"> </ChartZoomToolbarPosition> </ChartZoomSettings> </SfChart>

member.value: A double value that specifies the vertical distance, in pixels, from the toolbar's vertical position. For example, if the vertical alignment is set to Middle and the offset is 50, the toolbar will shift 50 pixels downward from the center. Negative values move the toolbar upward. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: Use this property to fine-tune the toolbar's vertical placement beyond the predefined alignment options.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip
member.summary: Provides option to customize the axis's crosshair tooltip.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip.Enable
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the crosshair tooltip is enabled.
member.value: true if the crosshair tooltip is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property can be used to enable or disable the crosshair tooltip on the chart's axis.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable crosshair and display a tooltip for the X-axis in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true"></ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip.Fill
member.summary: Gets or sets the fill color of the tooltip background.
member.value: A string representing the fill color of the tooltip background. The default fill color is determined by the chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with a fill color of rgba(97, 97, 97, 1).
member.remarks: The fill color accepts values in hex or rgba as a valid CSS color string.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and customize the fill color of the X-axis tooltip in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true" Fill="red"></ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip.TextStyle
member.summary: Gets or sets an instance of which controls the customization of the text style of the crosshair tooltip.
member.value: An instance of .
member.remarks: Use this property to customize specific styling attributes, such as color and font properties, for the crosshair tooltip text.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and customize the text style of the X-axis crosshair tooltip in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true"> <ChartCrosshairTextStyle Color="blue" Size="15px" /> </ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairLine
member.summary: Provides option to customize the crosshair line of the chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairLine.Color
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the crosshair line. Accepts values in hex or rgba as valid CSS color strings.
member.value: A string specifying the color of the crosshair line. The default value is inherited from .

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairSettings.Enable

member.summary: Gets or sets an instance of which controls the customization of the crosshair line of the chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairSettings.SnapToData
member.summary: Enables or disables snapping of the horizontal crosshair to the nearest data point.
member.value: A boolean value indicating whether snapping is enabled. The default is false.
member.remarks: Setting this property to true aligns the horizontal crosshair with the nearest data point for improved precision.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairSettings.HighlightCategory
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the entire category range is highlighted when hovered over.
member.value: true to highlight the entire category range on hover; false otherwise. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property is applicable only to category axes.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and highlight the entire category when hovering over data points. <SfChart> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" HighlightCategory="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairSettings.LineType
member.summary: Gets or sets the line type for the crosshair.
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the type of the crosshair line. The options include: - None: Hides both vertical and horizontal crosshair lines. - Both: Shows both vertical and horizontal crosshair lines. - Vertical: Shows the vertical line. - Horizontal: Shows the horizontal line.
The default mode is LineType.Both.
member.remarks: This property determines how the crosshair line is displayed on the chart, allowing for customization based on user preferences.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair in a Chart and display it as a vertical line. <SfChart> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" LineType="LineType.Vertical" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairTextStyle
member.summary: Provides option to cusomize the tooltip text style of the crosshair tooltip.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairTextStyle.Color
member.summary: Gets or sets the color for the crosshair tooltip text.
member.value: A string representing the color for the crosshair tooltip text. The default crosshair tooltip text color is determined by the chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with a crosshair tooltip text color of rgba(249, 250, 251, 1).
member.remarks: The fill color accepts values in hex or rgba as a valid CSS color string.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and customize the text color of the X-axis crosshair tooltip in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true"> <ChartCrosshairTextStyle Color="blue" /> </ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairTextStyle.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the font size for the crosshair tooltip text.
member.value: A string representing the font size for the crosshair tooltip text. The default font size for the crosshair tooltip text is 12px.
member.remarks: This property allows the customization of tooltip text size to ensure readability across devices with different screen resolutions.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and customize the text size of the X-axis crosshair tooltip in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true"> <ChartCrosshairTextStyle Size="15px" /> </ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairTextStyle.FontFamily
member.summary: Gets or sets the font family for the crosshair tooltip text.
member.value: A string representing the font family for the crosshair tooltip text. The default font family is determined by the chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with the font family Roboto.
member.remarks: The font family can be customized to adhere to organizational typography standards or particular aesthetic choices within charts.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and customize the font family of the X-axis crosshair tooltip in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true"> <ChartCrosshairTextStyle FontFamily="Arial" /> </ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartCrosshairTextStyle.FontWeight
member.summary: Gets or sets the font weight for the crosshair tooltip text.
member.value: A string representing the font weight for the crosshair tooltip text. The default font weight is determined by the chart's theme. By default, the theme is set to with a font weight of 400.
member.remarks: This property allows modification of text thickness across crosshair tooltips, offering enhanced visual emphasis according to user needs.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to enable the crosshair and customize the text font weight of the X-axis crosshair tooltip in a Chart. <SfChart> <ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip Enable="true"> <ChartCrosshairTextStyle FontWeight="bold" /> </ChartAxisCrosshairTooltip> </ChartPrimaryXAxis> <ChartCrosshairSettings Enable="true" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.summary: Gets or sets the format for the tooltip content.
member.value: A string that defines the format for the tooltip content. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks:
The property allows customization of the tooltip content. By default, the tooltip displays information for the x and y values of a point. Additional information can be included in the tooltip using a format string.
For example, the format "$series.name : $point.x" displays the series name and x-value of the point in the tooltip.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to customize the tooltip format in a chart to display the series name and the Y value of a point.

member.value: A string representing the tooltip header text. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks: This property can be used to provide additional context or information related to the data point being displayed.

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to set a custom header for the tooltip in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" Header="Sales" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10"> </ChartMarker> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

example.code: // This example demonstrates how to set the opacity of the tooltip in a chart. <SfChart> <ChartTooltipSettings Enable="true" Opacity="0.5" /> <ChartSeriesCollection> <ChartSeries DataSource="@Data" XName="XValue" YName="YValue"> <ChartMarker Visible="true" Width="10" Height="10"> </ChartMarker> </ChartSeries> </ChartSeriesCollection> </SfChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.ChartTooltipSettings.ShowNearestPoint

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel
member.summary: Defines the options for customizing and displaying the label of the last value in the stock chart series.
member.remarks: This property allows you to display a label for the last value in a series, with customizable appearance options such as background color, line color, and dash pattern in stock chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets and sets the content of the UI element.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.ShowLabel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the label and indicator for the last data point in the series are visible.
member.value: true to display the last value label and the corresponding grid line indicator; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

example.code: <SfStockChart> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" /> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.remarks: Use this property to toggle the visibility of the last data label in the stock chart series. This is particularly useful for highlighting trend endpoints or enhancing visual clarity in analytical charts.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.Background
member.summary: Gets or sets the background color of the last value label.
member.value: A string representing the background color (e.g., "#ffffff" or "transparent"). The default value is "transparent".

example.code: <SfStockChart> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" Background=”red” /> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.remarks: Useful for enhancing label visibility, especially when the stock chart background contains multiple colors.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.LineWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the line displayed behind the last value label.
member.value: A double value specifying the thickness of the grid line. The default value is 1.

example.code: <SfStockChart> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" LineWidth=”0.5” /> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.remarks: Thicker lines can improve visibility, especially when multiple series are present in the stock chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.LineColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the grid line displayed behind the last value label.
member.value: A string specifying the grid line color. The default value is an empty string, which means the series color will be used.

example.code: <SfStockChart> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" LineColor=”Black” /> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.remarks: This property helps provide a direct reference line across the stock chart to the last value, improving readability and data interpretation.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.DashArray
member.summary: Gets or sets the dash pattern for the grid line behind the last value label.
member.value: A string defining the dash array (e.g., "4,2" for dashed lines). The default value is an empty string, which results in a solid line.

example.code: <SfStockChart> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries XName="X" YName="Y" DataSource="@StockData" Type="ChartSeriesType.Line"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" DashArray=”2,5” /> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.remarks: This property is useful for distinguishing the indicator line from other grid lines or series lines.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.Rx
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal radius of the rounded corners of the last data label.
member.value: A value representing the horizontal width of the rounded corner. The default value is 5.
member.remarks: This property affects the appearance of the corners of the last data label's background. This property is applicable only when is enabled.

example.code: // The following example demonstrates setting a horizontal radius for the data label corners: <SfStockChart Title="AAPL Historical"> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries DataSource="@StockDetails" Type="ChartSeriesType.Candle" XName="Date" YName="Close" High="High" Low="Low" Open="Open" Close="Close" Volume="Volume"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" Rx="10"> <StockChartLastDataLabelBorder Color="Green" Width="1"></StockChartLastDataLabelBorder> </StockChartLastDataLabel> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Charts.StockChartLastDataLabel.Ry
member.summary: Gets or sets the horizontal radius of the rounded corners of the last data label.
member.value: A value representing the horizontal width of the rounded corner. The default value is 5.
member.remarks: This property affects the appearance of the corners of the last data label's background. This property is applicable only when is enabled.

example.code: // The following example demonstrates setting a horizontal radius for the data label corners: <SfStockChart Title="AAPL Historical"> <StockChartSeriesCollection> <StockChartSeries DataSource="@StockDetails" Type="ChartSeriesType.Candle" XName="Date" YName="Close" High="High" Low="Low" Open="Open" Close="Close" Volume="Volume"> <StockChartLastDataLabel ShowLabel="true" Ry="10"> <StockChartLastDataLabelBorder Color="Green" Width="1"></StockChartLastDataLabelBorder> </StockChartLastDataLabel> </StockChartSeries> </StockChartSeriesCollection> </SfStockChart>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.Chart3DAxis
member.summary: Gets or sets instance of which is used to customize the primary x-axis of the 3D Chart.

example.code:
<SfChart3D>
                <Chart3DAxes>
                    <Chart3DAxis ValueType = "Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.ValueType.Category" RowIndex="0" ColumnIndex="0" Name="XAxis"></Chart3DAxis>
                </Chart3DAxes>
            
                <Chart3DSeriesCollection>
                    <Chart3DSeries XName = "Browser" YName="Users" XAxisName="XAxis" DataSource="@StatisticsDetails" Type="Chart3DSeriesType.Column">
                    </Chart3DSeries>
                </Chart3DSeriesCollection>
            </SfChart3D>
            @code {
                public class Statistics
                {
                    public string Browser { get; set; }
                    public double Users { get; set; }
                }
            
                public List<Statistics> StatisticsDetails = new List<Statistics>
                {
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Chrome", Users = 65.3 },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Safari", Users = 18.3},
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Edge", Users = 5},
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Firefox", Users = 3},
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Samsung Internet", Users = 2.6},
                    new Statistics { Browser = “Opera”, Users = 2.4},
                };
            }

member.value: An instance of . The default value is instance of .
member.remarks: By using this class we can add multiple axes to the 3D Chart. Each axis can be customized with different properties. This is child component of .

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.Chart3DPrimaryXAxis
member.summary: Gets or sets instance of which is used to customize the primary x-axis of the 3D Chart.
member.value: An instance of .

example.code:
<SfChart3D>
                <Chart3DSeriesCollection>
                    <Chart3DSeries XName="Browser" YName="Users" DataSource="@StatisticsDetails">
                    </Chart3DSeries>
                </Chart3DSeriesCollection>
                <Chart3DPrimaryXAxis Title="Browser Name" LabelFormat="{value} Month" Format="MMM" IsIndexed="false" MaximumLabels="5" OpposedPosition="false" RangePadding="ChartRangePadding.None"
                                     ValueType="Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.ValueType.Category" IntervalType="IntervalType.Months" Interval="2" Name="PrimaryXAxis" Visible="true" MinorTicksPerInterval="1" Minimum="0.5"
                                     Maximum="8" LogBase="100" ColumnIndex="0" RowIndex="0" Span="1" MaxLabelWidth="50" EnableTrim="true" EdgeLabelPlacement="EdgeLabelPlacement.Hide"
                                     LabelPlacement="LabelPlacement.BetweenTicks" LabelIntersectAction="LabelIntersectAction.Rotate45" LabelRotationAngle="45" LabelPadding="10" TitlePadding="15" IsInversed="false"
                                     PlotOffset="10" PlotOffsetBottom="5" PlotOffsetLeft="5" PlotOffsetRight="5" PlotOffsetTop="5" DesiredIntervals="5" TitleRotationAngle="90" StartFromZero="true">
                    <Chart3DAxisMajorGridLines Color="red" Width="2"></Chart3DAxisMajorGridLines>
                    <Chart3DAxisMajorTickLines Color="red" Width="1" Height="15"></Chart3DAxisMajorTickLines>
                    <Chart3DMinorGridLines Color="blue" Width="0.5"></Chart3DMinorGridLines>
                    <Chart3DAxisMinorTickLines Color="blue" Width="0.5" Height="10"></Chart3DAxisMinorTickLines>
                    <Chart3DAxisTitleStyle FontFamily="Arial" Color="Gray" FontStyle="Bold" FontWeight="600" FontSize="14px" Opacity="0.9" TextOverflow="TextOverflow.Wrap"></Chart3DAxisTitleStyle>
                </Chart3DPrimaryXAxis>
            </SfChart3D>
            @code {
                public class Statistics
                {
                    public string Browser { get; set; }
                    public double Users { get; set; }
                    public string Color { get; set; }
                }
            
                public List<Statistics> StatisticsDetails = new List<Statistics>
                {
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Chrome", Users = 65.3, Color = "red" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Safari", Users = 18.3, Color = "blue" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Edge", Users = 5, Color = "green" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = “Firefox”, Users = 3, Color = "orange"  },
                    new Statistics { Browser = “Samsung Internet”, Users = 2.6, Color = "yellow" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = “Opera”, Users = 2.4, Color = "pink" },
                };
            }

member.remarks: Use this class to customize the primary x-axis of the 3D Chart such as axis interval, range, and label settings.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.Chart3DLegendSettings
member.summary: Gets or sets the legend customization options for the 3D Chart component.

example.code:
<SfChart3D>
                <Chart3DSeriesCollection>
                    <Chart3DSeries XName="Browser" YName="Users" DataSource="@StatisticsDetails">
                    </Chart3DSeries>
                </Chart3DSeriesCollection>
            	
                <Chart3DPrimaryXAxis ValueType="Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.ValueType.Category">
                </Chart3DPrimaryXAxis>
            
                <Chart3DLegendSettings Alignment="Alignment.Center" Background="red" Visible="true" Width="350px" Height="50px" Position="LegendPosition.Bottom" ShapeHeight="20" ShapeWidth="20"
                ToggleVisibility="false" Reverse="true">
                    <Chart3DLegendBorder Color="red" Width="2"></Chart3DLegendBorder>
                    <Chart3DLegendMargin Bottom="5" Left="5" Top="5" Right="5"></Chart3DLegendMargin>
                    <Chart3DLegendTextStyle FontFamily="Arial" Color="Gray" FontStyle="Bold" FontWeight="600" FontSize="14px" Opacity="0.9" TextOverflow="TextOverflow.Trim"></Chart3DLegendTextStyle>
                    <Chart3DLegendTitleStyle FontFamily="Arial" Color="Gray" FontStyle="Bold" FontWeight="600" FontSize="14px" Opacity="0.9" TextOverflow="TextOverflow.Trim"></Chart3DLegendTitleStyle>
                </Chart3DLegendSettings>
            </SfChart3D>
            @code {
                public class Statistics
                {
                    public string Browser { get; set; }
                    public double Users { get; set; }
                    public string Color { get; set; }
                }
            
                public List<Statistics> StatisticsDetails = new List<Statistics>
                {
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Chrome", Users = 65.3, Color = "red" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Safari", Users = 18.3, Color = "blue" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Edge", Users = 5, Color = "green" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Firefox", Users = 3, Color = "orange"  },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Samsung Internet", Users = 2.6, Color = "yellow" },
                    new Statistics { Browser = "Opera", Users = 2.4, Color = "pink" },
                };
            }

member.value: Accepts the instance of class. The default value is instance of .
member.remarks: Use this class to customize the legend appearance in the 3D Chart. The legend can be positioned at the top, left, bottom, or right of the chart area.

member.summary: Gets or sets an instance of that specifies the location of the legend relative to the 3D Chart. If x is set to 20, the legend will move 20 pixels to the right of the 3D Chart.
member.value: The default value is an instance of .
member.remarks: The must be set to LegendPosition.Custom to position the legend in the 3D Chart using the specified x and y offsets.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Chart3D.Chart3DLegendSettings.Position
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the legend in the .
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the position of the legend. Options include:
: Places the legend based on the width and height of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the top of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the left of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the bottom of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the right of the chart.
: Displays the legend based on the given x and y location values.

member.summary: Gets or sets the alignment of the legend.
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the legend alignment. Options include: - Near: Aligns the legend to the left or top based on the . - Center: Aligns the legend to the center of the 3D chart. - Far: Aligns the legend to the right or bottom based on the .
The default value is Alignment.Center.
member.remarks: The alignment of the legend works as follows: - Near: Aligns the legend to the top-left of the 3D chart if is LegendPosition.Top and to the right-top of the 3D chart if is LegendPosition.Right. - Center: Aligns the legend to the top center of the 3D chart if is LegendPosition.Top and to the right center of the 3D chart if is LegendPosition.Right. - Far: Aligns the legend to the top-right of the 3D chart if is LegendPosition.Top and to the right-bottom of the 3D chart if is LegendPosition.Right.

member.summary: Asynchronously prints the specified element referenced by the optional parameter. If no element reference is provided, the chart will print.
member.param: Optional reference to the element to be printed. If not provided, the chart is printed.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous printing operation.

example.code:

                    </Chart3DSeries>

member.summary: Provides attribute-level configuration of minimum date, maximum date, and date format for date editors within the .
member.remarks: This attribute customizes allowed date ranges and their format for a specific property in a DataForm model class. Set MinimumDate and MaximumDate as string representations, and optionally define a format string according to .NET date formatting patterns.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.DataFormDateOptionsAttribute.MinimumDate
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum date, as a string, that is allowed for selection in a date editor field within the DataForm.
member.value: A string representing the earliest selectable date. The default is string.Empty, which imposes no restriction.
member.remarks:
Set to an empty string (string.Empty) if you do not intend to limit the lower bound. The format must match the property. The restriction applies only if both MinimumDate and Format are provided. Usage example:

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.FormGroup.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the is enabled.
member.value: true if the FormGroup is enabled; otherwise, false. Interaction with the form fields and their child components is disabled when the Enabled property is set to false. When set to true, the FormGroup and its child components become interactive. The default value is true.
member.remarks: The property provides a way to enable and disable the FormGroup and all its child components at runtime. This is useful for scenarios where certain sections of the form need to be disabled based on user input or business logic, such as progressive forms where later sections are enabled only after prerequisites are met. When the property is set to false, form field interactions such as input, focus, validation, and submission are prevented for the entire group. Enabling the FormGroup will restore full interactivity. This property affects all child FormItems and their associated editors but does not impact form-level events like submission until validation rules are satisfied. Ideal for conditional UI flows and preventing premature interactions.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.SfDataForm
member.summary: Provides a configurable and customizable data form for editing model values in Blazor applications. The automatically generates form items based on model property metadata, and provides support for templates, layout options, data annotations, and integrated validation.
member.remarks: The component is designed for rapid form development by automatically generating form fields for all properties in the given Model, or by allowing explicit configuration of form items for custom layouts and templates. The form integrates with EditContext and Blazor validation features, supports layout customization (column count, column spacing, floating labels), and exposes extensibility points such as custom buttons and validation message display. To use advanced features, define items through or use auto-generation. See the example for common usage.
member.example:
A simple example using to render a form for an Employee model:
<SfDataForm Model="@employee" ColumnCount="2"> <SfDataFormItem Field="FirstName" /> <SfDataFormItem Field="LastName" /> <SfDataFormItem Field="Email" /> <FormButtons> <SfButton Content="Submit" IsPrimary="true" /> </FormButtons> </SfDataForm>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.SfDataForm.AutoComplete
member.summary: Gets or sets the value of the autocomplete attribute of the component.
member.value: Accept the value.
member.remarks: on, the browser is allowed to automatically complete the input field based on the user's previous inputs. off, the browser is not allowed to automatically complete the input field. The autocomplete feature in the browser can be helpful in providing suggestions to users while they fill out the components. However, in certain scenarios, it might be necessary to disable this feature for security or privacy reasons.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataForm.SfDataForm.EnableFloatingLabel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Floating Label feature is enabled for all form fields in the component.
member.value: true if the Floating Label feature is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

remarks.para: When set to true, the Floating Label feature is enabled, causing labels to move to a floating position above the field when it is focused or contains user input, and it is enabled globally.
When set to false, the existing behavior of label in the form fields is maintained, and the Floating Label feature is disabled globally.
Note: Floating label functionality does not work when the label position is set to left. To enable the Floating Label feature, ensure that the label position is set to top.
The value from the property or property (Display name attribute) will be used as the Floating label text. When both properties are specified, the property takes precedence.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Adaptors
member.summary:
Specifies the data adaptors provided in component.
BlazorAdaptor Default. BlazorAdaptor is used to process Enumerable data. It contains methods to process the given collection based on the queries.
ODataAdaptor
OData Adaptor provies ability to consume and manipulate data from OData services.
ODataV4Adaptor
ODatav4 Adaptor provies ability to consume and manipulate data from OData v4 services
WebApiAdaptor
WebApi Adaptor provies ability to consume and manipulate data from WebApi services. This adaptor is targeted to interact with Web API created using OData endpoint, it is extended from ODataAdaptor
UrlAdaptor
URL Adaptor is used when you are required to interact with all kind of remote services to retrieve data.
RemoteSaveAdaptor
Remote Save Adaptor is used for binding JSON data. It interacts with remote services only for CRUD operations.
CustomAdaptor
CustomAdaptor specifies that own data query and manipulation logic has been provided using custom adaptor component extended from DataAdaptor class.
JsonAdaptor
JsonAdaptor is used to process JSON data at the client side. It contains methods to process the given JSON data based on the queries.
GraphQLAdaptor
GraphQLAdaptor provides ability to consume and manipulate data from GraphQL service. It requires setting in the component.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLAdaptorOptions
member.summary: Gets or Sets the properties to be specified for GraphQLAdaptor.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLAdaptorOptions.Query
member.summary: Defines the GraphQL query used to fetch data from the GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds the GraphQL query string that is used to request data from the GraphQL service. The query string should be formatted according to the GraphQL syntax.
member.remarks: The following parameter is passed in the Query string, dataManager - Contains the class properties. The class properties are used for performing data operations.

example.code:
<SfDataManager Url=https://localhost:7140/graphql GraphQLAdaptorOptions=@AdaptorOptions Adaptor="Adaptors.GraphQLAdaptor">
            </SfDataManager>
            @code{
                private GraphQLAdaptorOptions AdaptorOptions { get; set; } = new GraphQLAdaptorOptions
                {
                    Query = @"
                        query orderDatas($dataManager: DataManagerRequestInput!) {
                            orderDatas(dataManager: $dataManager) {
                                count, result { OrderID, EmployeeID, Freight, OrderDate } , aggregates
                        }
                    }"
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLAdaptorOptions.Mutation
member.summary: Defines the mutations used to perform CRUD operations in the GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds an instance of the class, which provides a way to define and manage mutations for performing CRUD operations in the GraphQL service.
member.remarks: The Mutation property provides a way to define and manage mutations for performing CRUD operations in the GraphQL service. These mutations facilitate creating, updating, and deleting data, allowing comprehensive data manipulation through GraphQL service.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLAdaptorOptions.ResolverName
member.summary: Defines the resolver function name used in the GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds the name of the resolver function, which is used to retrieve data from the GraphQL service and bind it to the corresponding component.
member.remarks: The ResolverName property should be specified in PascalCase, and the same name will be used as the resolver function's name in the GraphQL service. This property plays a pivotal role in connecting the component to the GraphQL service. By specifying the resolver function name, the component can fetch the necessary data to populate itself with information In GraphQL service, the resolver function should return DataResult class object containing Result, Count and optional Aggregates information. When working with the GraphQL service, it's important to include Aggregates details in the returned DataResult object when rendering footer summaries. However, if footer summaries are not being rendered, there's no need to include Aggregates information in the returned DataResult object.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLMutation
member.summary: Represents a collection of mutations used to perform CRUD operations in a GraphQL service.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLMutation.Insert
member.summary: Defines the mutation used to perform an insert operation in a GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds the GraphQL mutation query for data insertion in the GraphQL service. The mutation query should be formatted according to the GraphQL syntax and enable inserting data into the service.
member.returns: Returns the newly inserted record details.
member.remarks: The Insert property allows you to specify the GraphQL mutation insert query to perform data insertion in the GraphQL service. The following parameters are passed in the Insert query string, record - The new record which is need to be inserted. index - Specifies the index at which the newly added record will be inserted. action - Indicates the type of operation being performed. additionalParameters - An optional parameter that can be used to perform additional operations.

example.code:
<SfDataManager Url=https://localhost:7140/graphql GraphQLAdaptorOptions=@AdaptorOptions Adaptor="Adaptors.GraphQLAdaptor">
            </SfDataManager>
            @code{
                private GraphQLAdaptorOptions AdaptorOptions { get; set; } = new GraphQLAdaptorOptions
                {
                    Mutation = new GraphQLMutation
                    {
                        Insert = @"
                           mutation insert($record: OrderInput!, $index: Int!, $action: String!, $additionalParameters: Any) {
                              insertOrder(order: $record, position: $index, action: $action, additionalParameters: $additionalParameters) {
                               OrderID, EmployeeID, Freight, OrderDate
                             }
                        }"
                    }
                }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLMutation.Update
member.summary: Defines the mutation used to perform an update operation in a GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds the GraphQL mutation query for updating data in the GraphQL service. The mutation query should be formatted according to the GraphQL syntax and enable updating existing data in the service.
member.remarks: The Update property allows you to specify the GraphQL mutation update query to perform data updation in the GraphQL service. The following parameters are passed in the Update query string, record - The new record which is need to be updated. action - Indicates the type of operation being performed. primaryColumnName - The primaryColumnName specifies the field name of the primary column. primaryColumnValue - The primaryColumnValue specifies the primary column value which is needs to be updated in the collection. additionalParameters - An optional parameter that can be used to perform additional operations.

example.code:
<SfDataManager Url=https://localhost:7140/graphql GraphQLAdaptorOptions=@AdaptorOptions Adaptor="Adaptors.GraphQLAdaptor">
            </SfDataManager>
            @code{
                private GraphQLAdaptorOptions AdaptorOptions { get; set; } = new GraphQLAdaptorOptions
                {
                    Mutation = new GraphQLMutation
                    {
                        Update = @"
                           mutation update($record: OrderInput!, $action: String!, $primaryColumnName: String!, $primaryColumnValue: Int!, $additionalParameters: Any) {
                             updateOrder(order: $record, action: $action, keyField: $primaryColumnName, keyValue: $primaryColumnValue, additionalParameters: $additionalParameters) {
                               OrderID, EmployeeID, Freight, OrderDate
                             }
                        }"
                    }
                }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLMutation.Delete
member.summary: Defines the mutation used to perform delete operation in GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds the GraphQL mutation query for deleting the data in the GraphQL service. The mutation query should be formatted according to the GraphQL syntax and enable deleting the existing data in the service.
member.remarks: The Delete property allows you to specify the GraphQL mutation delete query to perform delete operation in the GraphQL service. The following parameters are passed in the Delete query string, primaryColumnValue - The primaryColumnValue specifies the primary column value which is needs to be removed from the collection. action Indicates the type of operation being performed. primaryColumnName - The primaryColumnName specifies the field name of the primary column. additionalParameters - An optional parameter that can be used to perform additional operations.

example.code:
<SfDataManager Url=https://localhost:7140/graphql GraphQLAdaptorOptions=@AdaptorOptions Adaptor="Adaptors.GraphQLAdaptor">
            </SfDataManager>
            @code{
                private GraphQLAdaptorOptions AdaptorOptions { get; set; } = new GraphQLAdaptorOptions
                {
                    Mutation = new GraphQLMutation
                    {
                        Delete = @"
                           mutation delete($primaryColumnValue: Int!, $action: String!, $primaryColumnName: String!, $additionalParameters: Any) {
                             deleteOrder(id: $ primaryColumnValue, action: $action, keyField: $primaryColumnName, additionalParameters: $additionalParameters) {
                               OrderID, EmployeeID, Freight, OrderDate
                             }
                        }"
                    }
                }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.GraphQLMutation.Batch
member.summary: Defines the mutation used to perform CRUD operation Synchronously in GraphQL service.
member.value: This property holds the GraphQL mutation query for bulk changes in the GraphQL service. The mutation query should be formatted according to the GraphQL syntax and enable CRUD operations Synchronously.
member.remarks: The Batch property allows you to specify the GraphQL mutation bacth query to perform CRUD operation in the GraphQL service. The following parameters are passed in the Batch query string, changed - Specifies the collection of record to be updated. added - Specifies the collection of record to be inserted. deleted - Specifies the collection of record to be removed. action - Indicates the type of operation being performed. primaryColumnName - The primaryColumnName specifies the field name of the primary column. additionalParameters - An optional parameter that can be used to perform additional operations. dropIndex - Specifies the record position, from which new records will be added while performing row drag and drop.

example.code:
<SfDataManager Url=https://localhost:7140/graphql GraphQLAdaptorOptions=@AdaptorOptions Adaptor="Adaptors.GraphQLAdaptor">
            </SfDataManager>
            @code{
                private GraphQLAdaptorOptions AdaptorOptions { get; set; } = new GraphQLAdaptorOptions
                {
                    Mutation = new GraphQLMutation
                    {
                        Batch = @"
                           mutation batch($changed: [OrderInput!], $added: [OrderInput!], $deleted: [OrderInput!], $action: String!, $primaryColumnName: String!, $additionalParameters: Any, , $dropIndex: Int!) {
                             batchUpdate(changed: $changed, added: $added, deleted: $deleted, action: $action, keyField :$primaryColumnName, additionalParameters: $additionalParameters,  dropIndex: $dropIndex) {
                               OrderID, EmployeeID, Freight, OrderDate
                             }
                        }"
                    }
                }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Data.QueryableExtensions.Where(System.Linq.IQueryable,System.Linq.Expressions.ParameterExpression,System.Linq.Expressions.Expression)
member.summary:
Use this function to generate WHERE expression based on Predicates. The AndPredicate and OrPredicate should be used in combination to build the predicate expression which is finally passed on to this function for creating a Lambda.
DataClasses1DataContext db = new DataClasses1DataContext();.
var orders = db.Orders.Skip(0).Take(100).ToList();.
var queryable = orders.AsQueryable();.
var parameter = queryable.Parameter("ShipCountry");.
var binaryExp = queryable.Predicate(parameter,.
"ShipCountry", "USA", true);.
var filteredOrders = queryable.Where(parameter, binaryExp);.
foreach (var order in filteredOrders).
{.
Console.WriteLine(order);.
}.
Build Predicates for Contains / StartsWith / EndsWith,.
IQueryable queryable = nw.Orders.AsQueryable();.
var parameter = queryable.Parameter();.
var exp1 = queryable.Predicate(parameter, "ShipCountry", "h", FilterType.Contains);.
var exp2 = queryable.Predicate(parameter, "ShipCountry", "a", FilterType.StartsWith);.
var andExp = exp2.OrPredicate(exp1);.
var filters = queryable.Where(parameter, andExp);.
foreach (Orders item in filters).
{.
Console.WriteLine("{0}/{1}", item.OrderID, item.ShipCountry);.
}.

member.summary: Specifies the endpoint URL. DataManager requests this URL when data is needed.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataManager.AdaptorInstance
member.summary: Specifies the custom adaptor class type. DataManager uses this type value to instantiate custom adaptor class.
member.remarks: DataManager uses Activator.CreateInstance method to create custom adaptor instance. Injecting services into custom adaptor class, is not supported while using this approach. To inject and use services, provide custom adaptor as a Blazor component by extending DataAdaptor class.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.DataManager.Adaptor
member.summary:
Gets or sets the data adaptor to be used by component.
BlazorAdaptor Default. BlazorAdaptor is used to process Enumerable data. It contains methods to process the given collection based on the queries.
ODataAdaptor
OData Adaptor provies ability to consume and manipulate data from OData services.
ODataV4Adaptor
ODatav4 Adaptor provies ability to consume and manipulate data from OData v4 services
WebApiAdaptor
WebApi Adaptor provies ability to consume and manipulate data from WebApi services. This adaptor is targeted to interact with Web API created using OData endpoint, it is extended from ODataAdaptor
UrlAdaptor
URL Adaptor is used when you are required to interact with all kind of remote services to retrieve data.
RemoteSaveAdaptor
Remote Save Adaptor is used for binding JSON data. It interacts with remote services only for CRUD operations.
CustomAdaptor
CustomAdaptor specifies that own data query and manipulation logic has been provided using custom adaptor component extended from DataAdaptor class.
JsonAdaptor
JsonAdaptor is used to process JSON data at the client side. It contains methods to process the given JSON data based on the queries.
GraphQLAdaptor
GraphQLAdaptor provides ability to consume and manipulate data from GraphQL services.
GraphQLAdaptor GraphQLAdaptor provides ability to consume and manipulate data from GraphQL service.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings
member.summary: Represents the settings for a context menu (shortcut menu) in a diagram component.

remarks.para: The class enables customization of context menus in diagram components. Configure menu visibility, define custom items, and handle menu events through this component.

example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent @ref="diagram" Height="600px" Width="90%" @bind-Nodes="nodes" >
            <ContextMenuSettings @bind-Show="@show" @bind-ShowCustomMenuOnly="@customMenuOnly" @bind-Items="@Items" ContextMenuOpening="@BeforeOpen" ContextMenuItemClicked="@ItemClicked">
            </ContextMenuSettings>
            </SfDiagramComponent>
             @code {
            SfDiagramComponent diagram;
            DiagramObjectCollection<Node> nodes = new DiagramObjectCollection<Node>();
            ContextMenuSettings ContextMenuSettings;
            List<ContextMenuItem> Items;
            bool customMenuOnly = false;
            bool show = true;
            protected override void OnInitialized()
            {
            
                Items = new List<ContextMenuItem>()
                {
                         new ContextMenuItem()
                        {
                            Text = "Save As...",
                            Id = "save",
                            IconCss = "e-save",
                        },
                        new ContextMenuItem()
                        {
                            Text = "Group",
                            Id = "load",
                            IconCss = "e-group"
                        }
                };
               Node node = new Node()
               {
                 // Position of the node
                 OffsetX = 250,
                 OffsetY = 250,
                 // Size of the node
                 Width = 100,
                 Height = 100,
                   };
                   nodes.Add(node);
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings.Show
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the context menu (shortcut menu) is displayed in the diagram component.
member.value: true if the context menu can be enabled; otherwise, false.

remarks.para: By default, the property is set to false which disables the context menu; set this property to true to enable the context menu functionality.
When enabled, the context menu will appear when users perform a right-click action on diagram elements, providing quick access to contextual commands and operations.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings.Items
member.summary: Gets or sets the collection of ContextMenuItem objects that define the items displayed in the context menu.
member.value: A collection of objects or null.

remarks.para: Defines the menu items displayed when the context menu is triggered. Each item represents a menu option with text, icon, and actions.

example.para: The following example demonstrates how to configure context menu items
example.code:
<SfDiagramComponent>
            <ContextMenuSettings  @bind-Items="@Items" >
            </ContextMenuSettings>
             </SfDiagramComponent>
             @code {
            protected override void OnInitialized()
            {
            
                Items = new List<ContextMenuItem>()
                {
                         new ContextMenuItem()
                        {
                            Text = "Save As...",
                            Id = "save",
                            IconCss = "e-save",
                        },
                };
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Diagram.ContextMenuSettings.ShowCustomMenuOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether only the custom menu items are displayed in the context menu.

remarks.para: By default, ShowCustomMenuOnly is set to false. Set this property to true to display only custom menu items.

member.value: A boolean value where true displays only custom menu items, and false displays both default and custom menu items.

example.code:
<ContextMenuSettings @bind-Show="@show" @bind-ShowCustomMenuOnly="@customMenuOnly" >
             </ContextMenuSettings>
             @code {
             bool customMenuOnly = false;
             bool show = true;
             protected override void OnInitialized()
             {
            
             }
