member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.ContextMenuItems
member.summary: Gets or sets both built-in and custom context menu items.
member.value: A list of built-in context menu items names or instance of for custom items.

example.code:
<SfGantt @ref="Gantt" DataSource="@TaskCollection" ContextMenuItems=contextMenuItems EnableContextMenu="true">
                <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress"
                    Dependency="Predecessor" ParentID="ParentId"></GanttTaskFields>
               <GanttEditSettings AllowAdding = "true"></GanttEditSettings>
                <GanttEvents ContextMenuItemClicked = "ContextMenuItemClickedHandler" TValue="TaskData"></GanttEvents>
            </SfGantt>
            @code{
             private SfGantt<TaskData> Gantt;
             private object contextMenuItems = new List<object> { "Add", "TaskInformation", new Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ContextMenuItemModel { Text = "Refresh", Target = ".e-content", Id = "refresh" } };
             private List<TaskData> TaskCollection { get; set; }
             private async Task ContextMenuItemClickedHandler(ContextMenuClickEventArgs<TaskData> args)
             {
               if (args.Item.Id == "refresh")
               {
                  await Gantt.RefreshAsync();
               }
             }
             }

member.remarks:
The available built-in items are,
AutoFitAll Auto fit the size of all columns
AutoFit Auto fit the current column
SortAscending Sort the current column in ascending order
SortDescending Sort the current column in descending order
TaskInformation Displays the current task.
Save Saves the edited Task
Cancel Cancels the edited Task
DeleteTask Deletes the current Task
Add Adds a new row to the Gantt
Convert Convert Current Task to Milestone or vice-versa
Indent Indent the selected record to one level
Outdent Outdent the selected record to one level
DeleteDependency Deletes the current dependency task link.
Context menu items display when clicking mouse right. Enable the built in context menu item using EnableContextMenuItems.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.EnableRowVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable row virtualization on the grid. When enabled, only the rows visible within the viewport are rendered and on vertical scrolling, subsequent rows are loaded.
member.value: true if need to enable row virtualization to render only the rows visible within the viewport, which enhances performance; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

example.code: <SfGantt DataSource = "@TaskCollection" EnableRowVirtualization="true"> <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress" ParentID="ParentId"> </GanttTaskFields> </SfGantt>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.EnableTimelineVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable timeline virtualization on the chart side. When enabled, only the timeline cells in the current viewport are rendered and subsequent timeline cells are loaded dynamically on horizontal scrolling.
member.value: true If need to enable timeline virtualization to load project with larger timespan with better performance; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If `EnableTimelineVirtualization` set to true, then the Gantt loads only the timeline cells thrice the width of the Gantt element, which improves performance for large time span.

example.code: <SfGantt DataSource = "@TaskCollection" EnableTimelineVirtualization ="true"> <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress" ParentID="ParentId"> </GanttTaskFields> </SfGantt>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.EnableColumnVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to enable the column virtualization for the Gantt.
member.value: true if need to enable column virtualization; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: If 'EnableColumnVirtualization' is set to true, then the Gantt will Initially, render only the columns that are in the current viewport and also load projects with a large number of columns with better performance. Subsequent columns are loaded on horizontal scrolling. This helps to load a large dataset with a large number of columns in the Gantt.

example.code: <SfGantt DataSource = "@TaskCollection" EnableColumnVirtualization="true"> <GanttTaskFields Id = "TaskId" Name="TaskName" StartDate="StartDate" EndDate="EndDate" Duration="Duration" Progress="Progress" ParentID="ParentId"> </GanttTaskFields> </SfGantt>

member.summary: Gets or sets the toolbar items in Gantt.
member.value:
The available built-in toolbar items are:
Add Adds a new record.
Edit Edits the selected task.
Update Saves the edited task.
Delete Deletes the selected task.
Cancel Cancels the edit state.
Search Searches tasks by the given key.
ExpandAll Expands all the task of Gantt.
CollapseAll Collapses all the task of Gantt.
PrevTimeSpan Extends timeline with one unit before the timeline start date
NextTimeSpan Extends timeline with one unit after the timeline finish date.
ZoomIn Zoom-in the timeline
ZoomOut Zoom-out the timeline
ZoomToFit Displays all tasks within the viewable Gantt chart within current view port.
ExcelExport Exports Gantt data in Excel format.
CsvExport Exports Gantt data in CSV format.
member.remarks: The toolbar items are strings that represent built-in or custom actions that can be performed on the Gantt tasks. Both built-in and custom toolbar items can be added to toolbar.

example.code: <SfGantt @ref = "Gantt" DataSource="@TaskCollection" Toolbar="@(new List<string>() { "Add", "Cancel", "Delete", "Edit", "Update", new ItemModel() { Text = "QuickFilter", TooltipText = "Quick Filter", PrefixIcon = "e-click", Id = "QuickFilter" }})"> </SfGantt>

            {
               FontName = "Segoe UI",
               FontColor = "#666666",
               FontSize = 12
            };
            Theme.Header = ThemeStyle;

            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.SfGantt`1.ExportToPdfAsync(Syncfusion.Blazor.Gantt.GanttPdfExportProperties)
member.summary: Exports the Gantt chart data to a Pdf document.
member.param: An object containing the properties of the PDF export. The options for customizing the PDF document during export.

member.remarks: should contain information such as file name, data to be exported and any other information related to PDF export. class provides various properties to customize PDF export. should be enabled.

example.code:
<SfGantt @ref="Gantt"  DataSource="@TaskCollection" AllowPdfExport="true" Toolbar="@(new List<string>(){"PdfExport"})"> 
                <GanttEvents OnToolbarClick="ToolbarClickHandler" TValue="TaskData"></GanttEvents>
                </SfGantt> 
                @code{
                private SfGantt<TaskData> Gantt;
                public async Task ToolbarClickHandler(Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.ClickEventArgs args){
                    GanttPdfExportProperties exportProperties = new GanttPdfExportProperties();
                    exportProperties.FileName = "New File.pdf";
                    if(args.Item.Text == "PDF export")
                    {
                        await Gantt.ExportToPdfAsync(exportProperties);
                    }
                }
                }

member.summary: Handles changes to the start date for a task item in the Gantt chart when updated via the StartDate dialog field.
member.param: The new start date value to assign, provided as an object.
The name of the column field being updated, typically indicating the start date field.
The that represents the task to be updated.
member.returns: The updated start date of the task as a nullable object.
member.remarks:
This method validates the provided value for the start date and applies changes to the task item in the TaskItemCollection. It adjusts the ProjectStartDate if the task's start date is earlier than the overall project start. The method also triggers appropriate notify methods to update related fields like the end date and duration based on the condition of these fields.
If the Gantt chart allows for segmentation and the relevant fields are defined, it updates the segments of the task item. Proper validation of the input value is performed via ValidateScheduleFields prior to making these updates.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.TooltipTemplateContext
member.summary: Provides contextual information for customizing tooltip content in the Blazor DataGrid via the .

remarks.para: This context is passed to the to enable dynamic rendering of tooltip content based on the hovered cell.
The context includes details such as the cell value, row and column indices, associated data object, and column metadata.
When hovering over a content cell, the will be a non-negative value and will contain the corresponding data object. When hovering over a header cell, will be -1 and will be .
These properties can be used to apply conditional styling or logic within the tooltip template, allowing differentiation between header and content cells.

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders" ShowTooltip="true">
            <GridTemplates>
            <TooltipTemplate>
            @{
               var tooltip = context as TooltipTemplateContext;
               @if (tooltip.RowIndex == -1)
            {
               @tooltip.Value 
            }
            else {
               @tooltip.Column.Field
            }
            }
            </TooltipTemplate>
            </GridTemplates>
            <GridColumns>
            <GridColumn Field=@nameof(Order.OrderID) HeaderText="Order ID"></GridColumn>
            </GridColumns>
            </SfGrid>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.TooltipTemplateContext.Value
member.summary: Gets the value of the currently hovered cell.
member.value: A representing the value displayed in the cell. The default value is .

remarks.para: This value is useful for displaying raw or formatted data in the tooltip. For templated columns or special display types like DisplayAsCheckbox, it reflects the underlying data value.
Applicable for both header and content cells. When hovering over a header cell, this property returns the column's HeaderText. For content cells, it returns the corresponding cell value.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.TooltipTemplateContext.ColumnIndex
member.summary: Gets the column index of the currently hovered column.
member.value: An integer representing the column index of the hovered cell.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.TooltipTemplateContext.RowIndex
member.summary: Gets the index of the currently hovered row.
member.value: An representing the row index. Returns -1 for header cells.

remarks.para: When hovering over a content cell, this property returns the corresponding row index within the grid.
For header cells, it always returns -1. This distinction is useful for customizing tooltip styles or behavior based on whether the hovered element is a header or a content cell.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.TooltipTemplateContext.Data
member.summary: Gets the data object of the currently hovered row.
member.value: The data associated with the hovered row. Returns null for header cells.
member.remarks: This object provides access to the full row data, enabling dynamic tooltip content based on multiple fields or business logic. When hovering over a content cell, this property returns the corresponding row object. For header cells, it always returns null. This distinction is useful for customizing tooltip styles or behavior based on whether the hovered element is a header or a content cell.

members.member:
Gets the associated with the currently hovered cell.
The object containing details such as header text, field name, and formatting options. /// Gets the associated with the hovered cell.
A object representing the column associated with the hovered cell.
This property provides metadata about the column, such as field name, header text, and formatting options, which can be used to customize tooltip content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.CaptionTemplateContext.GroupAggregates
member.summary: Retrieves the aggregate data context for a grouped column.
member.value: An instance of containing the aggregate values for the grouped column. This object typically includes calculated aggregates such as sum, average, and other values.
member.remarks: The property provides access to aggregate information, including field names and corresponding aggregate values, which are useful when columns are grouped. It supports the retrieval of aggregate values for display within the group caption template. Note that these values are available only when the aggregated columns are positioned first. The GroupAggregates property contains values only if the first column has an associated group aggregate.If columns are dynamically hidden, shown, or reordered, and the new first column has a group aggregate, the GroupAggregates context will update to reflect this change. It's important to note that GroupAggregates holds values only when the first column contains an aggregate value.

member.value: An instance of representing the coordinates (X1, Y1, X2, Y2) of the lines drawn within the header or footer. The coordinates are defined as follows: X1 and Y1 specify the starting coordinates for the line. X2 and Y2 specify the ending coordinates for the line.
member.remarks: class instance specifies the precise location of the lines within the header or footer. The lines drawn in the header, coordinates should be greater than the and property values and within the height and width range of the header. For the footer, the coordinates should be greater than the and property values and within the height and width range of the footer. Lines are only drawn when ContentType is set to .

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.PdfHeaderFooterElement.Position
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the content to be drawn within the header or footer in the exported Pdf.
member.value: An instance of representing the horizontal (X) and vertical (Y) alignment of the content within the header or footer.
member.remarks: class represents the alignment of the content within the header or footer, specifying the position relative to the header or footer. The X and Y coordinates should be greater than the and property values and within the height and width range of the header. For the footer, they should be greater than the and property values and within the height and width range of the footer.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.PdfHeaderFooterContent.TextDirection
member.summary: Gets or sets the tion of the PDF header and footer content. It allows changing the text direction.
member.value: One of the values in the enumeration that specifies the text direction. The default value is .
member.remarks:
The PdfTextDirection property can be set to one of the following values:
None: Content is displayed without any shaping or formatting based on languages. For example, the content Welcome to سينكفيوجن products will be rendered as Welcome to نجويفكنيس products
LeftToRight: Content is shaping based on language and the reading order of content is from left to right. For example, the content Welcome to سينكفيوجن products will be rendered as Welcome to سينكفيوجن products
RightToLeft: Content is shaping based on language and the reading order of content is from right to left. For example, the content Welcome to سينكفيوجن products will be rendered as products سينكفيوجن Welcome to

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders" Toolbar="@(new List<string>() { "PdfExport" })" AllowPdfExport="true">
             <GridEvents OnToolbarClick="ToolbarClickHandler" TValue="Order"></GridEvents>
             </SfGrid>
            @code{
             SfGrid<BusinessObject> Grid;
             public List<PdfHeaderFooterContent> HeaderContent = new List<PdfHeaderFooterContent>
             {
                  new PdfHeaderFooterContent() { TextDirection = Syncfusion.PdfExport.PdfTextDirection.RightToLeft, Type = ContentType.Text, Value = "Welcome to سينكفيوجن products", Position = new PdfPosition() { X = 300, Y = 50 }},
             }
             public async Task ToolbarClickHandler(Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.ClickEventArgs args)
             {
             if (args.Item.Text == "PDF Export")
             {
                      PdfExportProperties ExportProperties = new PdfExportProperties();
                      PdfHeader Header = new PdfHeader()
                      {
                               Contents = HeaderContent,
                      };
                      ExportProperties.Header = Header;
                      await this.Grid.PdfExport(ExportProperties);
             }
             }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.FilteringEventArgs.PreventFilterQuery
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to prevent the grid column’s default filter query during the API call.
member.value: The default value is false.
member.remarks: By default, when a filter is applied to a grid column, the grid sends a default filter request with the column name and filter value to the server. In some cases, the default filter request may be too long and exceed URL length limitations, resulting in a long URI exception. This property provides an option to generate a custom filter query for a specific grid column and override the default filter request. To utilize this property, set it to true within this event, and then override the ProcessCustomFilterQuery method in the adapter.

member.remarks: This property holds a collection of filter predicate values for a column currently undergoing filtering. - For filter types such as or , multiple predicate details are included from filtering using checkboxes and custom filters. - For filter types like or , only a single filter predicate detail is present. In essence, this property contains the current filter predicate details when a single or multiple values are filtered for a column. If the filter for a column is removed, the property becomes null. To clear or reset filtering from all columns in the grid, use the method, which results in both the and ColumnName properties becoming null.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ActionEventArgs`1.ExcelSearchOperator
member.summary: Gets or sets the Excel search operator.
member.value: The enum value that represents the selected search operator.
member.remarks:
Use this property to get or set the operator that will be used to filter data based on Excel-style search criteria. The available operators are specified by the enum. The default value is . The available operators are:
None: No operator is selected. For example, if we set
Contains: Checks whether the value contains the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "an", then the item would contains "an", columns to be filtered.
StartsWith: Checks whether the value begins with the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "an", then the item would startswith "an", columns to be filtered.
EndsWith: Checks whether the value ends with the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "an", then the item would endswith "an", columns to be filtered.
Equal: Checks whether the value is equal to the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "an", then the item would equal to "an", columns to be filtered.
NotEqual: Checks for values not equal to the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "an", then the item would notequal to "an", columns to be filtered.
GreaterThan: Checks whether the value is greater than the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "10", then the item would greaterthan to "10", columns to be filtered.
GreaterThanOrEqual: Checks whether a value is greater than or equal to the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "10", then the item would greaterthan or equal to "10", columns to be filtered.
LesserThan: Checks whether the value is less than the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "10", then the item would lessthan to "10", columns to be filtered.
LesserThanOrEqual: Checks whether the value is less than or equal to the specified value. For example, if we set and the search term is "10", then the item would lessthan or equal to "10", columns to be filtered.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ActionEventArgs`1.RequestType
member.summary: Gets the current in the grid like sorting, filtering, grouping, and etc.
member.value: The current action being performed in the grid.
member.remarks:
The request type assigned to the grid depends on the actions performed. The available request types include:
Add: When adding a new record in the normal or dialog edit mode enabled DataGrid.
BeforeBeginEdit: Before the current record becomes editable state in the normal or dialog edit mode enabled DataGrid (occurs only in event).
BeginEdit: After the current record becomes editable state in the normal or dialog edit mode enabled DataGrid.
Save: When saving a record in the normal or dialog edit mode enabled DataGrid.
Delete: When deleting a record in the normal or dialog edit mode enabled DataGrid.
Cancel: When canceling an edit operation in the normal or dialog edit mode enabled DataGrid.
Filtering: When filtering data in the DataGrid.
FilterBeforeOpen: Before opening the filter dialog for , and filter types (occurs only in event.).
FilterChoiceRequest: While fetching data to render the filtering checkboxes in or filter type.
FilterAfterOpen: After a filter dialog is opened (occurs only in When a filter dialog is opened. It will assigned only in event).
Sorting: When sorting data in the DataGrid.
Grouping: When grouping data in the DataGrid.
UnGrouping: When ungrouping a column in the DataGrid.
Paging: When navigating pages in the DataGrid.
Reorder: When reordering a column in the DataGrid.
RowDragAndDrop: When dragging and dropping rows in the DataGrid.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ActionEventArgs`1.PreventFilterQuery
member.summary: Gets or Sets whether to prevent the grid column’s default filter query during the API call.
member.value: The default value is false.
member.remarks: By default, when a filter is applied to a grid column, the grid sends a default filter request with the column name and filter value to the server. In some cases, the default filter request may be too long and exceed URL length limitations, resulting in a long URI exception. This property provides an option to generate a custom filter query for a specific grid column and override the default filter request. To use this property, set it to true in the OnActionBegin event with RequestType as Filtering, and override the ProcessCustomFilterQuery method in the adaptor.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridColumn.EditType
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of editor component to be rendered in the edit form.
member.value: One of the enumeration that specifies the editor component to be rendered in the edit form. If EditType is not provided then the EditType will inferred from the property type of the TValue. If TValue is ExpandoObject/ DynamicObject, then the EditType will inferred from the first data row. If EditType is not mentioned then the below components will rendered for the corresponding mentioned column types. For String type column, will rendered in the edit form. For Date and DateTime type columns, will rendered in the edit form. For DateOnly type column, will rendered in the edit form. For TimeOnly type column, will rendered in the edit form. For Boolean type column, will rendered in the edit form. For Number type column, will rendered in the edit form.
member.remarks: The EditType property can be set to one of the following values: DefaultEdit: will rendered in the edit form DropDownEdit: will rendered in the edit form. BooleanEdit: will rendered in the edit form. DatePickerEdit: will rendered in the edit form. DateTimePickerEdit: will rendered in the edit form. NumericEdit: will rendered in the edit form. TimePickerEdit: will rendered in the edit form.

example.code: <SfGrid DataSource="@Orders"> <GridColumns> <GridColumn Field=@nameof(Order.Freight) EditType="EditType.NumericEdit" ></GridColumn> </GridColumns> </SfGrid>

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the column should be fixed at the beginning of the Grid. A fixed column cannot be moved through reordering or grouping actions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridColumn.Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the column type of the . It determines how the data in the column will be displayed based on the specified type.
member.value: One of the enumerations that specify the column type. If the column type is not explicitly defined, the Type will be inferred from the property type of TValue. If TValue is ExpandoObject or DynamicObject, the Type will be inferred from the first row of the grid data.
member.remarks: The Type property can be set to one of the following values: String: The column will display the string values in the UI. For example “Alfki”, “UK”. Number: The column will display the numeric values such as int, int?, float, double, decimal etc. For example 2, 2.5, 3.33 Integer: Displays integer values from struct. Example: 5, 123 Double: Displays double values from struct. Example: 3.33, 45.567 Long: Displays long integer values from struct. Example: 255486129307 Decimal: Displays decimal values from struct. Example: 123.45M Boolean: The column will display the boolean values such as true or false. Date and DateTime: The column will display the datetime value from the and struct. DateOnly: The column will display the date value from struct. For example 2/1/2023 TimeOnly: The column will display the time value from struct. For example 11:15 AM CheckBox: Display the checkbox for selection purpose. No data operation is assosiated with this column. This Type property is mainly used for ExpandoObject and DynamicObject.

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders">
              <GridColumns>
             <GridColumn Field=@nameof(Order.OrderDate) Type="ColumnType.DateOnly"></GridColumn>
              </GridColumns>
             </SfGrid>
            @code{
            public class Order
            {
                 public DateOnly? OrderDate { get; set; }
            }
            }

member.summary:
Defines the mode to edit. The available editing modes are:
Normal Default. Editing is done in an inline form. Edit form is rendered inline as one of the table rows.
Dialog Editing is done in a Dialog/Pop component.
Batch Enables cell editing. Multiple cells can be edited, added or deleted and saved.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridEditSettings.ShowAddNewRow
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display a new blank row during grid initialization, facilitating the addition of new records.
member.value: true, a new blank row is displayed on the grid content. The default value is false.
member.remarks: By default, the new blank row is displayed at the top of the grid content. A new blank row can be displayed either at the top or bottom of the corresponding page, depending on the setting of the property. However, it's important to note that the ShowAddNewRow property solely pertains to the display of a new blank row in the editing mode. If the property is set to false, the new blank row will be disabled. Additionally, if any of the grid column's properties is set to false, the corresponding column cell will also be disabled.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridEvents`1.OnActionBegin
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is raised when the grid actions such as sorting, paging, grouping, ungrouping, reorder, rowdraganddrop, filtering, add, edit, delete, save and cancel action begins.
member.remarks: This event handler receives a object which provides the details of the current grid action. You can differentiate the actions using . To cancel the current action, set the property to true.
member.value: An event callback function.

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders">
                <GridEvents OnActionBegin="ActionBeginHandler" TValue="Order"></GridEvents>
            </SfGrid>
            @code {
                public void ActionBeginHandler(ActionEventArgs<Order> args)
                {
                    args.Cancel = true;
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridEvents`1.OnBatchAdd
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is raised before new records are added to the UI when a user clicks the add toolbar item or presses the insert key.
member.remarks: This event will be raised only for mode. This event handler receives a object which provides access to the added records and allows for cancellation of the batch add operation using the property. Within this event handler, you can customize the default data that is being added to the grid element before it is added.
member.value: An event callback function.

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders" Toolbar="@(new List<string>() { "Add", "Delete", "Update", "Cancel" })">
            <GridEvents OnBatchAdd="BatchAddHandler" TValue="Order"></GridEvents>
            <GridEditSettings AllowAdding="true" AllowDeleting="true" AllowEditing="true" Mode="EditMode.Batch"></GridEditSettings>
            </SfGrid>
            @code {
                public void BatchAddHandler(BeforeBatchAddArgs<Order> args)
                {
                  args.Cancel = true;
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridEvents`1.OnBatchDelete
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is raised before records are deleted in the grid element. You can perform delete action by click delete toolbar item or pressing the delete key. If no rows have been selected for deletion, a popup will be displayed allowing the user to select the rows they wish to delete before the operation is performed.

            </SfGrid>
            @code {
                public void BatchDeleteHandler(BeforeBatchDeleteArgs<Order> args)
                {
                  args.Cancel = true;
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridEvents`1.BeforeCopyPaste
member.summary: An event that is raised before copy or paste action in the Grid cells. You can cancel this entire copy or paste action by using this event.
member.remarks: This event triggers before event, so you can cancel entire pasting operation by using this event. Also, this event handler receives a object which provides the details of before paste/copy action.
member.value: An event callback function.

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders" @ref="DefaultGrid" >
             <GridEvents TValue="Orders" BeforeCopyPaste="Copy"></GridEvents>
             ........
             </SfGrid>
             @code{
             public async Task Copy(BeforeCopyPasteEventArgs args)
             {
                  //you can cancel the entire copy action here
                   if(args.Action == "Copy"){
                      args.Cancel = true;
                   }
                 // you can cancel the entire paste action here
                   if(args.Action == "Paste"){
                      args.Cancel = true;
                   }
             }

member.summary: An event that is raised before pasting the copied cell value for each cell. You can cancel the pasting action for particular cell or change the value by using this event.

member.value: An event callback function.

example.code:
<SfGrid DataSource="@Orders" @ref="DefaultGrid" >
            <GridEvents TValue="Orders" BeforeCellPaste="Paste"></GridEvents>
            ........
            </SfGrid>
            @code{
            public async Task Paste(BeforeCellPasteEventArgs<Orders> args)
            {
              if(ColumnIndex == 1 && RowIndex == 4){
                  //you can modified the content to be paste here.
                 args.CellValue = "Modified value"; 
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridGroupSettings.EnableLazyLoading
member.summary: The Lazy load grouping, allows the Grid to render only the initial level caption rows in collapsed state while grouping. The child rows of each caption will render only when we expand the captions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridGroupSettings.ExpandAllGroups
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether all groups in the grid are expanded by default during the initial render, when row virtualization is enabled.
member.value: true to expand all groups initially; otherwise, false. The default is false.
member.remarks:
This property only affects the grid if is set to true. If is true, this property is ignored, and groups are not auto expanded.
Performance Note: Expanding all groups on large, virtualized datasets may have a noticeable impact on grid rendering performance. Consider leaving this property as false to optimize load times with large data sources.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridGroupSettings.PersistGroupState
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the expand or collapse state of grouped rows is retained during operations such as sorting, filtering, paging, editing, and .
member.value: A indicating whether the expand or collapse state of grouped rows is preserved during operations. The default value is .

remarks.para: When set to true, the preserves the expanded or collapsed state of groups using a GroupKey. The GroupKey represents the common value under which rows are grouped, such as a specific CustomerID when grouping by that column. For example, if grouped by CustomerID with a value of ALFKI, all rows with CustomerID = ALFKI are grouped under the header Customer ID: ALFKI, and their expand or collapse state is retained after operations like sorting or filtering.
The expand or collapse state is reset when grouping or ungrouping actions are performed, as these actions alter the grid's grouping structure.

Grouping state persistence is distinct from grid persistence. While may preserve other grid settings across sessions, does not maintain the grouping state when the browser page is reloaded, navigated, or when the data source is dynamically changed.
Performance note: Enabling this feature may increase memory usage for large datasets due to the storage of group states.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridInfiniteScrollSettings
member.summary: Configures grid infinite scrolling.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridInfiniteScrollSettings.ChildContent
member.summary: Defines the child content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridInfiniteScrollSettings.InitialBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of blocks to be initially rendered when the Grid is loaded. Each block corresponds to a page size of the Grid, resulting in the rendering of a certain number of tr elements determined by multiplying the initial block size with the page size.
member.value: The default value is 3, indicating that the Grid will display three blocks, which translates to a specific number of tr elements, during the initial rendering.
member.remarks: The InitialBlocks property determines the quantity of blocks, each equivalent to a page size, to display during the first load. Additional blocks will be dynamically loaded as the user scrolls through the Grid. For example, when the bottom of the scrollbar is reached, one block of records will be fetched and loaded to display new set of data's. If the is not explicitly provided, it will be calculated based on the viewport height to ensure an optimal user experience. The InitialBlocks size should be set greater than the viewport height to guarantee a smooth and seamless user experience.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridInfiniteScrollSettings.MaximumBlocks
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of blocks to be rendered in the Grid during scrolling when EnableCache is set to true. This caching mode optimizes performance by storing blocks in a cache for large data sets.
member.value: The default value is 3.
member.remarks: When EnableCache is set to true, the MaximumBlocks property determines the maximum number of blocks to be kept in the cache. Exceeding this limit will remove the oldest blocks from the cache to make space for new ones.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridInfiniteScrollSettings.EnableCache
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Grid will cache visited blocks of data, allowing reuse of previously loaded block data when revisiting the same block. This reduces the frequency of data requests while navigating through the same block.
member.value: true to enable data caching for visited blocks; false by default.
member.remarks: Enabling this caching mode maintains row elements in the DOM based on the count. If the number of maintained rows exceeds this limit during scrolling, the Grid removes rows from the DOM to accommodate new row elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.GridRowDropSettings.AllowEmptyAreaDrop
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that enables dropping rows into empty areas of the grid content during drag-and-drop operations.
member.value: A boolean value indicating whether rows can be dropped into blank areas within the grid content. The default value is true.
member.remarks:
When set to true, users can drop rows not only above or below existing rows, but also into empty spaces within the grid. If the grid contains rows and a row is dropped into an empty area, it will be appended as the last row in the grid. When set to false, dropping is restricted to valid drop indicators displayed between rows only.
This setting applies to row reordering both within the grid and outside the grid.

member.summary: Gets or sets a template to customize the tooltip content when hovering over grid cells and headers.
member.value: A used to define custom tooltip content. No default value.

remarks.para: This template enables rich customization of tooltip content in the Blazor DataGrid. It is rendered when tooltips are enabled via the ShowTooltip property.
The template receives a context parameter of type , which provides access to relevant data such as the grid column, row data, and cell value.
To activate tooltip, ensure that the ShowTooltip property is set to . Without this setting, the TooltipTemplate will not be rendered.
This feature is useful for displaying additional contextual information, such as formatted values, icons, or images—especially when working with templated columns or truncated content.

member.summary: Sets the lazy load page size based on the provided grid height.
member.param: The height of the grid as a string. If not provided, the height from the parent grid is used.
member.remarks: This method calculates the block size by dividing the grid height by the row height and subtracting one. The lazy load block size is set to half of the lazy load page size, rounded up.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.SfGrid`1
member.summary: Blazor Grid component displays tabular data and it has in-built support for various data binding, editing, sorting and filtering.
member.typeparam: A type which provides schema for the grid component.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.SfGrid`1.AddRecordAsync(`0,System.Nullable{System.Int32})
member.summary: Adds a new record to the Grid at a specific row index.
member.param: New record to be added. The data should be of the same type as the generic type of the grid.
The index in which the new record is to be added. If no index is provided, the record will be added to the end of the grid.
member.remarks: This method adds the row only if is set to true.

example.code:
<button id="AddRecord" @onclick="AddItem">AddRecord</button>
            <SfGrid @ref="grid" DataSource="@Orders">
             ........
            </SfGrid>
            @code{
               SfGrid<Order> grid;
               private async Task AddItem()
               {
                   var data = new Order() { OrderID = 1000, CustomerID = "ALFKI", OrderDate = new DateTime(1995, 03, 25), Freight = 25.7 * 2) };
                   await grid.AddRecordAsync(data, 1); // pass data and index here.
               }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.SfGrid`1.ApplyBatchChangesAsync(Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.BatchChanges{`0})
member.summary: Updates the Grid component UI with a batch of changes, including new records, edited records, and deleted records.
member.param: It contains the collection of records to add, edit, and delete.
member.remarks: This method is used to make bulk changes to the grid UI when in EditMode.Batch. The edited and newly added records will be visually highlighted in the grid UI, and the highlighting will be cleared once the changes are saved or canceled.
member.value: A task representing the asynchronous operation. The task result can indicate the success or failure of the batch update operation.

example.code:
<button id="GetData" @onclick="SetData">Apply Batch Changes</button>
             <SfGrid @ref="grid" DataSource="@Orders">
              <GridEditSettings AllowAdding="true" AllowEditing="true" AllowDeleting="true" Mode="EditMode.Batch"></GridEditSettings>
              ........
             </SfGrid>
             @code{
                SfGrid<Order> grid;
                private async Task SetData()
                {
                  var batchChanges = new BatchChanges<Order>()
                    {
                        AddedRecords = new List<Order>() { new Order() { OrderID = 1, CustomerID = "ANTAR" } }, DeletedRecords = new List<Order>() { new Order() { OrderID = 1002 } }, ChangedRecords = new List<Order>() { new Order() { OrderID = 1001, CustomerID = "VINET" } } 
                    }
                   await grid.ApplyBatchChangesAsync(batchChanges);
                }
             }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.SfGrid`1.AutoFitColumnsAsync
member.summary: Changes the column width to automatically fit its content and ensure that the content is not wrapped or hidden. This method will ignore any hidden columns.
member.remarks: You can use this method in the event or set the property to autofit the columns at initial rendering.

example.code:
<button id="AutoFit" @onclick="AutoFit">AutoFit Column</button>
            <SfGrid @ref="Grid" DataSource="@Orders">
             ........
            </SfGrid>
            @code{
               SfGrid<Order> Grid;

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.SfGrid`1.EnableInfiniteScrolling
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Grid loads the next set of data's on-demand, when the vertical scrollbar reaches the end of the scroller. This feature enables loading large datasets into the Grid without the need of traditional pagination.
member.value: Set true to enable infinite scroll by loading data when vertical scroll bar reaches the end of scrollbar. The default value is false.
member.remarks: During the initial rendering, the grid loads a block of data based on the property. The default value of InitialBlocks is 3. After that the buffering data's are loaded based on the page size or rows which are rendered within the provided height. Subsequently, as the user scrolls to the end of the grid, additional blocks of data will be loaded in on-demand. In the default Infinite Scrolling mode, a block of data accumulates every time the scrollbar reaches the end. However, in the cache mode, blocks of data are rendered based on the MaximumBlocks setting. If the number of blocks exceeds this limit during scrolling, the Grid removes rows from the DOM to accommodate the new block of data. EnableCache and MaximumBlocks can be configured through the properties of the class.

member.summary: Gets or sets the order weight of the column.
member.remarks: Columns are sorted in increasing order based on the order value. Columns without this attribute have an order value of 0. Negative values are valid and can be used to position a column before all non-negative columns. If an order is not specified, presentation layers should consider using the value 10000. member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageEditorZoomSettings
member.summary: Represents the settings for zooming actions in the .
member.remarks: The `ZoomSettings` tag allows you to control the zoom level of the Image Editor. The maximum zoom level determines how close the user can zoom in to the image, while the minimum zoom level determines how far out the user can zoom.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageEditorZoomSettings.ZoomTrigger
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of zooming needs to be performed in the .
member.value: A flagged Enum value that specifies the type of zooming option to perform zooming. And by default, all type of zooming were performed in an .
member.remarks:
It is a flagged Enum. Use this property to enable or disable specific types of zooming in the image editor. The following zooming options are available:
MouseWheel: Zooming is performed by scrolling the mouse wheel up and down.
Pinch: Zooming is performed using pinch gestures on touch-enabled devices.
Commands: Zooming is performed by clicking the CTRL key and either the plus (+) or minus (-) buttons on the keyboard.
Toolbar: Zooming is performed using toolbar buttons.
By default, this property is set to `MouseWheel|Touch|Commands|Toolbar`, which enables all types of zooming.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageEditorZoomSettings.MinZoomFactor
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum zoom level that restricts the range of zooming allowed by this zoom settings.
member.value: A double value that specifies the minimum zooming level. And the default value is 1 (100%).
member.remarks: User can specify MinZoomFactor as 0.1, and it can zoom out 9 actions from the original image.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageEditorZoomSettings.MaxZoomFactor
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum zoom level that restricts the range of zooming allowed by this zoom settings.
member.value: A double value that specifies the maximum zooming level. And the default value is 10 (1000%).
member.remarks: User can specify MaxZoomFactor as 20, and it can zoom in 20 actions from the original image.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageEditorZoomSettings.ZoomFactor
member.summary: Gets or sets the zooming level applied to the image at initial load in the .
member.value: A double value that specifies the minimum zooming level. And the default value is 1 (100%).
member.remarks: The default ZoomFactor (set as 1) loads the original image.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageEditorZoomSettings.ZoomPoint
member.summary: Gets or sets the point in which the zooming has been performed in the .
member.value: An value that specifies the current zooming point. And the default value is null, and it can be considered as center point of the .
member.remarks: The given value is an object which has x and y coordinates.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.SfImageEditor.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the value that indicates the width of the .
member.value: A string value that can accept various types of input such as numbers (e.g., 950), pixels (e.g., 950px), em units (950em), or percentages (e.g., 100%) to specify the width of the image editor. The default value is 100%.
member.remarks: When specifying the width as a percentage, it is relative to the width of the parent element. You can use different units to set the width according to your layout requirements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.SfImageEditor.AllowUndoRedo
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the undo and redo functionality is enabled in the .
member.value: true if the undo and redo functionality is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: The undo-redo history is limited to 16 actions. After the 16th action, the first action in history is removed.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.SfImageEditor.EnableImageSmoothing
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether image smoothing is applied when rendering images.
member.value: true to enable image smoothing; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

remarks.para: When image smoothing is enabled, the component applies anti-aliasing to images during rendering, which can reduce pixelation and jagged edges in scaled or rotated images. This may result in slightly blurred details for high-resolution images.
When disabled, images are rendered with crisp, unaltered pixels, which may be preferable for pixel art, text, or other content requiring sharp edge definition.
This property internally controls the HTML5 Canvas imageSmoothingEnabled and imageSmoothingQuality properties.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.SfImageEditor.IsReadOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the component is in read-only mode.
member.value: true if the read-only mode is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When the read-only mode is enabled, users won't be able to make changes to the content within the . This is useful when you want to provide a view-only experience without allowing user modifications.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.SfImageEditor.ShowQuickAccessToolbar
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the quick-access toolbar functionality is enabled in the .
member.value: true if the quick access toolbar is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: The quick-access toolbar is shown when annotations are selected. It provides options for clone, delete, and edit text.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.SfImageEditor.HtmlAttributes

member.value: This property allows you to specify additional attributes for customizing the rendering of the component. The default value is `null`.

member.summary: Represents the settings of a frame in the .

member.summary: Gets or sets the type of frame in the .
member.value: An enumeration value that specifies the type of the frame, such as None, Mat, Bevel, Line, Inset, and Hook.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.Color
member.summary: Gets or sets the color of the frame in the .
member.value: A string value specifying the color of the frame. The color can be provided in various formats, including named colors ("red", "blue") and hexadecimal notation ("#RRGGBB"). The default frame color is typically white.
member.remarks: The frame color is used to define the outline color of the frame drawn on an image using the . It helps distinguish the frame from the content of the image.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.GradientColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the gradient color of the frame in the .
member.value: A string value specifying the gradient color of the frame. The color can be provided in various formats, including named colors ("red", "blue") and hexadecimal notation ("#RRGGBB"). The default gradient color is typically absent, resulting in a solid color frame.
member.remarks: The gradient color can be used to give the frame a more dynamic and visually appealing appearance. When set, the frame will transition from the primary frame color to the gradient color, creating a gradient effect.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.Size
member.summary: Gets or sets the size of the frame as a percentage in the .
member.value: An integer value specifying the size of the frame as a percentage. The size value indicates how much of the image's dimensions the frame occupies. It can be provided as an integer percentage (e.g., 20). The default frame size is often set to a reasonable percentage to maintain a balanced appearance.
member.remarks: Adjusting the frame size allows you to control the width or thickness of the frame drawn on an image using the . Smaller percentages result in thinner frames, while larger percentages result in thicker frames.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.Inset
member.summary: Gets or sets the inset value of the frame as a percentage in the .
member.value: An integer value specifying the inset of the frame as a percentage. The inset value determines how far the frame is drawn inside the image boundaries. It can be provided as an integer percentage (e.g., 10). The default inset value is often set to zero.
member.remarks: The inset value is applicable only to specific frame types such as Line, Inset, and Hook. It helps create an internal margin between the frame and the image's edges. For other frame types, inset is not used.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.Offset
member.summary: Gets or sets the offset value of the frame as a percentage in the .
member.value: An integer value that specifies the offset of the frame as a percentage. The offset determines how far the line is positioned from another line in the image's boundaries. It can be provided as an integer percentage (e.g., 5). The default offset value is typically zero.
member.remarks: The offset value is relevant for specific frame types such as Line and Inset. It allows you to control the position of the frame within the image. The offset is measured from the edge where the frame is applied towards the center of the image. Other frame types do not use the offset property.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.BorderRadius
member.summary: Gets or sets the border radius value of the frame as a percentage in the .
member.value: An integer value that specifies the border radius of the frame. The border radius controls the curvature of the frame's corners or edges. It can be provided as an integer percentage (e.g., 10). The default border radius is typically zero, resulting in sharp corners.
member.remarks: The BorderRadius value is applicable only to specific frame types such as Line and Bevel. It allows you to round the corners or edges of the frame, giving it a softer appearance. For other frame types, the border radius property is not used.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.FrameLineStyle
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of lines to be drawn for line-type frames on the image in the .
member.value: A FrameLineStyle enumeration value that specifies the type of line to be applied as a frame. The default value is Solid.
member.remarks: The FrameLineStyle value is applicable only to Line frames. It allows you to customize the appearance of the lines used to create the frame. Different line types can give your frame a distinct visual style.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.ImageEditor.ImageFrameSettings.LineCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of lines to be drawn on the image in the .
member.value: An integer value that specifies the number of lines to be applied as a frame. The lines are drawn parallel to the image edges. Each line contributes to the frame's appearance, giving it a unique style. The default value is typically zero, resulting in no additional lines.
member.remarks: The LineCount value is applicable only to Line frames. It enables you to create a distinctive frame effect by adding multiple parallel lines around the image's edges.

member.summary: A set of string constants used by the component.

The In-place Editor component is most useful for editing a value dynamically within its context (in-place). It has the built-in support to handle all the form components, including TextBox, Dropdown List, DatePicker, and Rich Text Editor. The component comes with different edit modes and a fully customizable UI.

member.remarks: The component is a powerful tool for in-context editing, reducing the need for separate forms or dialogs. It supports various data types and can be integrated with other Syncfusion Blazor components like , SfDropDownList, and SfDatePicker.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.SfInputBase.InputEditContext
member.summary: Gets or sets the edit context for form validation and data binding.
member.value: An instance that manages form validation. The default value is null.
member.remarks:
This cascading parameter is automatically provided by parent form components like EditForm or DataAnnotationsValidator. The EditContext serves as the central hub for form validation operations:
Tracks which fields have been modified and their validation state
Coordinates validation message display across form components
Manages validation triggers and field-level validation events
Provides integration with data annotation validation attributes
Components within an EditForm automatically receive this parameter to participate in centralized form validation. This enables seamless integration with Blazor's form validation infrastructure, including automatic validation message display, validation state styling, and coordinated form submission handling.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.SfInputBase.Autocomplete
member.summary:
Gets or sets whether the browser is allowed to automatically enter or select a value for the input component. By default, autocomplete is enabled for the input component. Possible values are:
On Specifies that autocomplete is enabled
Off Specifies that autocomplete is disabled
member.value: A string value specifying the autocomplete behavior. The default value is "on".
member.remarks: The autocomplete attribute provides a hint to the browser about the type of information expected in the field. When set to "on", the browser may suggest previously entered values or auto-fill the field based on the user's browsing history and form completion patterns. When set to "off", the browser should not automatically complete or suggest values for this field, which is particularly useful for sensitive data entry fields. This property supports all standard HTML5 autocomplete values including specific field types like "name", "email", "current-password", etc.
member.example:

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.SfInputBase.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to persist component's state between page reloads. When set to true, the property is persisted.
member.value: true if the component's state persistence is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks:
When state persistence is enabled, the component's property is automatically saved to and restored from the browser's local storage. This feature provides several benefits:
Maintains user input across page refreshes or browser restarts
Improves user experience by preserving form data during navigation
Reduces data loss in scenarios where users accidentally navigate away
The persistence mechanism uses the component's as the storage key, so ensure unique IDs when using multiple components with persistence enabled. The stored data is specific to the current origin (protocol + domain + port) and will not be shared across different domains. Clearing browser data or local storage will remove the persisted values.
member.example:
In the following code example, enable state persistence for the input component.
<SfTextBox ID="userInput" EnablePersistence="true" Placeholder="This value will be persisted"></SfTextBox>

member.remarks: When RTL is enabled, the component layout and text direction will be adjusted to support right-to-left languages such as Arabic or Hebrew. This affects text alignment, element positioning, and overall component orientation.

In the following code example, enable RTL support for the input component.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.SfInputBase.FloatLabelType
member.summary: Gets or sets the floating label behavior of the input component. The text acts as a label.
member.value: One of the enumeration values. The default value is .
member.remarks:
The floating label provides an enhanced user experience by animating the placeholder text as a label, creating a more intuitive and accessible form interface:
If is , the placeholder text remains static and does not float as a label
If is , the placeholder text smoothly animates above the input component as a label when the field gains focus or contains a value
If is , the placeholder text is persistently displayed as a label above the input component regardless of focus or content state
This feature improves form usability by maintaining context about what information should be entered in each field, even after the user has started typing. The floating label animation follows Material Design principles and provides better accessibility for screen readers.
member.example:
In the following code example, set the floating label as Auto.
<SfTextBox FloatLabelType="FloatLabelType.Auto" Placeholder="Enter a value"></SfTextBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.SfInputBase.HtmlAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of additional attributes such as styles, class, and more that will be applied to the input component.
member.value: A dictionary collection containing HTML attributes to be applied to the component. The default value is null.
member.remarks:
This property allows you to pass additional HTML attributes that will be applied to the component's root element. If you configure both a component property and its equivalent HTML attribute in this collection, the component considers the property value over the HTML attribute. This is particularly useful for applying custom styling, data attributes, ARIA attributes, event handlers, or other HTML attributes that are not exposed as direct component properties.
The following attributes are handled specially and applied to the container rather than the input element: "title", "style", and "class". member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.SfInputBase.TabIndex
member.summary: Gets or sets the tab order of the input component for keyboard navigation.
member.value: An integer representing the tab order. The default value is 0.
member.remarks:
The tab index determines the sequential keyboard navigation order (using the Tab key) among elements in the page. This property enhances accessibility by providing predictable navigation patterns and ensuring compliance with web accessibility standards:
Elements with tabindex="0" participate in the natural tab order based on their position in the DOM structure
Positive values (1, 2, 3, etc.) create a prioritized tab sequence, with lower numbers receiving focus first in the navigation cycle
A value of -1 removes the element from the tab sequence but still allows programmatic focus via JavaScript or other methods
Elements with positive tab indexes are always focused before elements with tabindex="0" or no tabindex attribute
Best practice recommends using tabindex="0" for most interactive elements and avoiding positive values unless absolutely necessary, as they can create confusing navigation patterns that don't follow the visual layout of the page and may negatively impact user experience. Proper tab order implementation is crucial for keyboard users and assistive technology compatibility.
member.example:
In the following code example, set tab indexes for multiple input components.
<SfTextBox TabIndex="1" Placeholder="First input"></SfTextBox> <SfTextBox TabIndex="2" Placeholder="Second input"></SfTextBox> <SfTextBox TabIndex="3" Placeholder="Third input"></SfTextBox>

The value/brightness as a percentage (0-100). Represents the lightness of the color.
The alpha/opacity value in range 0-1. Default is 1 (fully opaque).
member.returns: A double array containing RGB values [R, G, B, A] where R, G, B are in range 0-255 and A is 0-1.
member.remarks: This method performs color space conversion from HSV to RGB model. The conversion uses the standard HSV-to-RGB algorithm which divides the hue into six sectors and applies different mathematical formulas based on the sector. The HSV color model is particularly useful for color pickers as it allows intuitive color selection by separating hue (color choice) from saturation (color intensity) and value (brightness). The resulting RGB values are rounded to integers in the 0-255 range suitable for display systems.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.Utils.HexToRgb(System.String)
member.summary: Converts a hexadecimal color string to RGB values with alpha channel.
member.param: The hexadecimal color string in various formats like "#RGB", "#RRGGBB", "#RRGGBBAA".
member.returns: A double array containing RGBA values [R, G, B, A] where R, G, B are in range 0-255 and A is in range 0-1.
member.remarks: This method parses hexadecimal color strings and extracts RGB color components along with the alpha channel. The method handles various input formats by first normalizing them using the RoundValue method to ensure a consistent 9-character format (#RRGGBBAA). The alpha value is extracted from the last two characters and converted to a decimal value between 0 and 1. If parsing fails due to invalid format, default values are used to prevent exceptions. Returns an empty array if the input is null or empty.

example.code:
string hexColor = "#FF8040CC"; // Orange color with some transparency double[] rgba = Utils.HexToRgb(hexColor); // Returns [255, 128, 64, 0.8]
string shortHex = "#F84"; // Short format double[] rgbaShort = Utils.HexToRgb(shortHex); // Automatically expanded and converted

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.Utils.ConvertToHsvString(System.Double[])
member.summary: Converts an HSV color array to CSS hsv() or hsva() string format.
member.param: A double array containing HSV values [H, S, V] or [H, S, V, A] where H is 0-360, S and V are 0-100, and A is 0-1.
member.returns: A CSS-formatted HSV string like "hsv(h,s,v)" or "hsva(h,s,v,a)" depending on alpha presence, or empty string if input is null.
member.remarks: This method formats HSV color values as CSS-compatible hsv() or hsva() strings that can be used in modern web browsers. The method automatically determines whether to use hsv() or hsva() format based on the array length and alpha value. If the array has 4 elements and the alpha value is not 1 (not fully opaque), it uses hsva() format. The value component (brightness) is rounded to an integer before formatting. Any trailing comma in the generated string is automatically removed for proper CSS compliance.

example.code:
double[] hsv = {240, 100, 80}; // Blue color string cssHsv = Utils.ConvertToHsvString(hsv); // Returns "hsv(240,100,80)"
double[] hsva = {120, 60, 90, 0.7}; // Green color with transparency string cssHsva = Utils.ConvertToHsvString(hsva); // Returns "hsva(120,60,90,0.7)"

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.Utils.ConvertRgbToNumberArray(System.String)
member.summary: Parses a CSS color string (rgb or rgba format) and converts it to a numeric array.
member.param: A CSS color string in rgb() or rgba() format like "rgb(255,0,0)" or "rgba(255,0,0,0.5)".
member.returns: A double array containing the parsed color values [R, G, B, A]. Returns a 4-element array with default values if input is null.
member.remarks: This method extracts numeric color values from CSS rgb() or rgba() function strings. It locates the opening parenthesis, removes the closing parenthesis if present, and splits the remaining content by commas to extract individual color components. Each component is converted to a double value using invariant culture to ensure consistent parsing regardless of system locale. If the input string is null, a default 4-element double array is returned to prevent null reference exceptions. This method is particularly useful for parsing user input or CSS color values in web-based color pickers.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Internal.Utils.Slice(System.Double[],System.Int32)
member.summary: Creates a new array containing the first n elements from the source array.
member.param: The source array to slice from.
The number of elements to include in the new array, starting from index 0.
member.returns: A new double array containing the first 'last' elements from the source array.
member.remarks: This method performs an array slicing operation, creating a new array with a specified number of elements copied from the beginning of the source array. This is useful for truncating color arrays or extracting specific components (e.g., getting only RGB values from an RGBA array). The method uses Array.Copy for efficient memory copying. The caller should ensure that the 'last' parameter does not exceed the length of the source array to avoid runtime exceptions.

example.code: double[] rgba = {255, 128, 64, 0.8}; // RGBA color array double[] rgb = Utils.Slice(rgba, 3); // Returns [255, 128, 64] - just RGB values

member.remarks: This private helper method is used internally for hexadecimal color conversion operations. It converts a double value to an integer, then formats it as a hexadecimal string. member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Hex
member.summary: Represents color values in hexadecimal format without opacity information.
member.remarks: The Hex format uses a 6-character hexadecimal representation (e.g., #FF0000 for red). This format does not include alpha/opacity information and is widely supported across web technologies and design applications.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Hexa
member.summary: Represents color values in hexadecimal format with opacity information.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Rgb
member.summary: Represents color values in RGB (Red, Green, Blue) format without opacity information.
member.remarks: The RGB format uses three integer values ranging from 0 to 255 for red, green, and blue components (e.g., rgb(255, 0, 0) for red). This format is commonly used in web development and provides intuitive color representation based on primary color components.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Rgba
member.summary: Represents color values in RGBA (Red, Green, Blue, Alpha) format with opacity information.
member.remarks: The RGBA format extends RGB by adding an alpha channel for opacity control. It uses three integer values (0-255) for RGB components and a decimal value (0-1) for alpha (e.g., rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5) for semi-transparent red).

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Hsv
member.summary: Represents color values in HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) format without opacity information.
member.remarks: The HSV format uses cylindrical color representation where Hue is an angle (0-360 degrees), Saturation is a percentage (0-100%), and Value/Brightness is a percentage (0-100%). This format is often preferred by designers for intuitive color manipulation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Hsva
member.summary: Represents color values in HSVA (Hue, Saturation, Value, Alpha) format with opacity information.
member.remarks: The HSVA format extends HSV by adding an alpha channel for opacity control. It combines the intuitive color manipulation of HSV with transparency support, making it ideal for applications requiring both precise color control and opacity adjustment.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType.Opacity
member.summary: Represents the opacity/alpha channel value independently of color information.
member.remarks: The Opacity format focuses specifically on the alpha channel value, typically represented as a decimal between 0 (fully transparent) and 1 (fully opaque). This format is useful when you need to work with transparency values separately from color components.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.Mode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the mode of color picker to be rendered.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is
member.remarks:
The ColorPicker supports two distinct modes of operation:
Picker mode: Provides a continuous color spectrum with HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) controls for precise color selection
Palette mode: Displays a grid of predefined colors for quick selection, with support for custom color groups and recent colors
The mode determines the user interface layout and interaction patterns. Picker mode is ideal for applications requiring precise color selection, while Palette mode is better suited for applications with predefined color schemes or brand-specific color sets. When is enabled, users can toggle between these modes at runtime.

member.remarks: When enabled, users can switch between Picker and Palette modes using a toggle button in the ColorPicker interface. This allows for flexible color selection methods within the same component instance.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.NoColor
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether to enable or disable the no color option.
member.value: true, if the no color option is enabled. The default value is false.
member.remarks: The no color option is only available in palette mode and provides users with the ability to select "no color" or transparent as a valid choice. When enabled, an additional tile is displayed in the palette that represents the absence of color, often shown as a crossed-out or empty tile. member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.PresetColors
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the collection of custom color values that will be rendered as color picker element.
member.value: A dictionary where keys represent group names and values are string arrays of color values. The default value is null.
member.remarks:
Preset colors option is only available in palette mode. The feature allows you to define custom color groups for quick access:
Dictionary keys serve as group headers (e.g., "Brand Colors", "Theme Colors", "Custom Palette")
Dictionary values contain arrays of hex color codes that will be rendered as clickable color tiles
Colors should be specified in valid hex format (#RGB, #RRGGBB, #ARGB, #AARRGGBB)
Multiple groups can be defined to organize colors by theme, brand, or purpose
This property enhances user experience by providing quick access to commonly used colors specific to your application or brand.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.ShowButtons

member.value: true if the apply/cancel buttons are enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When enabled, users must click the "Apply" button to confirm their color selection and close the picker. When disabled, the color selection is applied immediately without requiring confirmation. The "Cancel" button allows users to discard their changes and revert to the previous color value.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the color value for color picker. It should be specified as Hex code.
member.value: A string representing the color value in hexadecimal format. The default value is #008000ff.
member.remarks:
The color value should be specified in hexadecimal format with optional alpha channel. Supported formats include:
#RGB - Short format (e.g., #F0A)
#RRGGBB - Standard format (e.g., #FF00AA)
#ARGB - Short format with alpha (e.g., #8F0A)
#AARRGGBB - Full format with alpha (e.g., #88FF00AA)
When the value changes through user interaction or programmatic assignment, the event is triggered. The alpha component represents opacity where 00 is fully transparent and FF is fully opaque.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.ShowRecentColors
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether to show the recent colors section in the color picker interface.
member.value: true if the recent colors section is displayed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property is only applicable in palette mode and enhances user productivity by providing quick access to previously selected colors. When enabled, the ColorPicker maintains a dynamic list of recently used colors that appears as a separate section in the palette interface. The recent colors list is automatically updated each time a user selects a new color, maintaining the most recently used colors at the front. This feature is particularly beneficial in design applications where users frequently reuse colors within a project or session. The recent colors are session-specific and are not persisted across browser sessions unless is also enabled.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.ValueChanged
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is raised when the color value changed.
member.value: An event callback function that receives the new color value as a string parameter.
member.remarks: This event is essential for implementing two-way data binding with the ColorPicker component. It is triggered whenever the color value changes, either through user interaction or programmatic assignment. The event provides the new color value as a hexadecimal string, enabling parent components to respond to color changes immediately. When used with @bind-Value, this event callback is automatically handled by Blazor's data binding framework.

example.code:
<SfColorPicker Value="@selectedColor" ValueChanged="@OnColorValueChanged">
            </SfColorPicker>
            @code {
                private string selectedColor = "#ff0000";
                
                private void OnColorValueChanged(string newColor)
                {
                    selectedColor = newColor;
                    // Perform additional logic with the new color
                }
            }

Event source information and interaction context

                }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfColorPicker.GetValue(System.String,Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorValueType)
member.summary: Gets the color value in the specified format type.
member.param: The color value to convert. If null, uses the current property.
The target color format type for conversion. The default is .
member.returns: A string representing the color value converted to the specified format type, or null if conversion fails.
member.remarks:
This method supports conversion between various color formats including:
Hex: Hexadecimal format without alpha (e.g., #FF0000)
Hexa: Hexadecimal format with alpha (e.g., #FF0000FF)
Rgb: RGB format without alpha (e.g., rgb(255, 0, 0))
Rgba: RGB format with alpha (e.g., rgba(255, 0, 0, 1))
Hsv: HSV format without alpha (e.g., hsv(0, 100%, 100%))
Hsva: HSV format with alpha (e.g., hsva(0, 100%, 100%, 1))
Opacity: Returns only the opacity value as a decimal number
The input value can be in any supported format and will be automatically detected and converted. If conversion fails due to invalid input format or processing errors, the method returns null.
member.exception: Thrown when an error occurs during color format conversion or processing.
