member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.DropEffect
member.summary: Specifies the type of drop effect to be applied during drag-and-drop operations in input components.
member.remarks: The enumeration defines the visual feedback and behavior that occurs when an item is dropped during a drag-and-drop operation. This enum is commonly used in file upload components and other input controls that support drag-and-drop functionality. The drop effect determines how the dragged content will be handled when dropped onto the target area.
member.example:
Setting a drop effect for a file upload component:
<SfUploader DropEffect="DropEffect.Copy"> <UploaderEvents ValueChange="OnChange"></UploaderEvents> </SfUploader>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.DropEffect.Copy
member.summary: Creates a copy of the dragged item at the drop location.
member.remarks: When Copy is specified, the original item remains in its source location while a duplicate is created at the drop target. This is the most common drop effect for file uploads where the original file remains in its source directory.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.DropEffect.Move
member.summary: Moves the dragged item from its source to the drop location.
member.remarks: When Move is specified, the item is relocated from its original position to the drop target location. The original item is removed from the source location once the drop operation is completed successfully.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.DropEffect.Link
member.summary: Creates a link or reference to the dragged item at the drop location.
member.remarks: When Link is specified, a reference or shortcut to the original item is created at the drop target. The original item remains unchanged in its source location, and the link provides access to the original content. This is useful for creating shortcuts or references without duplicating the actual data.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.DropEffect.None
member.summary: Indicates that no drop effect should be applied, effectively disabling the drop operation.
member.remarks: When None is specified, the drop target will not accept the dragged item, and no operation will be performed. This effectively disables drag-and-drop functionality for the target area and provides visual feedback that dropping is not allowed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.DropEffect.Default
member.summary: Uses the default drop effect behavior as determined by the browser or component.
member.remarks: When Default is specified, the component will use the standard drop effect behavior provided by the browser. This typically defaults to the Copy operation for most file upload scenarios, but may vary based on the browser implementation and context. Using the default option allows the component to automatically determine the most appropriate drop effect.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FormEventArgs

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FormEventArgs.InputName

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FormEventArgs.Message

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FormEventArgs.Status

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BlurEventArgs
member.summary: Defines the event arguments for the blur event in input components.
member.remarks: This class is used when an input component loses focus. The blur event typically occurs when users click outside the input field or tab to another element, providing an opportunity to validate input or save changes.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BlurEventArgs.Model
member.summary: Gets or sets the model object associated with the blur event.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FocusEventArgs

member.remarks: This class is used when an input component receives focus. The focus event occurs when users click on the input field or navigate to it using keyboard navigation, providing an opportunity to initialize or prepare the input for user interaction.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FocusEventArgs.Model
member.summary: Gets or sets the model object associated with the focus event.
member.value: An object representing the component model or data context, or null if no model is associated.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput
member.summary: Defines the default required properties and configuration options for input components.
member.remarks: This class serves as a base interface for input component configuration, providing common properties such as CSS classes, localization settings, floating label behavior, and interaction states that are shared across various input components in the Syncfusion Blazor suite.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.Change
member.summary: Gets or sets the change event mapping function for the input component.
member.value: An object representing the change event handler, or null if no change handler is specified.
member.remarks: This property allows mapping custom change event handlers to input components. The change event is typically triggered when the input value is modified and the input loses focus or when the user explicitly commits the change.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS class names to be applied to the input component.
member.value: A string containing one or more CSS class names separated by spaces, or null if no custom classes are applied.
member.remarks: This property allows custom styling of input components by applying CSS classes. Multiple classes can be specified by separating them with spaces. These classes will be added to the input element's class attribute.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether right-to-left (RTL) text direction is enabled for the input component.
member.value: true if RTL text direction is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When enabled, this property renders the input component with right-to-left text direction support, which is essential for languages such as Arabic, Hebrew, and other RTL languages. This affects both text alignment and component layout direction.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the input component is enabled for user interaction.
member.value: true if the input component is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When set to false, the input component becomes disabled and users cannot interact with it. Disabled input components typically appear grayed out and do not respond to user input or focus events.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.FloatLabelType
member.summary: Gets or sets the floating label behavior for the input component.
member.value: An object specifying the floating label type, or null to use the default behavior.
member.remarks:
This property controls how floating labels behave in input components. The available options are:
Never - The label never floats above the input, even when focused or filled
Always - The label always remains floating above the input field
Auto - The label floats above the input when focused or when the input contains a value
The Auto mode provides the most intuitive user experience for most scenarios.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.Placeholder
member.summary: Gets or sets the placeholder text to be displayed in the input component when it's empty.
member.value: A string containing the placeholder text, or null if no placeholder is specified.
member.remarks: Placeholder text provides users with hints about the expected input format or content. The placeholder is displayed in a lighter color and disappears when the user starts typing or when the input receives focus.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.Readonly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the input component is in read-only mode.
member.value: true if the input is read-only; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When set to true, the input component displays its value but prevents user modification. Read-only inputs can still receive focus and allow text selection, but users cannot edit the content. This is useful for displaying data that should be visible but not editable.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.IInput.ShowClearButton
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display a clear button in the input component.
member.value: true to show the clear button; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When enabled, a clear button (typically an 'X' icon) appears within the input component, allowing users to quickly clear the input value with a single click. The button only appears when the input contains text.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ActionCompleteEventArgs
member.summary: Provides information about the event callback.
member.remarks: This event is triggered after all selected files have been processed (either successfully uploaded or failed). It provides comprehensive information about the completed upload operation, including details of all files that were part of the upload batch.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ActionCompleteEventArgs.FileData
member.summary: Gets or sets the list of selected files' details from the component.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeRemoveEventArgs
member.summary: Provides information about the event callback.
member.remarks: This event is triggered before files are removed from the uploader component. It provides an opportunity to cancel the removal operation, modify the request parameters, or perform custom validation before the files are actually removed from the server.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeRemoveEventArgs.Cancel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the file removal action has been canceled.
member.value: true to cancel the file removal operation; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: Setting this property to true will prevent the file removal operation from proceeding. This allows for conditional removal based on custom logic or user confirmation.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeRemoveEventArgs.CurrentRequest
member.summary: Gets or sets the XMLHttpRequest instance associated with the file removal operation.
member.value: An object containing XMLHttpRequest details, or null if no request is associated.
member.remarks: This property provides access to the underlying HTTP request object that will be used for the file removal operation. It allows for customization of request headers, authentication, and other HTTP-specific settings before the removal request is sent to the server.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeRemoveEventArgs.FilesData
member.summary: Gets or sets the list of file details that will be removed from the server.
member.value: A containing the details of files to be removed, or null if no files are specified.
member.remarks: This property contains information about all files that are scheduled for removal, including file names, sizes, and other metadata. This information can be used for logging, validation, or displaying confirmation messages to users before removal.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeRemoveEventArgs.CustomFormData
member.summary: Gets or sets additional custom data in key-value pair format to be submitted with the removal request.
member.value: An object containing key-value pairs of additional data, or null if no custom data is provided.
member.remarks: This property allows developers to include additional parameters or metadata with the file removal request. Common uses include authentication tokens, user identifiers, or other application-specific data required by the server-side removal handler.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeRemoveEventArgs.PostRawFile
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the selected raw file data should be sent to the server during removal.
member.value: true to send the raw file data to the server; otherwise, false. The default is true.
member.remarks: When set to true, the complete file information including binary data is sent to the server. When set to false, only the file metadata (such as filename and size) is sent. Setting this to false can improve performance when only file identification is needed for removal operations.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeUploadEventArgs

member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether requests should include credentials for cross-origin requests.
member.value: true to include credentials such as cookies and authorization headers in cross-site requests; otherwise, false. The default is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, the upload request will include credentials such as cookies, authorization headers, and client certificates for cross-origin requests. This is essential for authenticated uploads when the upload endpoint is on a different domain than the client application.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeUploadEventArgs.CurrentRequest
member.summary: Gets or sets the XMLHttpRequest instance associated with the file upload operation.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeUploadEventArgs.FilesData

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.BeforeUploadEventArgs.CustomFormData

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.AsyncSettingsModel.ChunkSize

The chunk size should be chosen based on network conditions, server capabilities, and file sizes. Typical values range from 1MB to 10MB for optimal performance.

This property is optional; if not specified, file removal functionality will be disabled. The server endpoint should implement proper validation and security measures for file removal operations.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.AsyncSettingsModel.RetryAfterDelay

member.value: A double value representing the delay time in milliseconds. The default value is 500 milliseconds.
member.remarks: This property specifies the waiting period before the uploader attempts to retry a failed upload. The delay helps handle temporary network issues or server unavailability by allowing time for conditions to improve before retrying. A reasonable delay prevents overwhelming the server with rapid retry attempts while ensuring timely recovery from temporary failures.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.AsyncSettingsModel.RetryCount

member.remarks: This property specifies how many times the uploader will attempt to retry a failed upload before giving up. Setting an appropriate retry count prevents infinite retry loops while providing sufficient opportunities to recover from temporary failures. The default value of 3 provides a good balance between resilience and preventing excessive server load from repeated failed attempts.

This property is essential for upload functionality; without it, upload operations cannot be performed. The server endpoint should implement proper file handling, validation, and security measures.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfMaskedTextBox
member.summary: The MaskedTextBox is an input element that allows to get input from the user.
The MaskedTextBox component allows input based on a specified mask pattern.
The MaskedTextBox is an input element that allows to get input from the user.

The MaskedTextBox is an input element that allows users to enter data in a specific format by applying a mask pattern. It provides features like custom characters, prompt characters, and validation to ensure proper data entry.
member.remarks: The component enables users to enter formatted input such as phone numbers, dates, social security numbers, and other structured data. It supports various mask characters, custom regular expressions, and provides real-time validation during input.
member.example:
A simple MaskedTextBox component for phone number input.
<SfMaskedTextBox Mask="000-000-0000" Placeholder="Enter phone number" @bind-Value="@phoneNumber"></SfMaskedTextBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfMaskedTextBox.Blur
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that will be invoked when the loses focus.
member.value: An that is invoked when the component loses focus. The callback receives a containing the event details.
member.remarks: This event is triggered when the user moves focus away from the component, such as by clicking elsewhere or using keyboard navigation. You can use this event to perform validation, save data, or update other components when the user finishes interacting with the masked text input.

example.code:
<SfMaskedTextBox Mask="(999) 000-0000" Blur="@OnBlur">
            </SfMaskedTextBox>
            @code{
                private void OnBlur(MaskBlurEventArgs args)
                {
                    // Handle blur event
                    Console.WriteLine("MaskedTextBox lost focus");
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfMaskedTextBox.ValueChange
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that will be invoked when the content of has changed.
member.value: An that is invoked when the component's value changes. The callback receives a containing the new value and event details.
member.remarks: This event is triggered whenever the user modifies the content of the masked text box, including when characters are entered, deleted, or modified. The event provides access to both the raw value and the formatted value according to the specified mask pattern. This is the primary event for implementing data binding and handling user input changes in real-time.

example.code:
<SfMaskedTextBox Mask="(999) 000-0000" ValueChange="@OnChange">
            </SfMaskedTextBox>
            @code{
                private void OnChange(MaskChangeEventArgs args)
                {
                    var TextValue = args.Value;

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfOtpInput.OnBlur
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is invoked when any input field in the component loses focus.
member.value: An of type that provides blur event details.
member.remarks:
This event is triggered whenever a user leaves an OTP input field by clicking elsewhere, navigating with Tab key, or through programmatic focus changes. The event provides information about which specific input field lost focus and the current state of the component.
This event is useful for implementing validation, triggering form submissions when OTP is complete, or updating UI elements based on focus changes.

example.code:
<SfOtpInput OnBlur="@HandleBlur"></SfOtpInput>
            @code {
                private void HandleBlur(OtpFocusOutEventArgs args)
                {
                    Console.WriteLine($"Input field {args.Index} lost focus. Current value: {args.Value}");
                    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(args.Value) && args.Value.Length == 4)
                    {
                        ValidateOtp(args.Value);
                    }
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfOtpInput.OnInput
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is invoked whenever the value of any input field changes.
member.value: An of type that provides input change details.
member.remarks:
This event is triggered in real-time as users type, delete, or paste characters in any of the OTP input fields. It provides both the previous and current values, along with the index of the field that changed.
This event is ideal for implementing real-time validation, progress indicators, or triggering actions when the OTP reaches a certain length. It fires before the event.
The event includes information about which specific input field triggered the change, making it useful for field-specific logic or validation.

example.code:
<SfOtpInput OnInput="@HandleInput"></SfOtpInput>
            @code {
                private void HandleInput(OtpInputEventArgs args)
                {
                    Console.WriteLine($"Field {args.Index} changed from '{args.PreviousValue}' to '{args.Value}'");
                    
                    if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(args.Value) && args.Value.Length == 4)
                    {
                        // OTP is complete, trigger validation
                        _ = ValidateOtpAsync(args.Value);
                    }
                }
            }

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.OtpInputStyle.Underlined

member.remarks: This style creates a clean, minimal look that works well in modern, flat design interfaces. It's particularly suitable for mobile applications and contemporary web designs.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.OtpInputStyle.Filled
member.summary: Displays input fields with a filled background color instead of borders.
member.remarks: This style provides a solid, prominent appearance that can help draw attention to the input area. It works well when you want the OTP input to be a focal point of the interface.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TextTransform
member.summary: Defines the text case transformation options for the component.
member.remarks: This enumeration controls how the text case is automatically transformed as users type, providing consistency in OTP formatting regardless of how users enter the characters.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TextTransform.None
member.summary: No case transformation is applied; text appears exactly as entered by the user.
member.remarks: This is the default behavior where user input is preserved without any modification. Use this when the OTP system is case-sensitive or when you want to preserve user input exactly.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TextTransform.Uppercase
member.summary: Automatically converts all entered text to uppercase letters.
member.remarks: This is useful for OTP systems that expect uppercase input or when you want to ensure consistent formatting. Lowercase letters typed by users will be automatically converted.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TextTransform.Lowercase
member.summary: Automatically converts all entered text to lowercase letters.
member.remarks: This option ensures all text input is in lowercase, which can be useful for systems that are case-sensitive and expect lowercase input, or for maintaining visual consistency.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating
member.summary: The Blazor Rating component allows users to rate items by clicking on a set of symbols displayed on a numeric scale. This enables users to provide feedback or ratings for products, services, or content.
member.remarks: The Rating component supports various features including custom templates, different precision types, tooltips, labels, and accessibility features. It can be configured for read-only display or interactive rating input.
member.example:
A simple Blazor Rating component with a preset value.
<SfRating Value="3" />
A Blazor Rating component with a visible label.
<SfRating ShowLabel="true" />

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.AllowReset
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether to show or hide the reset button in the rating component.
member.value: true to show the reset button; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When true, the reset button will be visible to the user and they will be able to click it to reset the rating value to its default state. The reset functionality is only available when this property is set to true and the component is not in read-only or disabled mode.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets one or more CSS classes that can be used to customize the appearance of the rating component.
member.value: One or more CSS classes to customize the appearance of the rating component, such as by changing its colors, fonts, sizes, or other visual aspects. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to apply custom styling to the rating component by specifying CSS class names. Multiple CSS classes can be specified by separating them with spaces.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.Disabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether the rating component is enabled or disabled.
member.value: true to disable the rating component; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When true, the rating component will be disabled and the user will not be able to interact with it. A disabled rating component may have a different visual appearance than an enabled one, typically appearing grayed out.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.EmptyTemplate
member.summary: Gets or sets a template that defines the appearance of each unrated item in the rating component.
member.value: A of type that represents the empty item template content. The default value is null.
member.remarks: The is passed as context to the template, allowing access to information about the unrated item, such as its and . When this template is not specified, the default empty rating icon is used.
member.example: Rating with custom empty template.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.EnableAnimation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether to add animation when an item in the rating component is hovered.
member.value: true to enable hover animations; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When true, an animation will be added when the user hovers their cursor over an item in the rating component to provide visual feedback. This enhances the user experience by providing smooth visual transitions during mouse interactions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.EnableSingleSelection
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether to enable single item selection mode in the rating component.
member.value: true to enable single selection mode where only the selected item will be highlighted; false to use default behavior where all items up to the selected one are highlighted. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When true, only the selected item will be in the selected state, and all other items will be unselected. When false, all items before and including the selected one will be in the selected state, which is the traditional rating behavior.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.FullTemplate
member.summary: Gets or sets a template that defines the appearance of each rated item in the rating component.
member.value: A of type that represents the full item template content. The default value is null.
member.remarks: The is passed as context to the template, allowing access to information about the rated item, such as its and . When this template is not specified, the default filled rating icon is used.
member.example: Rating with custom full template.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.ID
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier for the rating element.
member.value: A string that represents the unique identifier for the rating element. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property sets the id attribute for the rating element. If not specified, a unique ID will be automatically generated. The ID is used for accessibility purposes and can be referenced by other elements or scripts.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.ItemsCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of items (symbols) displayed in the rating component.
member.value: An integer that specifies the number of items (symbols) displayed in the rating component. The default value is 5.
member.remarks: The rating component typically consists of a number of items, such as stars or other symbols, that represent the rating scale. This property determines how many rating items will be displayed, allowing users to select from a range of 1 to the specified count.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.LabelPosition
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the label in the rating component.
member.value: One of the enumeration values that specifies the position of the label. The default value is .
member.remarks: You can use this property to customize the position of the label within the rating component to suit the needs of your application. For example, you can set the property to to position the label at the top center of the rating component, or set it to to position the label at the left side of the component.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.LabelTemplate
member.summary: Gets or sets a template that is used as a custom label to override the default label of the rating.
member.value: A of type double that represents the label template content. The default value is null.
member.remarks: The current value of the rating is passed as context to the template, allowing you to build custom label content. When this property is set, it overrides the default label display and allows for complete customization of the label appearance and content.
member.example: Rating with label template. @context Out Of 5

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.Min
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum rating value that a user can select.
member.value: A double value representing the minimum rating that can be selected. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: You can use the property to customize the minimum possible rating in the component. For example, if you want to allow users to provide ratings from 1 to 5, you can set the property to 1 and to 5. If the current is less than the minimum, it will be automatically adjusted to the minimum value.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.Precision
member.summary: Gets or sets the precision type of the rating, which determines the granularity of the rating and allows users to provide ratings with varying levels of precision.
member.value: One of the enumeration values that specifies the precision type. The default value is .
member.remarks:
The property can be set to one of the following values:
: The rating is increased in whole number increments. For example, if the current rating is 3, the next possible ratings are 4, 5, and so on.
: The rating is increased in increments of 0.5 (half). For example, if the current rating is 3.5, the next possible ratings are 4, 4.5, 5, and so on.
: The rating is increased in increments of 0.25 (quarter). For example, if the current rating is 3.75, the next possible ratings are 4, 4.25, 4.5, and so on.
: The rating is increased in increments of 0.1. For example, if the current rating is 3.9, the next possible ratings are 4, 4.1, 4.2, and so on.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.ReadOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether the rating component is in read-only mode.
member.value: true to enable read-only mode; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When true, the rating component will be in read-only mode, which means that the user will not be able to interact with it and change the rating value. In read-only mode, the rating is displayed for viewing purposes only and cannot be modified by user interactions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.ShowLabel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether to display a label that shows the current value of the rating.
member.value: true to display the rating value label; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When true, a label will be displayed that shows the current value of the rating. The position of the label can be controlled using the property.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.ShowTooltip
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies whether to show tooltips for the rating items.
member.value: true to show tooltips for the rating items; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When true, tooltips will be displayed when hovering over rating items, showing the current rating value. The tooltip content can be customized using the property.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.TooltipTemplate

member.example:
Rating with tooltip template.
@context Star

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.UpdateMinValue
member.summary: Updates the minimum value for the rating items and validates the current value against the minimum constraint.
member.remarks: This method ensures that the minimum value is not negative and adjusts the current rating value if it falls below the minimum. If the current value is less than the minimum and no explicit value was set, the value is updated to the minimum. If an explicit value was set that is below the minimum, an is thrown.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.ValidateValue(System.Double)
member.summary: Validates and adjusts the rating value based on the specified precision type.
member.param: The rating value to validate and adjust.
member.remarks: This method ensures that the rating value conforms to the precision constraints defined by the property. The value is rounded to the nearest valid increment based on the precision type (Full, Half, Quarter, or Exact). If the adjusted value differs from the current value, the rating is updated with the new value.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfRating.GetItemValue(System.Double)
member.summary: Calculates the selection value of a particular rating item based on the current .
member.param: The position of the rating item, ranging from 1 to .
member.returns: A double value representing the selection level of the rating item, ranging from 0 to 1, where 0 is unselected and 1 is fully selected.
member.remarks: This method determines how much of a rating item should be visually selected based on the current rating value. For single selection mode with full precision, only the exact item is fully selected (1) or unselected (0). For normal mode, items are fully selected (1) if the current value is greater than or equal to their position, unselected (0) if the current value is less than the previous position, or partially selected for intermediate values.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature
member.summary: The component allows users to draw smooth signatures as vector outline of strokes using variable width Bézier curve interpolation. It provides the ability to save signatures as images and supports drawing using finger, pen, or mouse on tablets, touchscreens, and other devices.
member.remarks: The component is a user interface element for creating digital signatures or drawing text. It supports customizable stroke color, background color, and background image settings. The component provides features like undo/redo operations, signature clearing, and multiple export formats including PNG, JPEG, and SVG.
member.example:
In the below code example, a basic component is initialized.
<SfSignature style="height: 100%; width: 100%;"></SfSignature>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.HtmlAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of additional attributes that will applied to the component.
member.remarks: Additional attributes can be added as inline attributes or by specifying @attributes directive.
member.example:
In the below code example, signature height and width has been specified as style attribute in .
<SfSignature style="height: 100%; width: 100%;"></SfSignature>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.BackgroundColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the background color of the component.
member.value: A string representing the background color of the component that accepts hex value, RGB, and text values (like red). The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to customize the background color of the signature canvas. The color can be specified in various formats including hex (#FF0000), RGB (rgb(255,0,0)), or named colors (red).

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.BackgroundImage
member.summary: Gets or sets the background image for the component.
member.value: A string representing the URL or path of the image used to fill the background of the component. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to set a background image for the signature canvas. The image can be specified as a URL, base64 string, or relative path.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.Disabled
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to disable the component where the opacity is set to show disabled state.
member.value: true if the signature component is disabled for user interaction; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When this property is set to true, the signature component becomes non-interactive and displays with reduced opacity to indicate the disabled state. Users will not be able to draw signatures or interact with the component when it is disabled.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.IsReadOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to prevent interaction in the component.
member.value: true if the signature component is in read-only state where user interaction is prevented; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When this property is set to true, the signature component enters read-only mode, preventing users from drawing, editing, or modifying signatures. This is useful for displaying signatures that should not be altered while still allowing other operations like viewing or saving.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.SaveWithBackground
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to save the signature along with and while saving.
member.value: true if the signature component saves with background elements; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: This property determines whether the background color and background image are included when saving the signature. When set to true, the saved signature will include any background styling applied to the component. When set to false, only the signature strokes will be saved without background elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.StrokeColor
member.summary: Gets or sets the stroke color of the signature.
member.value: A string representing the color of the signature stroke that accepts hex value, RGB, and text values (like red). The default value is "#000000".
member.remarks: This property defines the color used for drawing signature strokes. The color can be specified in various formats including hex (#000000), RGB (rgb(0,0,0)), or named colors (black).

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.MinStrokeWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum stroke width for signature. The component calculates stroke width based on , and .
member.value: A double representing the minimum width of stroke. The default value is 0.5.
member.remarks: This property sets the minimum thickness for signature strokes. The component uses this value along with and to dynamically calculate stroke thickness based on drawing speed and pressure.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.MaxStrokeWidth
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum stroke width for signature. The component calculates stroke width based on , and .
member.value: A double representing the maximum width of stroke. The default value is 2.0.
member.remarks: This property sets the maximum thickness for signature strokes. The component uses this value along with and to dynamically calculate stroke thickness based on drawing speed and pressure.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.Velocity
member.summary: Gets or sets the velocity to calculate the stroke thickness based on the pressure of the contact on the digitizer surface. The component calculates stroke thickness based on , and .
member.value: A double representing the velocity used to calculate stroke thickness based on contact pressure on the digitizer surface. The default value is 0.7.
member.remarks: This property affects how the stroke thickness varies based on drawing speed and pressure. Higher values result in more variation in stroke thickness, while lower values produce more uniform strokes.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to persist the component's state between page reloads.
member.value: true if the component's state persistence is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the component's properties and signature data will be stored in the browser's local storage to persist the component's state across page reloads. This ensures that drawn signatures are not lost when the user navigates away from or refreshes the page.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.Changed
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is raised for actions like undo, redo, clear, and when the user completes signing on the component.
member.value: An that is invoked when signature actions occur. The callback receives a containing action details.
member.remarks: This event is triggered for various signature operations including stroke updates, undo/redo operations, and clearing the signature. You can use this event to respond to user interactions and implement custom logic based on the specific action performed.

example.code:
<SfSignature Changed="@changefunc"></SfSignature>
            @code 
            {
                private void changefunc(SignatureChangeEventArgs args) 
                {
                    if (args.ActionName == "Clear")
                    {
                        // validation code goes here
                    }
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSignature.OnSave
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is raised while saving the signature.
member.value: An that is invoked when the signature is being saved. The callback receives a containing save options.
member.remarks: This event allows you to modify the file name and file type (PNG, JPEG, SVG) using and . The event callback is triggered only for keyboard actions (Ctrl + S) and provides an opportunity to customize save parameters or cancel the save operation.

example.code:
<SfSignature OnSave="@beforesavefunc"></SfSignature>
            @code 
            {
                private void beforesavefunc(SignatureSaveEventArgs args) 
                {        
                    args.FileType = SignatureFileType.Jpeg;
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange
member.summary: Represents a color range configuration for slider track segments, defining the color and position boundaries of specific track sections.
member.remarks: The class allows you to customize different segments of the slider track with distinct colors and position ranges. This enables creating visually appealing sliders with multiple colored sections that can represent different value ranges or categories. Each color range is defined by a start position, end position, and associated color value.
member.example:
A simple ColorRange implementation.
<SfSlider TValue="int[]" Value="@rangeValue" Min="0" Max="100" Type="SliderType.Range"> <SliderColorRanges> <ColorRange Color="#ff0000" Start="0" End="25"></ColorRange> <ColorRange Color="#ffff00" Start="25" End="50"></ColorRange> <ColorRange Color="#00ff00" Start="50" End="75"></ColorRange> <ColorRange Color="#0000ff" Start="75" End="100"></ColorRange> </SliderColorRanges> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content for the ColorRange component.
member.value: A representing the child content. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property is used internally by the component infrastructure and should not be used directly in application code. The child content functionality is handled automatically by the parent slider component.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.Color
member.summary: Gets or sets the color value for the slider track segment.
member.value: A string representing the color value in any valid CSS color format (hex, RGB, HSL, or named colors). The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property defines the visual color that will be applied to the slider track segment between the specified and positions. The color can be specified using various CSS color formats such as hexadecimal (#FF0000), RGB (rgb(255, 0, 0)), HSL (hsl(0, 100%, 50%)), or named colors (red). If no color is specified, the default track color will be used for this segment.
member.example:
Setting different color formats for ColorRange.
<ColorRange Color="#ff0000" Start="0" End="25"></ColorRange> <ColorRange Color="rgb(255, 255, 0)" Start="25" End="50"></ColorRange> <ColorRange Color="hsl(120, 100%, 50%)" Start="50" End="75"></ColorRange> <ColorRange Color="blue" Start="75" End="100"></ColorRange>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.Start
member.summary: Gets or sets the starting position of the color range on the slider track.
member.value: A double value representing the start position within the slider's minimum and maximum range. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: This property defines where the colored track segment begins on the slider. The value should be within the slider's minimum and maximum range. The start position works in conjunction with the property to define the boundaries of the colored segment. If the start value is greater than the end value, the color range behavior is undefined and may not render as expected.
member.example:
Defining start position for a color range.
<ColorRange Color="#ff0000" Start="10" End="30"></ColorRange>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.End
member.summary: Gets or sets the ending position of the color range on the slider track.
member.value: A double value representing the end position within the slider's minimum and maximum range. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: This property defines where the colored track segment ends on the slider. The value should be within the slider's minimum and maximum range. The end position works in conjunction with the property to define the boundaries of the colored segment. The end value should typically be greater than the start value to create a valid color range. If the end value is less than or equal to the start value, the color range may not be visible or may not render as expected.
member.example:
Defining end position for a color range.
<ColorRange Color="#00ff00" Start="40" End="80"></ColorRange>

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.OnInitializedAsync
member.summary: Method invoked when the component is ready to start, after having received its initial parameters from its parent in the render tree.
member.remarks: This method initializes the color range by storing the initial property values and registering the color range with its parent component. The method creates a new ColorRangeDataModel instance with the current property values and adds it to the parent's color range collection. This initialization ensures that the color range is properly integrated into the slider's rendering and behavior system.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.OnParametersSetAsync
member.summary: Method invoked when the component has received parameters from its parent in the render tree and the incoming values have been assigned to properties.
member.remarks: This method monitors changes to the , , and properties and updates the parent component accordingly. When any of these properties change, the method updates the corresponding entry in the parent's color range collection and notifies the parent slider to refresh its rendering. This ensures that color range modifications are immediately reflected in the slider's visual appearance.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.ColorRange.Dispose(System.Boolean)
member.summary: Releases the unmanaged resources used by the and optionally releases the managed resources.
member.param: true to release both managed and unmanaged resources; false to release only unmanaged resources.
member.remarks: This method performs cleanup operations for the color range component, including clearing references to the parent component and color properties. The cleanup helps prevent memory leaks and ensures proper resource management when the component is no longer needed. This method is called automatically by the component lifecycle and should not be called directly from application code.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderOrientation
member.summary: Defines the orientation options for the Slider component.
member.remarks: The enum specifies how the slider is oriented on the page. This affects both the visual layout and interaction behavior of the slider component.

example.code: <SfSlider TValue="int" Value="30" Min="0" Max="100" Orientation="SliderOrientation.Horizontal"> </SfSlider>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderOrientation.Horizontal
member.summary: Renders the slider in horizontal orientation.
member.remarks: When set to Horizontal, the slider is displayed as a horizontal track from left to right. This is the default orientation and is suitable for most use cases where screen width is available.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderOrientation.Vertical
member.summary: Renders the slider in vertical orientation.
member.remarks: When set to Vertical, the slider is displayed as a vertical track from bottom to top. This orientation is useful when you have limited horizontal space or want to create a volume control-like interface.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderType
member.summary: Defines the different types of slider functionality available in the Slider component.
member.remarks: The enum determines how the slider behaves and what values it represents. Each type provides different interaction patterns and visual representations for different use cases.

example.code:
<!-- Default slider --> <SfSlider TValue="int" Value="50" Type="SliderType.Default"> </SfSlider>
<!-- Range slider --> <SfSlider TValue="int[]" Value="@(new int[]{20, 80})" Type="SliderType.Range"> </SfSlider>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderType.Default
member.summary: Creates a standard single-handle slider.
member.remarks: The Default type provides a single handle that can be moved to select a single value within the specified range. This is the most common slider type used for selecting individual values like volume, brightness, or progress.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderType.MinRange
member.summary: Creates a slider with range selection from minimum value to the selected value.
member.remarks: The MinRange type displays a filled track from the minimum value to the current handle position. This visually represents the range from the minimum value to the selected value, useful for scenarios like progress indicators or threshold selectors.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderType.Range
member.summary: Creates a dual-handle slider for selecting a range of values.
member.remarks: The Range type provides two handles allowing users to select both the start and end values of a range. The filled track appears between the two handles, making it ideal for price ranges, date ranges, or any scenario where both minimum and maximum values need to be specified.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Placement
member.summary: Defines the placement options for tick marks on the Slider component.
member.remarks: The enum controls where tick marks are positioned relative to the slider track. Tick marks help users identify precise values and provide visual reference points along the slider range. The placement depends on the slider's orientation (horizontal or vertical).

example.code: <SfSlider TValue="int" Value="50"> <SliderTicks Placement="Placement.Both" LargeStep="20" SmallStep="5" ShowSmallTicks="true"> </SliderTicks> </SfSlider>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Placement.None
member.summary: Disables the rendering of tick marks.
member.remarks: When set to None, no tick marks will be displayed on the slider. This provides a clean, minimal appearance when precise value indicators are not needed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Placement.Before
member.summary: Renders tick marks before the slider track.
member.remarks: For horizontal sliders, Before places tick marks above the track. For vertical sliders, Before places tick marks to the left of the track. This placement is useful when you want ticks on one side only for a cleaner appearance.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Placement.After
member.summary: Renders tick marks after the slider track.
member.remarks: For horizontal sliders, After places tick marks below the track. For vertical sliders, After places tick marks to the right of the track. This placement is commonly used for traditional slider designs.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Placement.Both
member.summary: Renders tick marks on both sides of the slider track.
member.remarks: When set to Both, tick marks appear on both sides of the slider track. This provides maximum visibility and is useful when the slider needs to be easily readable from different viewing angles or when emphasizing the precision of value selection.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipPlacement
member.summary: Defines the placement options for tooltips on the Slider component.
member.remarks: The enum controls where tooltips are positioned relative to the slider handle. The placement is relative to the slider's orientation and affects the tooltip's visibility and user experience.

example.code: <SfSlider TValue="int" Value="50"> <SliderTooltip IsVisible="true" Placement="TooltipPlacement.Before" ShowOn="TooltipShowOn.Hover"> </SliderTooltip> </SfSlider>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipPlacement.Before
member.summary: Positions the tooltip before the slider handle.
member.remarks: For horizontal sliders, Before places the tooltip above the handle. For vertical sliders, Before places the tooltip to the left of the handle. This placement keeps tooltips away from the user's interaction area and provides clear value visibility.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipPlacement.After
member.summary: Positions the tooltip after the slider handle.
member.remarks: For horizontal sliders, After places the tooltip below the handle. For vertical sliders, After places the tooltip to the right of the handle. This placement is useful when space constraints require tooltips on the opposite side of the default position.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipShowOn
member.summary: Defines when tooltips should be displayed on the Slider component.
member.remarks: The enum controls the trigger conditions for showing tooltips. Different display modes provide varying levels of user interaction and accessibility support. The choice affects both user experience and performance, especially in touch-enabled environments.

example.code: <SfSlider TValue="int" Value="50"> <SliderTooltip IsVisible="true" ShowOn="TooltipShowOn.Hover" Format="C2"> </SliderTooltip> </SfSlider>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipShowOn.Auto
member.summary: Displays the tooltip automatically on both focus and click interactions.
member.remarks: The Auto mode combines focus and click triggers, providing optimal accessibility support. The tooltip appears when users either tab to the slider handle (focus) or click/tap it directly. This mode ensures tooltips work well across different input methods including keyboard, mouse, and touch.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipShowOn.Focus
member.summary: Displays the tooltip only when the slider handle receives focus.
member.remarks: The Focus mode shows tooltips when users navigate to the slider using keyboard (Tab key) or screen readers. This mode is ideal for accessibility-focused applications and provides a clean interface for mouse users while ensuring keyboard navigation users always see current values.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipShowOn.Hover
member.summary: Displays the tooltip when hovering over the slider handle.
member.remarks: The Hover mode shows tooltips on mouse hover events, providing immediate feedback for mouse users. This mode works well for desktop applications but may not be suitable for touch-only devices where hover interactions are not available. Consider combining with other trigger modes for better accessibility.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.TooltipShowOn.Always
member.summary: Keeps the tooltip continuously visible at all times.
member.remarks: The Always mode permanently displays the tooltip, ensuring the current value is always visible. This mode is useful for critical value displays or when users need constant reference to the current setting. However, it may impact visual layout and should be used carefully to avoid interface clutter.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider
member.summary: Interface for holding slider properties and providing essential functionality for slider components.
member.remarks: This interface defines the contract for slider implementations, providing access to core properties like orientation, value ranges, styling, and event handling. It serves as the foundation for different types of slider components within the Syncfusion Blazor framework.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.Slider
member.summary: Gets or sets the element reference to the slider DOM element.
member.value: An that represents the slider's DOM element.
member.remarks: This property provides direct access to the slider's DOM element, which can be used for direct manipulation or accessing element-specific properties and methods.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS class names applied to the slider component.
member.value: A string containing space-separated CSS class names. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to apply custom styling to the slider by specifying CSS classes. Multiple classes should be separated by spaces.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.CustomValues
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom values for the slider when using custom step values instead of numeric ranges.
member.value: An array of string values representing custom slider values. The default value is null.
member.remarks: When this property is set, the slider will use these custom string values instead of the numeric Min, Max, and Step properties. This is useful for creating sliders with predefined text values like sizes (Small, Medium, Large) or ratings.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.EnableAnimation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether animations are enabled for slider interactions.
member.value: true if animations are enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider handle will animate smoothly when moving between positions. Disabling animations can improve performance on slower devices or when frequent value changes occur.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the slider's state should be persisted across browser sessions.
member.value: true if persistence is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider will remember its current value and other state information in browser storage. This allows the slider to maintain its state when the page is refreshed or when the user returns to the page.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the slider should render in right-to-left (RTL) mode.
member.value: true if RTL mode is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider's layout and interaction behavior will be adapted for right-to-left languages. This affects the direction of value increase/decrease and the visual layout of slider elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the slider is enabled and interactive.
member.value: true if the slider is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When disabled, the slider will be non-interactive and typically rendered with a disabled visual state. Users will not be able to change the slider value through mouse, touch, or keyboard interactions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.Max

member.value: A double representing the maximum allowable value. The default value is 100.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.Min
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum value of the slider range.
member.value: A double representing the minimum allowable value. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: This property defines the lower bound of the slider's value range. The Min value must be less than the Max value for the slider to function properly.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.Slider.Internal.ISlider.Orientation

members.member:
Represents the SfSlider partial class that contains constant string values used throughout the slider component implementation.
Specifies the type of values handled by the slider component. This can be any numeric type such as int, float, double, or decimal that supports range operations and value manipulation within the slider's minimum and maximum bounds.
This partial class serves as a centralized repository for CSS class names, HTML attributes, theme identifiers, and other string constants that are used consistently across the SfSlider component's rendering and functionality. The constants defined here ensure maintainability and consistency in the component's HTML output and styling behavior.
The class supports generic type parameters to accommodate different numeric value types while maintaining type safety throughout the slider's value handling operations.
The Slider component allows the user to select a value or range of values by dragging handles over a slider bar. Supports various types including Default, MinRange, and Range modes with customizable steps, ticks, and tooltips. The component is generic and can work with different value types including numeric arrays for range selection.
Represents the lifecycle methods and initialization logic for the component.
This partial class contains the component lifecycle methods including initialization, parameter changes, rendering, and script initialization for the Slider component. It handles component setup, property validation, persistence management, and dynamic updates throughout the component's lifecycle.
Represents a highly customizable slider component that allows users to select single values or value ranges through an intuitive drag interface with support for various orientations, step configurations, and visual enhancements.
Specifies the data type of the slider value, supporting numeric types (int, double, float, decimal), nullable numeric types, and arrays for range selection scenarios.
The component provides a comprehensive solution for value selection with three distinct operational modes:
: Single-handle slider for selecting individual values
: Single-handle slider with visual range indication from minimum to current value
: Dual-handle slider for selecting value ranges with start and end points
Key features include horizontal and vertical orientation support, customizable step intervals, tick mark configuration, tooltip display options, animation effects, accessibility compliance (ARIA support), RTL layout support, and extensive theming capabilities.
The component integrates seamlessly with Blazor's form validation system, supports two-way data binding, and provides extensive event handling for value changes, tooltip interactions, and lifecycle events. Performance optimizations include immediate or deferred value updates and state persistence across browser sessions.
Basic slider with integer values and default configuration:
<SfSlider TValue="int" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100" Step="5"> </SfSlider>
@code { private int SliderValue = 30; }
Range slider with dual handles for selecting value ranges:
<SfSlider TValue="int[]" Type="SliderType.Range" @bind-Value="@RangeValues" Min="0" Max="200"> <SliderTicks Placement="Placement.After" LargeStep="25" ShowSmallTicks="true" SmallStep="5"></SliderTicks> <SliderTooltip IsVisible="true" ShowOn="TooltipShowOn.Hover"></SliderTooltip> </SfSlider>
@code { private int[] RangeValues = new int[] { 40, 160 }; }
Vertical slider with custom values and styling:
<SfSlider TValue="string" Orientation="SliderOrientation.Vertical" CustomValues="@(new string[] { "XS", "S", "M", "L", "XL" })" @bind-Value="@SelectedSize" CssClass="custom-slider"> </SfSlider>
@code { private string SelectedSize = "M"; }
Specifies the partial class SfSlider.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.OnInitializedAsync

member.returns: A representing the asynchronous initialization operation.
member.remarks:
This method performs critical initialization tasks including:
Validates slider type compatibility with the provided value type
Configures locale settings and generates component identifiers
Sets up HTML attributes and CSS classes based on component properties
Initializes persistence values if EnablePersistence is true
Configures RTL support, button visibility, and orientation-specific styling
The method throws if Range slider type validation fails.

member.returns: A representing the asynchronous parameter update operation.
member.remarks:
This method is called whenever component parameters change and handles:
Property change notifications for all slider properties
Synchronization between internal state and public properties
Persistence storage updates when EnablePersistence is enabled
Dynamic property change processing through DynamicPropertyChange
The method ensures that all property changes are properly tracked and applied to maintain component consistency. It clears the PropertyChanges collection after processing to prepare for subsequent updates.
