member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.ID
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique HTML identifier for the slider element, enabling DOM manipulation, CSS targeting, and accessibility linking.
member.value: A representing the HTML id attribute value. When or empty, an auto-generated unique identifier is used. Default is .

remarks.para: The ID property serves multiple purposes in web applications:

item.description: Provides a unique DOM reference for JavaScript interop operations
Enables CSS selectors for custom styling: #my-slider { ... }
Supports accessibility features by linking labels: <label for="slider-id">
Facilitates form association and validation message targeting

remarks.para: When not explicitly set, the component automatically generates a unique identifier in the format "sfSlider-{GUID}" to ensure DOM validity and prevent conflicts. The ID must be unique within the entire HTML document to maintain proper DOM structure and functionality.

This property is particularly valuable in scenarios involving multiple slider instances, dynamic component generation, custom theming, integration with third-party libraries, and accessibility compliance requirements.

example.para: Setting a meaningful ID for CSS targeting and accessibility:
example.code:
<label for="price-range">Select Price Range:</label> <SfSlider TValue="int[]" ID="price-range" Type="SliderType.Range" @bind-Value="@PriceRange" Min="0" Max="1000" CssClass="price-slider"> </SfSlider>
<style> #price-range .e-slider-track { background: linear-gradient(to right, #ff6b6b, #4ecdc4); } </style>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content template that defines nested configuration components for slider features including limits, tick marks, tooltips, and color ranges.
member.value: A containing nested component markup that configures slider behavior and appearance. Default is .

remarks.para: The child content enables declarative configuration of advanced slider features through nested component syntax. Supported child components include:

item.description: Defines movement constraints and handle position boundaries
Configures tick mark placement, intervals, and formatting
Controls tooltip visibility, positioning, and content formatting
Defines colored track segments based on value ranges

remarks.para: The child content is processed during component initialization and enables rich, declarative configuration without requiring complex property assignments. Each nested component provides specialized configuration options for its respective feature area.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.ValueExpression
member.summary: Gets or sets the lambda expression that identifies the bound property for validation, model binding, and change detection in Blazor forms.
member.value: An of type that represents the property accessor lambda. Default is .

remarks.para: This property is a fundamental part of Blazor's two-way data binding and validation infrastructure. It serves multiple critical functions:

item.description: Establishes the binding relationship between the slider value and a model property
Enables automatic validation message display when used within components
Provides property metadata for validation attribute processing
Supports change tracking and dirty state detection in forms

remarks.para: The expression is automatically generated by the Blazor compiler when using the @bind-Value directive (e.g., @bind-Value="@Model.SliderValue" generates () => Model.SliderValue). Manual assignment is rarely necessary and should only be done in advanced scenarios involving dynamic binding or custom form frameworks.
This property works in conjunction with to provide comprehensive form integration and validation support, enabling the slider to participate fully in Blazor's form validation lifecycle.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.SliderEditContext
member.summary: Gets the current EditContext that provides form validation and editing services for the slider component.
member.value: The instance that manages validation and editing state, or null if not within a form context.
member.remarks: This cascading parameter is automatically provided when the slider is placed within an EditForm or other component that establishes an editing context. The EditContext enables the slider to participate in form validation, display validation messages, and maintain editing state. This property is used internally by the component and does not typically need to be accessed by application code. When present, it allows the slider to integrate seamlessly with Blazor's form validation framework.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the custom CSS classes to be added to the slider element for styling and customization.
member.remarks: Use this property to enhance the appearance of the slider by providing one or more CSS class names, separated by spaces. These classes allow you to override or extend the default styles.
member.value: A string containing CSS class names separated by spaces. The default value is an empty string.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.CustomValues
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of custom values for the slider, which can be either numbers or strings that override the default min, max, and step behavior.
member.value: An array of string values that represent the custom slider values. The default value is null.
member.remarks: When this property is set, the slider will use these custom values instead of calculating values based on the , , and properties. This is useful for creating sliders with non-linear progressions, string values, or custom scales. The values can represent any sequence such as sizes (Small, Medium, Large), ratings, or custom numeric sequences.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.EnableAnimation
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable smooth animation effects when the slider handle moves.
member.value: true if animation effects are enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider handle will move smoothly with animation effects when the value changes programmatically or through user interaction. Disabling animation can improve performance in scenarios where rapid value changes occur or when animation is not desired. This property affects both handle movement and track fill animations.
member.example:
Creating a slider without animation for better performance.
<SfSlider TValue="int" EnableAnimation="false" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to persist the component's state between page reloads.
member.value: true if state persistence is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider will save its current value and state to browser storage and restore it when the page is reloaded. This feature is useful for maintaining user selections across browser sessions and page navigations. The persisted data includes the current value, and other relevant state information.
member.example:
Enabling state persistence for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="int" EnablePersistence="true" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to render the component in right-to-left (RTL) direction.
member.value: true if RTL direction is enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider layout will be mirrored to support right-to-left languages and cultures. In RTL mode, the minimum value appears on the right side and the maximum value on the left side for horizontal sliders. This property is essential for applications that need to support Arabic, Hebrew, and other RTL languages.
member.example:
Enabling RTL layout for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="int" EnableRtl="true" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the slider is enabled and interactive.
member.value: true if the slider is enabled and allows user interaction; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When disabled, the slider becomes non-interactive and appears in a disabled visual state. Users cannot change the slider value through mouse, touch, or keyboard interactions when this property is set to false. The disabled state is useful for preventing modifications in certain application states or user permission levels.
member.example:
Creating a disabled slider that cannot be interacted with.
<SfSlider TValue="int" Enabled="false" Value="50" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Max
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum value that can be selected on the slider.
member.value: A double value that represents the maximum selectable value on the slider. The default value is 100.
member.remarks: This property defines the upper boundary of the slider's value range. The slider handle cannot be moved beyond this maximum value. When used with the property, it establishes the complete range of selectable values. For range sliders, this represents the absolute maximum value for both handles.
member.example:
Setting a custom maximum value for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="double" Max="500" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Min
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum value that can be selected on the slider.
member.value: A double value that represents the minimum selectable value on the slider. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: This property defines the lower boundary of the slider's value range. The slider handle cannot be moved below this minimum value. When used with the property, it establishes the complete range of selectable values. For range sliders, this represents the absolute minimum value for both handles.
member.example:
Setting a custom minimum value for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="double" Min="10" Max="100" @bind-Value="@SliderValue"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Orientation
member.summary: Gets or sets the orientation of the slider, determining whether it is rendered horizontally or vertically.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies the slider orientation. The default value is .
member.remarks: The orientation affects the slider's layout and interaction behavior. In horizontal orientation, the slider extends from left to right with the minimum value on the left. In vertical orientation, the slider extends from bottom to top with the minimum value at the bottom. This property also influences how keyboard navigation works with the slider.
member.example:
Creating a vertical slider.
<SfSlider TValue="int" Orientation="SliderOrientation.Vertical" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.ReadOnly
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the slider is in read-only mode, preventing user interaction while displaying the current value.
member.value: true if the slider is in read-only mode and cannot be modified by user interaction; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: In read-only mode, the slider displays the current value but prevents any user interaction such as clicking, dragging, or keyboard input. This is different from the property as the slider maintains its normal visual appearance but blocks interaction. The value can still be changed programmatically even when read-only mode is enabled. This mode is useful for displaying values that should not be modified by the user.
member.example:
Creating a read-only slider to display a value.
<SfSlider TValue="int" ReadOnly="true" Value="75" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.ShowButtons
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display increase and decrease buttons alongside the slider for precise value adjustments.
member.value: true if the increase and decrease buttons should be displayed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider displays clickable increase (+) and decrease (-) buttons that allow users to adjust the value by the amount. These buttons provide an alternative input method for users who prefer precise, incremental adjustments over dragging the handle. The buttons respect the and boundaries and will be disabled when the limits are reached.
member.example:
Enabling increase/decrease buttons for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="int" ShowButtons="true" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100" Step="5"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Step
member.summary: Gets or sets the increment value for each step when the slider value changes through user interaction or button clicks.
member.value: A double value that specifies the step increment for value changes. The default value is 1.
member.remarks: This property determines the granularity of value changes when users interact with the slider through various methods: - Dragging the handle will snap to step intervals - Clicking the increase/decrease buttons (when is enabled) will change the value by this step amount - Using arrow keys will increment or decrement by this step value - Clicking on the track will move the handle to the nearest step position The step value should be a positive number and typically divides evenly into the range between and .
member.example:
Setting a custom step value for more precise control.
<SfSlider TValue="double" Step="0.5" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="10"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Ticks
member.summary: Gets or sets the configuration options for slider tick marks, including their placement, step values, and formatting.
member.value: A object that defines the tick mark configuration options. The default value is a new instance with default settings.
member.remarks: Tick marks provide visual indicators along the slider track to help users understand the scale and available values. The configuration allows you to control: - The placement of tick marks (before, after, or both sides of the track) using the property - The step interval for displaying major ticks using the property - The step interval for displaying minor ticks using the property - Show or hide small tick marks using the property - Custom formatting for tick labels using the property Tick marks enhance the user experience by providing visual reference points and making it easier to select specific values. The tick marks automatically respect the slider's orientation and RTL settings.
member.example:
Configuring tick marks for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="int" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> <SliderTicks Placement="Placement.After" LargeStep="20" SmallStep="5" ShowSmallTicks="true"></SliderTicks> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of slider behavior, determining whether it supports single value selection, minimum range display, or range selection.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies the slider behavior type. The default value is .
member.remarks: The slider type determines the interaction model and visual appearance: - : Standard single-value slider with one handle - : Single-value slider that displays a filled track from the minimum value to the current value - : Dual-handle slider that allows selection of a value range with filled track between the handles When using , the property should be bound to an array containing the start and end values of the range.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Value
member.summary: Gets or sets the current value of the slider.
member.value: The current value of the slider of type TValue. For range sliders, this should be an array containing the start and end values. The default value is the default value of TValue.
member.remarks: The value type and structure depends on the property: - For and : A single value of type TValue - For : An array of TValue with two elements representing the range start and end values The value must fall within the bounds defined by the and properties. Value changes trigger the event callback.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.ValueChanged
member.summary: Gets or sets an event callback that is invoked when the slider value changes.
member.value: An that is triggered when the slider value changes. The callback receives the new value of type TValue.
member.remarks: This event is raised when the slider value is changed through user interaction or programmatic updates. The callback receives the new value, which can be a single value or an array depending on the property. The timing of this event depends on the property: - When true: The event fires immediately during handle dragging - When false: The event fires only when the user releases the handle This event is essential for two-way data binding with the @bind-Value directive.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the slider component.
member.value: A string that specifies the width using CSS length units (e.g., "300px", "50%", "10em"). The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to control the horizontal dimension of the slider component. You can specify the width using various CSS units such as pixels (px), percentages (%), em, rem, etc. If not specified, the slider will use its default width based on the parent container and CSS styles. For vertical sliders, this property controls the width of the entire slider component container.
member.example:
Setting a custom width for the slider.
<SfSlider TValue="int" Width="400px" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.IsImmediateValue
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the slider value should be updated immediately during handle dragging or only when dragging ends.
member.value: true if the value is updated immediately during handle dragging; otherwise, false to update only when dragging ends. The default value is true.
member.remarks: This property controls when the property and event are updated during user interaction: - When set to true: The value updates continuously as the user drags the handle, providing real-time feedback - When set to false: The value updates only when the user releases the handle, reducing the frequency of value change events Setting this to false can improve performance when the value change handling is expensive or when you only need the final value.
member.example:
Configuring deferred value updates for better performance.
<SfSlider TValue="int" IsImmediateValue="false" @bind-Value="@SliderValue" Min="0" Max="100"> </SfSlider>

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.Reposition
member.summary: This method is used to reposition slider.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfSlider`1.RepositionAsync
member.summary: Repositions the slider handle and updates its position within the container.
member.returns: A representing the asynchronous operation of repositioning the slider.
member.remarks: This method can be invoked when the slider is rendered within a popup container or when the slider dimensions change dynamically. It ensures that the slider handle is correctly positioned based on the current container dimensions and slider properties. This is particularly useful when the slider's parent container changes size or visibility state.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1
member.summary: Configure handlers to handle the events of the Slider component.
member.typeparam: The type of the slider value.
member.remarks: The class provides event callback properties that allow you to respond to various slider interactions and state changes. This class is used as a child component within the component to define event handlers.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.OnChange
member.summary: Triggers whenever the Slider value changes while dragging the slider thumb.
member.value: An event callback function that receives as parameter.
member.remarks: This event fires continuously during the dragging operation, providing real-time feedback of the slider value changes. Use this event for immediate response to value changes, such as updating UI elements or performing calculations based on the current slider position. Note that this event may fire frequently during dragging operations, so consider performance implications for complex operations.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.ValueChange
member.summary: Triggers when the Slider value is changed after the dragging of slider thumb is completed.
member.value: An event callback function that receives as parameter.
member.remarks: This event fires once when the user completes the dragging operation and releases the slider thumb. Unlike , this event provides the final committed value and is ideal for operations that should occur only after the user has finished adjusting the slider. Use this event for actions like saving data, triggering API calls, or updating bound properties that shouldn't change continuously during dragging.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.Created
member.summary: Triggers when the Slider is successfully created.
member.value: An event callback function that receives an object parameter.
member.remarks: This event fires once when the slider component has been fully initialized and rendered in the DOM. Use this event to perform initialization tasks that require the slider to be fully created, such as setting focus, calculating dimensions, or configuring additional functionality that depends on the slider's rendered state. This is the ideal place to execute code that needs to run after the component is ready for user interaction.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.TicksRendered
member.summary: Triggers when the ticks are rendered on the Slider.
member.value: An event callback function that receives as parameter.
member.remarks: This event fires after the slider ticks have been rendered on the slider track. Use this event to perform operations that depend on the ticks being fully rendered, such as applying custom styling, adding tooltips to specific tick marks, or performing calculations based on tick positions. This event is particularly useful when you need to interact with the rendered tick elements or perform post-rendering customizations.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.TicksRendering
member.summary: Triggers when the ticks elements are being rendered in the Slider, which is used to customize the ticks labels dynamically.
member.value: An event callback function that receives as parameter.
member.remarks: This event fires before each tick is rendered, allowing you to customize the appearance and content of individual tick labels. Use this event to modify tick text, apply conditional formatting, or change tick visibility based on custom logic. This is the primary mechanism for dynamic tick customization and is called for each tick during the rendering process. You can access and modify tick properties such as text, value, and styling through the event arguments.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.OnTooltipChange
member.summary: Triggers when the Slider tooltip value is changed.
member.value: An event callback function that receives as parameter.
member.remarks: This event fires when the tooltip content is about to be displayed or updated, allowing you to customize the tooltip text and format. Use this event to provide custom formatting for tooltip values, add units or prefixes, or implement conditional tooltip content based on the current slider value. The event provides access to both the current value and the tooltip text, enabling dynamic tooltip customization. This is particularly useful for displaying formatted values, currency, percentages, or other custom representations in the tooltip.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderEvents`1.Destroyed
member.summary: Triggers when the component is destroyed.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits
member.summary: Represents the limits configuration for the Slider component, allowing you to define restricted areas and handle constraints within the slider range.
member.remarks: The class provides functionality to set limit bars on the slider component, which can restrict user interaction within specific ranges. You can configure minimum and maximum start/end values, enable or disable limits, and control handle locking behavior. This is particularly useful for scenarios where you need to prevent users from selecting values outside certain boundaries.

example.code: <SfSlider TValue="int" Min="0" Max="100" Value="30"> <SliderLimits Enabled="true" MinStart="10" MaxStart="40" MinEnd="60" MaxEnd="90" StartHandleFixed="false" EndHandleFixed="false"> </SliderLimits> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.ChildContent
member.summary: Specifies the ChildContent.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the limits functionality is enabled for the slider.
member.value: true if limits are enabled; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the slider will display limit bars that restrict user interaction within the specified ranges. The limit bars are visual indicators that help users understand the allowed selection boundaries.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.EndHandleFixed
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the end handle (second handle) is locked and cannot be moved by the user.
member.value: true if the end handle is fixed and cannot be moved; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property is applicable only for range sliders. When set to true, the end handle becomes immovable, allowing users to interact only with the start handle. This is useful in scenarios where you want to maintain a fixed upper boundary while allowing adjustment of the lower value.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.MaxEnd
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum end limit value for the slider range.
member.value: A nullable double representing the maximum end limit value. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property defines the upper boundary for the end limit bar. When specified, it creates a limit bar that restricts the slider's end handle from moving beyond this value. If null, no maximum end limit is applied. The value should be within the slider's overall Min and Max range.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.MaxStart
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum start limit value for the slider range.
member.value: A nullable double representing the maximum start limit value. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property defines the upper boundary for the start limit bar. When specified, it creates a limit bar that restricts the slider's start handle from moving beyond this value. If null, no maximum start limit is applied. The value should be within the slider's overall Min and Max range and should be coordinated with to create a valid range.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.MinEnd
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum end limit value for the slider range.
member.value: A nullable double representing the minimum end limit value. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property defines the lower boundary for the end limit bar. When specified, it creates a limit bar that restricts the slider's end handle from moving below this value. If null, no minimum end limit is applied. The value should be within the slider's overall Min and Max range and should be coordinated with to create a valid range.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderLimits.MinStart
member.summary: Gets or sets the minimum start limit value for the slider range.
member.value: A nullable double representing the minimum start limit value. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property defines the lower boundary for the start limit bar. When specified, it creates a limit bar that restricts the slider's start handle from moving below this value. If null, no minimum start limit is applied. The value should be within the slider's overall Min and Max range.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks
member.summary: Represents a component that configures and renders ticks for the component.
member.remarks: The class provides properties to customize the appearance and behavior of ticks on the slider scale, including major and minor ticks positioning, formatting, and visibility options.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure ticks for a slider component:
<SfSlider TValue="double" Min="0" Max="100" Value="30"> <SliderTicks Placement="Placement.Before" LargeStep="10" SmallStep="5" ShowSmallTicks="true"> </SliderTicks> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks.ChildContent
member.summary: Specifies the ChildContent.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string used to customize the display of slider scale values.
member.value: A string that specifies the format for displaying tick values. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to format the tick labels using standard or custom format strings. It supports internationalization and custom formatting through events. When set to null, the default numeric format is used.

example.code: <SliderTicks Format="C2" /> <!-- Currency format with 2 decimal places --> <SliderTicks Format="P0" /> <!-- Percentage format with no decimal places -->

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks.LargeStep
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance between two major (large) ticks on the slider scale.
member.value: A double value that represents the interval between major ticks. The default value is 10.
member.remarks: This property controls the spacing of major ticks along the slider track. Major ticks are typically larger and more prominent than minor ticks, often displaying labels. The value must be greater than zero and should be a multiple of the slider's step value for optimal alignment.

example.code: <SliderTicks LargeStep="20" /> <!-- Major ticks every 20 units -->

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks.Placement
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the ticks relative to the slider track.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies where ticks are positioned. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property determines the visual placement of ticks around the slider track. Available options include positioning ticks before the track, after the track, or on both sides. The placement affects both major and minor ticks uniformly.

example.code: <SliderTicks Placement="Placement.Before" /> <!-- Ticks appear before the track --> <SliderTicks Placement="Placement.Both" /> <!-- Ticks appear on both sides -->

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks.ShowSmallTicks
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to display minor (small) ticks on the slider scale.
member.value: A bool value that determines the visibility of minor ticks. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, minor ticks will be displayed between major ticks based on the interval. Minor ticks provide finer granularity and visual guidance for precise value selection. These ticks are typically smaller and less prominent than major ticks and usually don't display labels.

example.code: <SliderTicks ShowSmallTicks="true" SmallStep="2" LargeStep="10" /> <!-- Shows minor ticks every 2 units and major ticks every 10 units -->

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTicks.SmallStep
member.summary: Gets or sets the distance between two minor (small) ticks on the slider scale.
member.value: A double value that represents the interval between minor ticks. The default value is 1.
member.remarks: This property controls the spacing of minor ticks along the slider track when is enabled. Minor ticks appear between major ticks and provide finer visual increments for more precise value selection. The value must be greater than zero and should typically be smaller than for meaningful tick hierarchy.

example.code: <SliderTicks SmallStep="2.5" LargeStep="10" ShowSmallTicks="true" /> <!-- Minor ticks every 2.5 units, major ticks every 10 units -->

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip
member.summary: Represents a tooltip component for the Slider control that provides contextual information and value formatting for slider handles.
member.remarks: The class enables you to display tooltips on slider handles, showing current values and providing visual feedback to users. It supports customization through CSS classes, value formatting, positioning, and visibility control. The tooltip can be configured to appear on different events such as hover or touch interactions based on the device type.
member.example:
A simple Slider with tooltip configuration.
<SfSlider TValue="int" Value="30" Min="0" Max="100"> <SliderTooltip IsVisible="true" Format="N0" Placement="TooltipPlacement.Before" ShowOn="TooltipShowOn.Auto" /> </SfSlider>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip.ChildContent
member.summary: Specifies the ChildContent.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS class names to customize the appearance and styling of the tooltip element.
member.value: A string containing space-separated CSS class names that define custom styles and themes for the tooltip element. The default value is string.Empty.
member.remarks: This property allows you to apply custom CSS classes to modify the visual appearance of the tooltip. You can use this to change colors, fonts, borders, shadows, and other visual aspects of the tooltip to match your application's design theme. Multiple CSS classes can be applied by separating them with spaces.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip.Format
member.summary: Gets or sets the format string used to customize the display of tooltip content.
member.value: A string that specifies the format pattern for displaying the slider value in the tooltip. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property supports standard .NET format strings to control how the slider value is displayed in the tooltip. For example, use "N2" for numeric formatting with two decimal places, "C" for currency formatting, or "P" for percentage formatting. When set to null, the tooltip displays the raw value without any specific formatting. This property is particularly useful for internationalization scenarios where different locales require different number formatting.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip.IsVisible
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the tooltip is visible when interacting with the slider.
member.value: A bool value that determines the visibility of the tooltip. true to show the tooltip; false to hide it. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property controls the global visibility of the tooltip for the slider component. When set to true, the tooltip will appear based on the configured behavior. When set to false, the tooltip will remain hidden regardless of user interactions. This is useful for dynamically controlling tooltip visibility based on application state or user preferences.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip.Placement
member.summary: Gets or sets the position where the tooltip appears relative to the slider handle.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies the tooltip position. The default value is the default value.
member.remarks:
This property determines the placement of the tooltip relative to the slider handle:
Before - Tooltip appears above the horizontal slider bar or to the left of the vertical slider bar
After - Tooltip appears below the horizontal slider bar or to the right of the vertical slider bar
The tooltip position automatically adjusts based on the slider's orientation (horizontal or vertical) to provide optimal visibility and user experience.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SliderTooltip.ShowOn
member.summary: Gets or sets the interaction mode that determines when the tooltip should be displayed.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies the tooltip display trigger. The default value is .
member.remarks:
This property controls how the tooltip responds to user interactions based on the device type:
Auto - Automatically detects device type and shows tooltip on hover for desktop and tap-hold for touch devices
Hover - Shows tooltip when hovering over the slider handle (desktop behavior)
Click - Shows tooltip when clicking on the slider handle
Focus - Shows tooltip when the slider handle receives keyboard focus
The Auto mode provides the best user experience by adapting to the user's device capabilities.

member.remarks: This method is called during the component lifecycle initialization phase. It registers this tooltip component with its parent slider component so that the slider can access and manage the tooltip configuration.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox
member.summary: The TextBox is an input element that allows to get input from the user. It allows the user to edit or display the text value.

Represents the Syncfusion TextBox component, which is an input element that allows users to enter, edit, and display text values. The TextBox provides various customization options including floating labels, clear button, multiline support, and input validation.
member.remarks: The component supports both single-line and multiline input modes. It can be configured with floating labels, placeholder text, clear button functionality, and various input types. The component inherits from providing base functionality for text input operations.
member.summary: The TextBox is an input element that allows to get input from the user. It allows the user to edit or display the text value.

Represents the Syncfusion TextBox component for Blazor applications, which provides an enhanced input element that allows users to enter and edit text values with advanced features like floating labels, input validation, clear button functionality, and various styling options.
member.remarks: The SfTextBox component extends the standard HTML input element with additional functionality including: - Support for floating labels (Auto, Always, Never) - Built-in clear button with customizable behavior - Input validation with visual feedback - Accessibility features with ARIA support - Integration with Blazor's EditForm validation - Persistence support for maintaining state across browser sessions - Customizable styling and theming options

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.Blur
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that will be invoked when the TextBox loses focus.
member.value: An that is invoked when the TextBox loses focus. The callback receives a containing event data.
member.remarks: The event is triggered when the user clicks outside the TextBox or navigates away from it using keyboard navigation (such as pressing Tab). This event is useful for performing validation, saving changes, or updating the UI when the user finishes interacting with the TextBox.

example.code:
<SfTextBox Placeholder="Enter your name" Blur="@OnBlur">
            </SfTextBox>
            @code{
                private void OnBlur(FocusOutEventArgs args)
                {
                    // Perform validation or other actions when TextBox loses focus
                    Console.WriteLine("TextBox lost focus");
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.ValueChange
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that will be invoked when the content of TextBox has changed and the component loses focus.
member.value: An that is invoked when the TextBox content changes and loses focus. The callback receives a containing the previous and current values.
member.remarks: The event is triggered only when the TextBox loses focus and the value has actually changed from its previous state. This differs from the event, which fires on every keystroke. Use for final value processing, validation, or when you need to compare the old and new values.

example.code:
<SfTextBox Placeholder="Enter a value" ValueChange="@OnChange">
            </SfTextBox>
            @code{
                private void OnChange(ChangedEventArgs args)
                {
                    var TextValue = args.Value;
                    var PreviousValue = args.PreviousValue;
                    // Process the changed value
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.Input
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that will be invoked when the user types or pastes text into the TextBox.
member.remarks:
The event is triggered whenever the user interacts with the TextBox by typing, pasting, or using any input method to modify the content. It provides real-time updates as the user enters text, allowing you to perform actions or validation based on the changing input.
It is important to note that the event may fire frequently during user input, potentially with each keystroke, so it is generally suitable for handling real-time updates or feedback rather than more intensive processing.

example.code:
<SfTextBox Placeholder="Enter a value" Input="@OnInput">
            </SfTextBox>
            @code{
                private void OnInput(InputEventArgs args)
                {
                    var TextValue = args.Value;
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.Autocomplete
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the browser should automatically complete or suggest values for the TextBox component.
member.value:
One of the enumeration values. The default value is . Possible values are:

Specifies that autocomplete is disabled, preventing the browser from suggesting values.
member.remarks: This property controls the HTML autocomplete attribute behavior. When enabled, browsers may display a dropdown list of previously entered values for the same field.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.FloatLabelType
member.summary: Gets or sets the floating label behavior of the component. The text acts as a floating label.
member.value: One of the enumeration values. The default value is .

remarks.para: The floating label behavior determines how the placeholder text is displayed:

item.description: The placeholder text remains static and does not float as a label.
The placeholder text floats above the TextBox as a label when the component gains focus or has a value.
The placeholder text is always displayed as a label above the TextBox component.

member.example:
The following example demonstrates setting the floating label as Auto:
<SfTextBox FloatLabelType="FloatLabelType.Auto" Placeholder="Enter a value"></SfTextBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.Placeholder
member.summary: Gets or sets the placeholder text that is displayed when the has no value.

example.code: <SfTextBox Placeholder="Enter your email address" FloatLabelType="FloatLabelType.Auto"></SfTextBox>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.Readonly

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.HtmlAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of additional HTML attributes that will be applied to the outer wrapper element of the component.
member.value: A where the key is the attribute name and the value is the attribute value. The default value is null.

remarks.para: This property allows you to add custom HTML attributes to the TextBox wrapper element, such as:
Note: If you configure both a component property and its equivalent HTML attribute, the component property takes precedence.

example.code:
<SfTextBox HtmlAttributes="@customAttributes">
            </SfTextBox>
            
            @code {
                Dictionary<string, object> customAttributes = new Dictionary<string, object>()

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfTextBox.InputAttributes
member.summary: Gets or sets a collection of additional HTML attributes that will be applied directly to the input element of the component.
member.value: A containing attribute names and values to be applied to the input element. The default value is an empty dictionary.

remarks.para: This property captures unmatched attributes and applies them directly to the HTML input element. Common attributes include:

list.item: maxlength - Maximum number of characters allowed
minlength - Minimum number of characters required
pattern - Regular expression pattern for validation

remarks.para: Attributes can be specified using inline attributes or the @attributes directive.
Note: If you configure both a component property and its equivalent HTML attribute, the component property takes precedence.

example.code:
<!-- Using @attributes directive -->
            <SfTextBox Placeholder="Enter PIN" @attributes="@inputAttributes">
            </SfTextBox>
            
            <!-- Using inline attributes -->
            <SfTextBox Placeholder="Enter email" maxlength="50" pattern="[a-z0-9._%+-]+@[a-z0-9.-]+\.[a-z]{2,}$">
            </SfTextBox>
            
            @code {
                Dictionary<string, object> inputAttributes = new Dictionary<string, object>()
                {
                    { "maxlength", "4" },
                    { "pattern", "[0-9]{4}" },
                    { "autocomplete", "one-time-code" }
                };
            }

Multiple file selection and upload
Drag and drop functionality for intuitive file selection
Automatic upload with configurable settings
Progress bar visualization during upload operations
File validation with size and type restrictions
Template customization for enhanced user experience
Chunk upload support for large files
Resume and pause upload functionality
The component integrates seamlessly with server-side upload handlers and provides comprehensive event handling for upload lifecycle management.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfUploader.CancelAsync(Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FileInfo[])

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfUploader.ClearAllAsync
member.summary: Clears all file entries from the upload list, including both uploaded files and files in the upload queue.
member.returns: A that represents the asynchronous clear operation.

The method behavior varies based on whether the uploader is configured with server-side processing (SaveUrl) or client-side only processing. For server-side uploads, it communicates with the server to clear files, while for client-side only uploads, it clears the local file list.

Clear all files from the uploader:
await uploaderInstance.ClearAllAsync();

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfUploader.RemoveAsync(Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FileInfo[],System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Object)

member.param: An array of objects representing the files to remove from the file list and server. If null or empty, the complete file list will be cleared.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfUploader.ResumeAsync(Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FileInfo[],System.Nullable{System.Boolean})
member.summary: Resumes the chunked upload that was previously paused based on the specified file data.
member.param: An array of objects representing the files to resume. If null, all paused uploads will be resumed.
A value indicating whether custom UI is being used. Set to true if using custom UI templates.
member.returns: A that represents the asynchronous resume operation.
member.remarks: This method continues the upload process for files that were previously paused using . The upload resumes from the exact point where it was paused, utilizing the already uploaded chunks without re-uploading them. This feature is particularly useful for handling large file uploads where network interruptions or user preferences require temporary pausing.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.SfUploader.RetryAsync(Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.FileInfo[],System.Nullable{System.Boolean},System.Nullable{System.Boolean})
member.summary: Retries the canceled or failed file upload based on the specified file data.
member.param: An array of objects representing the files to retry. If null, all canceled or failed uploads will be retried.
A value indicating the retry starting point. Set to true to retry from the canceled stage, or false to retry from the initial stage.
A value indicating whether custom UI is being used. Set to true if using custom UI templates.
member.returns: A that represents the asynchronous retry operation.
member.remarks: This method allows users to restart uploads for files that have failed or been canceled during the upload process. When retrying from the canceled stage, the upload continues from where it was interrupted, preserving any successfully uploaded chunks. When retrying from the initial stage, the entire upload process starts over from the beginning. This functionality is essential for handling network issues, server timeouts, or user-initiated cancellations.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings
member.summary: Represents the asynchronous settings configuration for the component, enabling chunk upload, retry mechanisms, and server endpoint configurations.
member.remarks: The class provides comprehensive configuration options for handling asynchronous file upload operations. It supports chunk-based uploading for large files, automatic retry mechanisms for failed uploads, and configurable server endpoints for save and remove operations. This class is essential for implementing robust file upload functionality with enhanced reliability and performance optimization.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure asynchronous settings for the Uploader component:
<SfUploader> <UploaderAsyncSettings SaveUrl="/api/upload" RemoveUrl="/api/remove" ChunkSize="1048576" RetryCount="3" RetryAfterDelay="1000"> </UploaderAsyncSettings> </SfUploader>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings.ChildContent
member.summary: Specifies the content that has to be passed.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings.ChunkSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the chunk size in bytes for splitting large files into smaller chunks during upload.
member.value: A value representing the chunk size in bytes. The default value is 0, which disables chunk upload.
member.remarks: When the property is set to a value greater than 0, the automatically enables chunk upload functionality. Large files are divided into smaller chunks of the specified size and uploaded sequentially to the server. This approach improves upload reliability for large files and provides better progress tracking. The chunk size must be specified in bytes and should be chosen based on network conditions and server capabilities.

example.code: <UploaderAsyncSettings ChunkSize="1048576"> <!-- 1 MB chunks --> </UploaderAsyncSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings.RemoveUrl
member.summary: Gets or sets the server endpoint URL for handling file removal operations.
member.value: A representing the server URL that handles file removal requests. The default value is .
member.remarks: The property specifies the server endpoint that will receive and process file removal requests. The server endpoint must accept POST requests and should define a "RemoveFileNames" attribute to receive the file information that needs to be removed. This property is optional; if not specified, the remove functionality will be disabled. The server implementation should handle the removal of files from the storage location and return appropriate responses.

example.code: <UploaderAsyncSettings RemoveUrl="/api/files/remove"> </UploaderAsyncSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings.RetryAfterDelay
member.summary: Gets or sets the delay time in milliseconds before automatic retry attempts for failed uploads.
member.value: A value representing the delay in milliseconds before retry attempts. The default value is 500 milliseconds.
member.remarks: The property controls the waiting period between failed upload attempts and automatic retries. This delay helps prevent overwhelming the server with immediate retry requests and allows for temporary network issues to resolve. The delay is applied before each retry attempt, providing a progressive approach to handling upload failures. A reasonable delay value improves the success rate of retry operations while maintaining good user experience.

example.code: <UploaderAsyncSettings RetryAfterDelay="1000"> <!-- 1 second delay --> </UploaderAsyncSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings.RetryCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum number of retry attempts for failed file uploads.
member.value: An value representing the maximum number of retry attempts. The default value is 3.
member.remarks: The property defines the maximum number of automatic retry attempts the will perform when a file upload fails. This property is essential to prevent infinite retry loops and control resource usage. After the specified number of retry attempts is exhausted, the upload will be marked as failed. Setting an appropriate retry count helps balance between upload reliability and system performance. The retry mechanism works in conjunction with to provide controlled and intelligent retry behavior.

example.code: <UploaderAsyncSettings RetryCount="5"> <!-- Maximum 5 retry attempts --> </UploaderAsyncSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Inputs.UploaderAsyncSettings.SaveUrl
member.summary: Gets or sets the server endpoint URL for handling file upload and save operations.
member.value: A representing the server URL that handles file upload requests. The default value is .
member.remarks: The property specifies the server endpoint that will receive uploaded files and handle the save operations. The server endpoint must accept POST requests and should define the request parameter with the same input name used to render the component. This URL is essential for asynchronous file upload functionality and must be properly configured to handle multipart form data. The server implementation should process the uploaded files, save them to the desired location, and return appropriate responses indicating success or failure.

example.code: <UploaderAsyncSettings SaveUrl="/api/files/upload"> </UploaderAsyncSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.InteractiveChat.SfAIAssistView.AttachmentUploadChange
member.summary: Gets or sets the event callback that will be invoked when the attached files are uploaded in the component.
member.value: An that handles attachment upload events. The default value is an empty event callback.

remarks.para: This event is triggered when users upload file attachments within the AI AssistView component. Unlike traditional file upload scenarios, this event enables client-side file processing without requiring a server endpoint, making it ideal for AI-powered applications that need to process attachments locally or send them directly to AI services.

The event provides access to uploaded file information through the parameter, allowing developers to read file contents using the OpenReadStream() method of the interface. This is particularly useful for AI AssistView scenarios where file content needs to be analyzed, processed, or included in AI prompts.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Layouts.SfSplitter.EnableReversePanes
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the order of splitter panes should be reversed.
member.value: true, if the splitter panes are reordered. Otherwise, false.
member.remarks:
When set to true, the order of the panes within the component will be reversed. This means that the right-most or bottom-most pane will appear as the first pane, and the other panes will follow in reverse order.
Reversing the pane order can be useful in scenarios where you want to present content in the opposite direction, such as creating layouts that flow from right to left or from bottom to top.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Layouts.SfSplitter.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether right-to-left (RTL) mode is enabled for the component.
member.value: true if RTL mode is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks:
When RTL mode is enabled, the content of the component will be presented in a right-to-left direction. This affects the positioning and alignment of the splitter panes and other content.
Enabling RTL mode can be useful when designing applications for languages that are written from right to left, such as Arabic, Hebrew, or Persian.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Layouts.SfSplitter.Enabled
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the component is enabled.
member.value: true if the component is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks:
When the component is enabled, user interactions and behaviors associated with the Splitter, such as resizing panes, are allowed. When disabled, these interactions are restricted and the component becomes non-interactive.
By default, the component is enabled. You can set this property to false to prevent user interactions temporarily, if needed.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Layouts.SfSplitter.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether persistence of the component's state is enabled.
member.value: true if persistence is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When persistence is enabled, the state of the component is saved and restored across page reloads or navigations. This allows the component to remember its previous state and provide a consistent user experience.

member.summary: The Blazor Timeline component presents a series of events or activities in chronological order, allowing users to track the progression of time.
member.remarks: Timeline items can be populated by specifying within tag directive.

<SfTimeline> <TimelineItems> <TimelineItem></TimelineItem> <TimelineItem></TimelineItem> <TimelineItem></TimelineItem> <TimelineItem></TimelineItem> </TimelineItems> </SfTimeline>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Lists.AnimationSettings.Duration
member.summary: Gets or sets the time duration of transform object.
member.value: If we set the duration value, then the content transforms with in specified duration otherwise the default duration value 400 is set.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Lists.AnimationSettings.Easing
member.summary: Gets or sets the easing effect applied while transform.
member.value: If we set the easing value, then the specified easing effect is applied for expand action otherwise the default easing value `ease` is set.
member.remarks: The available easing value are: - `ease - Default value. The animation has a slow start, then fast, before it ends slowly.` - `linear - The animation has the same speed from start to end.` - `ease-in - The animation has a slow start.` - `ease-out - The animation has a slow end.` - `ease-in-out - The animation has both a slow start and a slow end.`

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Lists.AnimationSettings.Effect
member.summary: Gets or sets the effect which is shown in sub list transform.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is SlideLeft
member.remarks: The available effects are: - `None`. - `SlideLeft`. - `SlideDown`. - `Zoom`. - `Fade`.

example.code:

             @code {
                List<DataModel> ListData = new List<DataModel>();

                protected override void OnInitialized()
               {
                       base.OnInitialized();
                       ListData.Add(new DataModel
               {
                   Text = "Asia",
                   Id = "01",
                   Category = "Continent",
                   Child = new List<DataModel>() {
                       new DataModel {
                           Text = "India",
                               Id = "1",
                               Category = "Asia",
                               Child = new List<DataModel> () {
                                   new DataModel {
                                       Id = "1001",

                                           Category = "India"

                                           Category = "India"
                                   }
                               }
                       },

                               Category = "Asia",

                                       Text = "Zhejiang",
                                           Id = "2001",
                                           Category = "China"
                                   }
                               }
                       }
                   }
               });
               ListData.Add(new DataModel
                   {
                   Text = "North America",
                   Id = "02",
                   Category = "Continent",
                   Child = new List<DataModel>() {
                       new DataModel {
                           Text = "USA",

                                       Text = "New York",

                               }
                       },

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Maps.IMarker.WidthValuePath
member.summary: This property specifies the field name from the objects in the marker data source to adjust the width of each marker individually within the group.
member.value: Accepts the string value which represents the field name from the objects in the marker data source.
member.remarks: When a numeric or string value is provided in the specified field, that value is used to determine the width of the current marker. If a numeric value is provided, the default value of "0" will be applied. In this case, the marker will not be rendered if the field contains only the default value.To handle this, nullable numeric types should be used and the width will be taken from the Width property of MapsMarker.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Maps.IMarker.HeightValuePath
member.summary: This property specifies the field name from the objects in the marker data source to adjust the height of each marker individually within the group.
member.value: Accepts the string value which represents the field name from the objects in the marker data source.
member.remarks: When a numeric or string value is provided in the specified field, that value is used to determine the height of the current marker. If a numeric value is provided, the default value of "0" will be applied. In this case, the marker will not be rendered if the field contains only the default value.To handle this, nullable numeric types should be used and the height will be taken from the Height property of MapsMarker.

Gets or sets a value indicating whether the user can drag and drop markers on the map at any location.
true to enable marker drag and drop functionality; otherwise, false to disable marker drag and drop functionality. The default value is false.
You can enable or disable the marker drag and drop functionality through mouse or touch interactions in the component.

member.summary: This property specifies the field name from the objects in the marker data source to adjust the width of each marker individually within the group.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FilterType
member.summary: Specifies the filter type for searching values in the component.
member.remarks: This enumeration defines how the search operation is performed when filtering items in the MultiColumnComboBox. The filter type determines the matching logic used to find items based on user input.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to set the filter type for a MultiColumnComboBox:
<SfMultiColumnComboBox TValue="string" TItem="Employee" DataSource="@Employees" AllowFiltering="true" FilterType="FilterType.Contains"> </SfMultiColumnComboBox>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FilterType.Contains
member.summary: Filters items where the search term is found anywhere within the text values of the component.
member.remarks: This filter type performs a case-insensitive substring search, matching items that contain the search term at any position within the text. It provides the most flexible search experience for users.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FilterType.EndsWith
member.summary: Filters items where the search term matches the ending portion of the text values in the component.
member.remarks: This filter type performs a case-insensitive suffix match, displaying only items whose text ends with the specified search term. Useful for scenarios like searching by file extensions or suffixes.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FilterType.StartsWith
member.summary: Filters items where the search term matches the beginning portion of the text values in the component.
member.remarks: This filter type performs a case-insensitive prefix match, displaying only items whose text begins with the specified search term. Commonly used for autocomplete scenarios and alphabetical searching.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FloatLabelType
member.summary: Specifies the floating label behavior for the placeholder text in the component.
member.remarks: The floating label feature enhances user experience by providing dynamic placeholder behavior. It helps maintain context about the input field's purpose while allowing users to see their entered values clearly.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure floating labels:
<SfMultiColumnComboBox TValue="string" TItem="Employee" DataSource="@Employees" Placeholder="Select an employee" FloatLabelType="FloatLabelType.Auto"> </SfMultiColumnComboBox>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FloatLabelType.Never
member.summary: The placeholder text remains in its original position and does not float in the component.
member.remarks: In this mode, the placeholder text behaves like traditional HTML placeholder text, disappearing when the user starts typing. This provides a familiar, standard input field experience.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FloatLabelType.Always
member.summary: The placeholder text is always displayed as a floating label above the input field in the component.
member.remarks: The label remains visible at all times, positioned above the input field, providing constant context about the field's purpose. This ensures users always know what information is expected in the field.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.FloatLabelType.Auto
member.summary: The placeholder text floats above the input field when the user focuses on the field or enters text in the component.
member.remarks: This provides an optimal user experience by showing the placeholder normally until interaction begins, then floating it above to maintain context. The label automatically transitions between normal and floating positions based on user interaction and content presence.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextOverflowMode
member.summary: Defines how cell content is handled when it exceeds the available display area in the MultiColumnComboBox component.
member.remarks:
Text overflow handling is crucial for maintaining layout consistency while ensuring content remains accessible. Different overflow modes provide varying levels of user experience and content visibility.
Clip Truncates the cell content when it overflows its area.
Ellipsis Displays ellipsis when the cell content overflows its area.
EllipsisWithTooltip Displays ellipsis when the cell content overflows its area and shows tooltip on hover for full content visibility.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure text overflow handling:
<SfMultiColumnComboBox TValue="string" TItem="Employee" DataSource="@Employees" TextOverflowMode="TextOverflowMode.EllipsisWithTooltip"> </SfMultiColumnComboBox>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextOverflowMode.Clip
member.summary: Truncates the cell content abruptly when it exceeds the available display area.
member.remarks: This mode provides the most space-efficient display but may result in loss of important information. Content is cut off without any visual indication that more text exists.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextOverflowMode.Ellipsis
member.summary: Displays an ellipsis ("...") when the cell content exceeds the available display area.
member.remarks: This mode provides a visual indication that content extends beyond the visible area. Users can understand that more content exists, though they cannot access it directly.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextOverflowMode.EllipsisWithTooltip
member.summary: Displays an ellipsis ("...") when the cell content exceeds the available display area and shows the full content in a tooltip on hover.
member.remarks: This mode provides the optimal user experience by combining space efficiency with full content accessibility. Users can quickly scan truncated content while having access to complete information through hover interaction.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextWrapElement
member.summary: Defines which elements have text wrapping applied in the MultiColumnComboBox component.
member.remarks:
Text wrapping allows long text to be displayed across multiple lines within cells, improving readability and ensuring all content is visible. Different wrapping strategies can be applied based on specific UI requirements and content characteristics.
Both Default option. Applies text wrapping to both header and content cells.
Header Applies text wrapping only to header cells, keeping content cells on single lines.
Content Applies text wrapping only to content cells, keeping header cells on single lines.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to configure text wrapping:
<SfMultiColumnComboBox TValue="string" TItem="Employee" DataSource="@Employees" AllowTextWrap="true" TextWrapElement="TextWrapElement.Content"> </SfMultiColumnComboBox>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextWrapElement.Both
member.summary: Applies text wrapping to both column headers and cell content throughout the MultiColumnComboBox.
member.remarks: This is the default behavior that ensures comprehensive text visibility across all elements. Both headers and data cells will wrap their content across multiple lines when necessary, providing optimal content accessibility.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextWrapElement.Header
member.summary: Applies text wrapping only to column header cells in the MultiColumnComboBox.
member.remarks: This mode is useful when header text tends to be longer but content should remain compact. Content cells will display on single lines, potentially with overflow handling, while headers can expand vertically as needed.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.TextWrapElement.Content
member.summary: Applies text wrapping only to content cells in the MultiColumnComboBox.
member.remarks: This mode is ideal when data content may be lengthy but headers should remain concise. Header cells will display on single lines while content cells can wrap across multiple lines for full visibility.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.IMultiColumnComboBox
member.summary: Defines the contract for the Syncfusion Blazor Multi-Column ComboBox component, providing methods for managing child component properties and column configurations.
member.remarks:
The IMultiColumnComboBox interface serves as the primary contract for the Multi-Column ComboBox component, enabling dynamic updates to column properties and configurations. This interface is essential for components that need to programmatically modify column settings, data binding, and display properties at runtime.
Implementing this interface allows for: - Dynamic column property updates without full component re-rendering - Programmatic control over column configurations - Efficient handling of child component property changes - Integration with data-driven scenarios where column properties may change based on user interactions or data updates
This interface is typically implemented by the SfMultiColumnComboBox component to provide a standardized way of managing column properties and ensuring consistent behavior across different usage scenarios.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.IMultiColumnComboBox.UpdateChildProperties(Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.MultiColumnComboboxColumns)
member.summary: Asynchronously updates the child properties of the Multi-Column ComboBox component, allowing for dynamic modification of column configurations and display settings.
member.param: The MultiColumnComboboxColumns object containing the updated properties and configurations to be applied to the child component. This parameter must not be null.
member.returns: A Task representing the asynchronous operation of updating the child properties. The task completes when all property updates have been successfully applied to the component.
member.remarks:
This method provides a mechanism for dynamically updating column properties without requiring a full component refresh. It is particularly useful in scenarios where:
- Column configurations need to be modified based on user interactions - Data binding properties require updates after data source changes - Display settings need to be adjusted programmatically - Performance optimization is required to avoid full component re-rendering
The method operates asynchronously to ensure that UI updates do not block the main thread, providing a smooth user experience even when multiple property updates are being processed simultaneously.
Usage Considerations: - Ensure the properties parameter contains valid column configurations - The method should be awaited to ensure all updates are completed before proceeding - Multiple rapid calls to this method are handled efficiently through internal batching mechanisms - Property validation is performed internally to prevent invalid configurations
Performance Notes: - This method is optimized to update only the properties that have actually changed - Batch updates are more efficient than multiple individual property updates - The asynchronous nature prevents UI blocking during complex property updates
member.exception: Thrown when the properties parameter is null.
Thrown when the component is in an invalid state for property updates.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.MultiColumnComboboxColumn

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.MultiColumnComboBox.SfMultiColumnComboBox`2
member.summary: The MultiColumnComboBox component provides a rich user interface for selecting items from a data source with multiple columns displayed in a grid format. It supports features like filtering, paging, custom templates, and keyboard navigation.
member.typeparam: Specifies the type of value that the MultiColumnComboBox can bind to.
Specifies the type of data items in the MultiColumnComboBox data source.
member.example:
A basic MultiColumnComboBox with multiple columns.
<SfMultiColumnComboBox TValue="int" TItem="Employee" DataSource="@employees" ValueField="EmployeeId" TextField="EmployeeName"> <MultiColumnComboBoxColumns> <MultiColumnComboBoxColumn Field="EmployeeId" Header="ID" Width="120"></MultiColumnComboBoxColumn> <MultiColumnComboBoxColumn Field="EmployeeName" Header="Name" Width="150"></MultiColumnComboBoxColumn> <MultiColumnComboBoxColumn Field="Department" Header="Department" Width="120"></MultiColumnComboBoxColumn> </MultiColumnComboBoxColumns> </SfMultiColumnComboBox>
member.remarks: The MultiColumnComboBox component extends the functionality of a standard dropdown by displaying data in a tabular format with multiple columns. This allows users to view and select items based on multiple data fields simultaneously. The component supports various advanced features including filtering, paging, grouping, custom value handling, and extensive customization options through templates and styling.
member.summary: Represents a multi-column combobox component that provides a dropdown list with multiple columns to display data.
member.remarks:
The component allows users to select from a dropdown list that displays data in a multi-column grid format, providing better visualization of complex data structures. It supports features like filtering, sorting, paging, virtual scrolling, and custom templates. The component uses two generic type parameters:
TValue: The type of the value property, which represents the selected value of the combobox (e.g., int? for a nullable integer).
TItem: The type of the data items in the data source, typically a class or model representing the structure of the data (e.g., a Product class).

Action failure error messages
Accessibility labels and descriptions
Grid-related text content

remarks.para: The component will fall back to default English text if the Localizer is null or if specific locale keys are not found. This property is essential for applications that need to support multiple languages or cultures.

member.param: The used to build the component's render tree.

remarks.para: This method overrides the base implementation to construct the complete UI structure for the MultiColumnComboBox, which consists of:

item.description: A cascading value container that provides the component instance to child components
An input field component () with associated event handlers and styling
A dropdown popup containing a data grid () when ShowGrid is true
No records or action failure templates when applicable
An optional footer template when configured

remarks.para: The method delegates the actual rendering logic to RenderInputAndGridCombined which handles the complex component composition, event binding, and conditional rendering based on the component's current state and configuration.

This approach ensures proper component lifecycle management and maintains the hierarchical structure required for accessibility, keyboard navigation, and proper event handling between the input field and dropdown grid.
