member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfAccordion
member.summary: Accordion is a vertically collapsible panel that displays one or more panels at a time.
member.remarks: Accordion items can be populated by specifying within tag directive.
member.example:
In the below code example, a basic accordion component initialized with tag directive.
<SfAccordion> <AccordionItems> <AccordionItem Header="ASP.NET"> <ContentTemplate> Microsoft ASP.NET is a set of technologies in the Microsoft .NET Framework for building Web applications and XML Web services. </ContentTemplate> </AccordionItem> <AccordionItem Header="ASP.NET MVC"> <ContentTemplate> The Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern separates an application into three main components: the model, the view, and the controller. </ContentTemplate> </AccordionItem> <AccordionItem Header="JavaScript"> <ContentTemplate> JavaScript (JS) is an interpreted computer programming language. It was originally implemented as part of web browsers so that client-side scripts could interact with the user, control the browser, communicate asynchronously, and alter the document content that was displayed. </ContentTemplate> </AccordionItem> </AccordionItems> </SfAccordion>

example.code: <SfAccordion @bind-ExpandedIndices="@ExpandedIndices"> <AccordionItems> <AccordionItem Header="ASP.NET"> <ContentTemplate> Microsoft ASP.NET is a set of technologies in the Microsoft .NET Framework for building Web applications and XML Web services. </ContentTemplate> </AccordionItem> <AccordionItem Header="ASP.NET MVC"> <ContentTemplate> The Model-View-Controller (MVC) architectural pattern separates an application into three main components: the model, the view, and the controller. </ContentTemplate> </AccordionItem> <AccordionItem Header="JavaScript"> <ContentTemplate> JavaScript (JS) is an interpreted computer programming language. It was originally implemented as part of web browsers so that client-side scripts could interact with the user, control the browser, communicate asynchronously, and alter the document content that was displayed. </ContentTemplate> </AccordionItem> </AccordionItems> </SfAccordion> @code{ int[] ExpandedIndices = new int[] { 0, 1 }; }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfAccordion.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the accordion element in pixels/number/percentage.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfBreadcrumb.OverflowMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates how to display breadcrumb items when the breadcrumb items count exceeds .
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is
member.remarks: If the OverflowMode is Hidden, the exceeded items will be hidden and while clicking on the previous item, the hidden item will become visible. If the OverflowMode is Collapsed, only the first and last items will be visible, and the remaining items will be hidden with collapsed icon. When the collapsed icon is clicked, all items become visible and scroll will be enabled if the space is not enough to show all items. If the OverflowMode is Menu, it shows the number of breadcrumb items that can be accommodated within the container space, and creates a sub menu with the remaining items. If the OverflowMode is Wrap, it wraps the items on multiple lines when the Breadcrumb�s width exceeds the container space. If the OverflowMode is Scroll, it shows an HTML scroll bar when the Breadcrumb�s width exceeds the container space. If the OverflowMode is None, it shows all the items on a single line.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfDropDownTree`2.AutoUpdateCheckState
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that determines whether the checked state of parent nodes in the component is automatically updated based on the checked state of their child nodes.
member.value: true if automatic update of parent node checked states is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When the property is set to `true`, the checked state of parent nodes in the component will be automatically updated based on the checked state of their child nodes. This is useful for maintaining the consistency of the checkbox hierarchy and ensuring that parent nodes are checked only if all their child nodes are also checked. This property only works when the property is set to `true`.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfDropDownTree`2.LoadOnDemand
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that determines whether child nodes will be rendered while expanding and collapsing a parent node inside the popup, instead of loading all tree nodes initially in the component.
member.value: Set to true to load child nodes dynamically on expanding a parent node; otherwise, set to false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: By default, is disabled, so child nodes are rendered during initial rendering. Enabling this property as true can improve the performance of the component on initial load, as it loads only parent nodes initially.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfDropDownTree`2.ExpandOn
member.summary: Gets or sets the value that indicates the action on which the node expands or collapses in the popup of the component.
member.value: The default value is ExpandAction.DoubleClick.
member.remarks: The available actions are: - ExpandAction.Click: The expand/collapse operation happens when you single-click on the node in desktop. - ExpandAction.DblClick: The expand/collapse operation happens when you double-click on the node in desktop. - ExpandAction.None: The expand/collapse operation will not happen. In mobile devices, the node expand/collapse action happens on single tap always.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.GoToPageAsync(System.Int32)
member.summary: Navigates to the given page number in the Pager, it can also fetch the given page by traversing between the next and previous pagers if present in the Pager component.
member.param: Enter the page number to be shown in the Pager.
member.remarks: When the given page number is greater than the total pages, then no actions will be performed in the Pager.

example.code:
<button @onclick="HandleButtonClick">GoToPage</button>
            <SfPager @ref="Pager" PageSize=5 NumericItemsCount=4 TotalItemsCount=100>
             ........
            </SfPager>
            @code{
               SfPager Pager;
               private async Task HandleButtonClick()
               {
                 await Pager.GoToPageAsync(10); // pass the page number here.    
               }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.GoToLastPageAsync
member.summary: Navigates to the last page in the Pager by traversing the next pagers, if present in the Pager component.
member.remarks: If the current selected page is the last page of the Pager, then no actions will be performed in the Pager component.

example.code:
<button @onclick="HandleButtonClick">GoToLastPage</button>
            <SfPager @ref="Pager" PageSize=5 NumericItemsCount=4 TotalItemsCount=100>
             ........
            </SfPager>
            @code{
               SfPager Pager;
               private async Task HandleButtonClick()
               {
                 await Pager.GoToLastPageAsync();
               }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.GoToFirstPageAsync

            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.GoToNextPageAsync
member.summary: Navigate to the next page in the Pager. Consider the currently selected page is the last numeric item of the Pager, then it's loaded the next set of numeric items if it exists.

            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.GoToPreviousPageAsync

            }

               }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.UpdateNumericItemsCountAsync(System.Int32)
member.summary: Used to update the number of numeric elements shown in the Pager component, and the next pager icon is used to get the next set of entered numeric pages count, likewise the previous pager icon is used to traverse backward between the pages.

               {
                 await Pager.UpdateNumericItemsCountAsync(6); // pass the numeric items count here.    
               }
            }

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfPager.RefreshAsync

example.code:
<button @onclick="HandleButtonClick">Refresh</button>
            <SfPager @ref="Pager" PageSize=5 NumericItemsCount=4 TotalItemsCount=100>

member.summary: Gets or sets the list of toolbar items that will be populated using the tag directive.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfToolbar.OverflowMode
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates how to display toolbar items when the toolbar content exceeds the viewing area.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is
member.remarks: If the OverflowMode is Scrollable, all the elements are displayed in a single line with enabled horizontal scrolling. If the OverflowMode is Popup, prioritized elements are displayed on the toolbar and the rest of elements are moved to the popup. If the popup content overflows the height of the page, the rest of the elements will be hidden. If the OverflowMode is MultiRow, overflow toolbar items are displayed as in-line of toolbar. If the OverflowMode is Extended, hides the overflow items in next row. The extended content were shown when click on the expand icon.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfToolbar.ScrollStep
member.summary: Gets or sets the scrolling distance of toolbar scroller.
member.value: When the left/right navigation icon is clicked, then the toolbar scrolled based on the specified value otherwise the default value `0` is set.

example.code: <SfToolbar ScrollStep="50"></SfToolbar>

member.remarks: This property is applicable only when is set.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfToolbar.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the toolbar element in pixels/number/percentage.
member.value: If we set the width value, then the toolbar will render based on specified width otherwise the default width value `auto` is set.

example.code: <SfToolbar Width="500px"></SfToolbar>

member.remarks: If we set number values, then it is considered as pixels.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.ToolbarItem.Overflow
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates whether to display the toolbar item on toolbar or not, when the content is too large to fit available space.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is
member.remarks: If the OverflowOption is Show, always shows the toolbar item as the primary priority on the Toolbar. If the OverflowOption is Hide, always shows the toolbar item as the secondary priority on the popup. If the OverflowOption is None, no priority were set for toolbar item, as per normal order moves to popup when content exceeds. This property is applicable only when is Popup of Extended.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.ToolbarItem.Type
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the type of toolbar item to be rendered in toolbar.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.AllowDragAndDrop
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the allows nodes to be reordered using drag and drop.
member.value: true if drag and drop is allowed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: On desktop devices, nodes can be reordered by clicking and dragging them to the target position and releasing the mouse. On touch devices, nodes can be reordered using touch start, touch move, and touch end events.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.AllowEditing
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether node text can be edited by pressing the F2 key or double-clicking a node.
member.value: true if editing is allowed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When AllowEditing is set to true, the TreeView allows editing a node by double-clicking it or pressing the F2 key while the node is selected. When set to false, the TreeView allows the node text to be read-only.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.AllowMultiSelection
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether multi-selection of nodes is enabled in the component.
member.value: true if multi-selection is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When multi-selection is enabled, users can select multiple nodes in the component by holding down the CTRL key and clicking on the nodes they want to select. Consecutive nodes can be selected by holding down the SHIFT key and clicking on the initial and final nodes of the range to be selected. The property can also be used to enable checkbox support for node selection.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.AllowTextWrap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the text of nodes in the component is allowed to wrap to the next line when it exceeds the width of the node.
member.value: true if text wrapping is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When the AllowTextWrap property is set to true, the text of nodes in the component will wrap to the next line if its length exceeds the width of the node. This can be useful for displaying long or multi-line text in the tree view without truncating or clipping it.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.AutoCheck
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the checked state of parent nodes in the component is automatically updated based on the checked state of their child nodes.
member.value: true if the automatic update of parent node checked states is enabled; otherwise, false.
member.remarks: When the AutoCheck property is set to true, the checked state of parent nodes in the component will be automatically updated based on the checked state of their child nodes. This can be useful for maintaining the consistency of the tree view's checkbox hierarchy and ensuring that parent nodes are only checked if all of their child nodes are also checked. This property only works when the property is set to true.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.CheckedNodes
member.summary: Gets or sets the IDs of the nodes that are checked in the component.
member.value: A collection of strings containing the IDs of the nodes that are checked in the tree view.
member.remarks: The CheckedNodes property supports two-way binding in the component. By passing a collection of node IDs to this property, the checked state of the specified nodes can be set. The property can also be used to retrieve the IDs of the nodes that are currently checked in the tree view.

example.code:
<SfTreeView TValue="MusicAlbum" ShowCheckBox="true" @bind-CheckedNodes="@CheckedNodes">

                     HasChildren="HasChild" Expanded="Expanded" IsChecked="IsChecked">
                 </TreeViewFieldsSettings>
             </SfTreeView>

             }

                     Albums.Add(new MusicAlbum
                     {

             }
            
             <style>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.ExpandedNodes
member.summary: Gets or sets the IDs of expanded nodes in the component.
member.value: Pass the node's ID as a string array collection.
member.remarks: This property is used to track which nodes are currently expanded in the TreeView, allowing users to retain their expanded view even after the application is closed and reopened. This property supports two-way binding, ensuring that any changes to the expanded nodes in the TreeView will be reflected in the bound string array collection.
member.example:
<SfTreeView TValue="MusicAlbum" ShowCheckBox="true" @bind-ExpandedNodes="@ExpandedNodes">
                 <TreeViewFieldsSettings TValue="MusicAlbum" 
                     Id="Id" 
                     DataSource="@Albums" 
                     Text="Name" 
                     ParentID="ParentId" 
                     HasChildren="HasChild" 
                     Expanded="Expanded" 
                     IsChecked="IsChecked">
                 </TreeViewFieldsSettings>
             </SfTreeView>
            
             @code {
                 public class MusicAlbum
                 {
                     public int Id { get; set; }
                     public int? ParentId { get; set; }
                     public string Name { get; set; }
                     public bool Expanded { get; set; }
                     public bool? IsChecked { get; set; }
                     public bool HasChild { get; set; }
                 }
            
                 string[] ExpandedNodes = new string[] { "16", "18" };
            
                 List<MusicAlbum> Albums = new List<MusicAlbum>();
            
                 protected override void OnInitialized()
                 {
                     base.OnInitialized();
                     Albums.Add(new MusicAlbum
                     {
                         Id = 14,
                         HasChild = true,
                         Name = "MP3 Albums"
                     });
            
                     Albums.Add(new MusicAlbum
                     {
                         Id = 15,
                         ParentId = 14,
                         Name = "Rock"
                     });
                 }
             }
             
            
             In this example:
             - The `ExpandedNodes` property is bound to a string array containing the IDs of the expanded nodes.
             - The `MusicAlbum` class defines the data structure of each node in the tree.
             - The `Albums` list is populated with sample data in the `OnInitialized` method.
             - The  property is set to true to enable checkboxes for each node.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.LoadOnDemand

This improves the performance of the component on initial load by loading only parent nodes initially. If this property is set to false, all parent and child nodes are rendered on initial load, which may impact performance for large data sets.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.ShowCheckBox

member.value: Name of sort comparer object to be executed. The default value is null.
member.remarks: To define custom sorting logic, implement the comparer class using the [IComparer](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.icomparer-1?view=net-8.0) interface. This allows overriding the default sorting behavior of the component.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.SfTreeView`1.EnableVirtualization
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether virtualization is enabled in the component, which loads data on-demand through vertical scrolling.
member.value: true to enable virtualization in the TreeView; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, virtualization is enabled, and the TreeView will load only the nodes that are currently visible in the viewport, which can significantly improve the performance and responsiveness of the TreeView when dealing with large datasets. Subsequent nodes will be loaded dynamically as the user scrolls vertically through the TreeView. `Note:` - Virtualization is not compatible with expand and collapse animation. - The property of the TreeView must be set to use this virtualization feature. - The "Select All" action will only select visible items in the UI.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Navigations.TreeViewFieldOptions`1.Child
member.summary: Gets or sets the string value that represents the name of the child data source holding a list of objects.

example.code:
<SfTreeView TValue="MailItem" >
                <TreeViewFieldsSettings TValue="MailItem" Child="SubFolders" DataSource="@MyFolder" Text="FolderName"></TreeViewFieldsSettings>
            </SfTreeView>
            @code{ 
                public class MailItem
                {
                   public string FolderName { get; set; }
                   public List<MailItem> SubFolders { get; set; }
                }
                List<MailItem> MyFolder = new List<MailItem>();
                List<MailItem> Folder1 = new List<MailItem>();
                MyFolder.Add(new MailItem
                {
                    SubFolders = Folder1
                });

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageSeverity
member.summary: Specifies the type of severity to display the message with distinctive icons and colors in the component.
member.remarks: The enumeration provides predefined severity levels that control the visual appearance of messages. Each severity level is associated with specific icons, colors, and styling to effectively communicate the message context to users.
member.example:
Using different message severities in an component.
<SfMessage Severity="MessageSeverity.Success" Content="Operation completed successfully!" /> <SfMessage Severity="MessageSeverity.Error" Content="An error occurred during processing." /> <SfMessage Severity="MessageSeverity.Warning" Content="Please review the following items." />

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageSeverity.Normal
member.summary: The message is displayed with icons and colors for the normal severity level.
member.remarks: This is the default severity level that displays messages with neutral styling, typically used for general information or status updates.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageSeverity.Success
member.summary: The message is displayed with icons and colors for the success severity level.
member.remarks: This severity level is used to indicate successful operations or positive outcomes, typically displayed with green colors and success icons.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageSeverity.Info
member.summary: The message is displayed with icons and colors to denote it as informational content.
member.remarks: This severity level is used for providing information to users, typically displayed with blue colors and information icons.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageSeverity.Warning
member.summary: The message is displayed with icons and colors to denote it as a warning message.
member.remarks: This severity level is used to alert users about potential issues or important information that requires attention, typically displayed with orange/yellow colors and warning icons.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageSeverity.Error
member.summary: The message is displayed with icons and colors to denote it as an error message.
member.remarks: This severity level is used to indicate errors or critical issues that need immediate attention, typically displayed with red colors and error icons.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageVariant
member.summary: Specifies the predefined appearance variants for the component to control the visual presentation style.
member.remarks: The enumeration provides different styling options that work in conjunction with to create various visual presentations. Each variant offers a distinct way to display the severity-based colors and styling.
member.example:
Using different message variants with severity levels.
<SfMessage Severity="MessageSeverity.Success" Variant="MessageVariant.Filled" Content="Filled success message" /> <SfMessage Severity="MessageSeverity.Warning" Variant="MessageVariant.Outlined" Content="Outlined warning message" /> <SfMessage Severity="MessageSeverity.Info" Variant="MessageVariant.Text" Content="Text-only info message" />

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageVariant.Text
member.summary: The is differentiated using text color and light background colors.
member.remarks: This variant provides subtle styling with severity-based text colors and light background colors, offering a gentle visual distinction without being overpowering.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageVariant.Outlined
member.summary: The is differentiated using text color and border styling without background color.
member.remarks: This variant emphasizes the message through colored borders and text while maintaining a transparent background, providing clear visual separation without adding background weight.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageVariant.Filled
member.summary: The is differentiated using text color and dark background colors.
member.remarks: This variant provides the most prominent styling with bold, saturated background colors and contrasting text, making it highly visible and attention-grabbing.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageCloseEventArgs
member.summary: Provides information about the event.
member.remarks: This class contains event arguments that are passed when a message component is closed. It helps distinguish between automatic closures and user-initiated closures, which can be useful for tracking user interactions and implementing custom logic based on the closure method.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.MessageCloseEventArgs.IsInteracted
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the message close event was triggered by user interaction.
member.value: true if the event was triggered by user interaction such as clicking the close button or pressing the Escape key; otherwise, false for automatic closures such as timeout-based dismissals.
member.remarks: This property is essential for determining the cause of message closure. When true, it indicates that the user actively dismissed the message through direct interaction (clicking close button, pressing Escape key, etc.). When false, it indicates the message was closed automatically by the system (such as timeout expiration, programmatic closure, or other non-interactive triggers). This distinction helps in implementing different behaviors based on whether the closure was intentional user action or system-initiated.

member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS class or multiple classes separated by space that can be appended with the root element of the Message component to customize a message.
member.value: A string containing CSS class names separated by spaces. The default value is String.Empty.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfMessage.Severity
member.summary: Gets or sets the severity of the message, which is used to define the appearance (icons and colors) of the message. The available severity messages are Normal, Info, Success, Warning and Error.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is .
member.remarks: This property determines the visual styling and semantic meaning of the message by applying appropriate colors, icons, and styling based on the severity level. Each severity type conveys different levels of importance and context to the user, helping them understand the nature of the message at a glance.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfMessage.ShowCloseIcon
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to show or hide the close icon in the Message component. The end user can click the close icon to hide the message. The event triggered when message closed.
member.value: true if the close icon for the Message component is visible at the top right corner of the Message component; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When this property is set to true, a close icon appears in the top-right corner of the message, allowing users to dismiss the message by clicking on it. When the message is closed, the event is triggered, providing an opportunity to handle the close action programmatically.
member.example:
The below code example shows Message component with close icon enabled.

This message can be closed by clicking the close icon.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfMessage.ShowIcon
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to show or hide the severity icon in the Message component. When set to true, the severity icon is displayed at the left edge of the Message component. This icon will be distinctive based on the property.
member.value: true if the severity icon is displayed in the Message component; otherwise, false hides the severity icon. The default value is true.
member.remarks: This property controls the visibility of the severity icon that appears at the left edge of the message. The icon is automatically selected based on the property value, providing visual context for the message type. When set to false, only the text content and optional close icon are displayed.
member.example:
The below code example shows Message component with severity icon hidden.

This warning message displays without an icon.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfMessage.Variant
member.summary: Gets or sets the variant from predefined appearance variants to display the content of the Message component. The available variants are Text, Outlined and Filled.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is .

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton
member.summary: The Skeleton is a placeholder that animates a shimmer effect to let users know that the page's content is loading at the moment. In other terms, it simulates the layout of page content while loading the actual content.
member.remarks: The property will be prioritized and used as dimension for Circle and Square . The Skeleton component provides various shapes including text, rectangle, circle, and square placeholders. Different animation effects (wave, fade, pulse, or none) can be applied to enhance the loading experience. The component is fully accessible with ARIA label support for screen readers.
member.example:
Skeleton with default text shape.
<SfSkeleton Width="100%" Height="10px"></SfSkeleton>
Skeleton with rectangle .
<SfSkeleton Width="100px" Height="50px" Shape="SkeletonType.Rectangle"></SfSkeleton>
Skeleton with fade effect .
<SfSkeleton Width="50pt" Shape="SkeletonType.Circle" Effect="ShimmerEffect.Fade"></SfSkeleton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that defines the width of the Skeleton.
member.value: Accepts CSS units as string value (px, %, em, rem, etc.). The default value is null.
member.remarks: The property will be prioritized and used as dimension when is and . For these shapes, the value determines both width and height dimensions. If not specified for or shapes, defaults to "100%". Supports all standard CSS unit formats including pixels, percentages, and relative units.
member.example:
Skeleton with 50px radius applied for .
<SfSkeleton Width="50px" Shape="SkeletonType.Circle"></SfSkeleton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that defines the height of the Skeleton.
member.value: Accepts CSS units as string value (px, %, em, rem, etc.). The default value is null.
member.remarks: Not required to define this property when is and . For these shapes, the property value is used for both dimensions. This property is primarily used for and shapes. Supports all standard CSS unit formats including pixels, percentages, and relative units.
member.example:
Skeleton with 10px height applied for .
<SfSkeleton Width="100px" Height="10px"></SfSkeleton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.Visible
member.summary: Gets or sets the visibility state of the Skeleton.
member.value: true, if the Skeleton is in visible state; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When set to false, the Skeleton component will be hidden from view but still rendered in the DOM. This property is useful for conditionally showing or hiding the loading placeholder based on application state. The visibility is controlled through CSS classes that apply appropriate display properties.
member.example:
Skeleton rendered with hidden state.
<SfSkeleton Visible="false" Width="50px" Shape="SkeletonType.Square"></SfSkeleton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.Shape
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the shape of the Skeleton.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is .
member.remarks: If the is or , the property value will be prioritized and used as dimension for both width and height. For and shapes, both and properties are used for proper dimensioning. The shape determines the visual appearance and how the shimmer effect is applied to the placeholder.
member.example:
Skeleton with different shapes.
<SfSkeleton Shape="SkeletonType.Circle" Width="50px"></SfSkeleton> <SfSkeleton Shape="SkeletonType.Rectangle" Width="100px" Height="50px"></SfSkeleton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.Effect
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the animation effect of the Skeleton.
member.value: One of the enumeration. The default value is .
member.remarks: The animation effect provides visual feedback to users indicating that content is loading. creates a horizontal moving shimmer effect across the placeholder. creates a fading in and out animation effect. creates a pulsing animation that scales the placeholder. disables all animation effects for a static placeholder.
member.example:
Skeleton with fade effect.
<SfSkeleton Effect="ShimmerEffect.Fade" Width="50px" Shape="SkeletonType.Circle"></SfSkeleton>
Skeleton with pulse effect.
<SfSkeleton Effect="ShimmerEffect.Pulse" Width="50px" Shape="SkeletonType.Circle"></SfSkeleton>
Skeleton with no effect.
<SfSkeleton Effect="ShimmerEffect.None" Width="100px" Height="10px"></SfSkeleton>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.Label
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that defines 'aria-label' for Skeleton accessibility.
member.value: Accepts a string value. The default value is Loading....
member.remarks: This property improves accessibility by providing a meaningful label that screen readers can announce to users. When not explicitly set, the component will use a localized default value based on the current culture settings. The label helps assistive technologies understand that content is currently loading. This is particularly important for users who rely on screen readers to navigate web applications.
member.example:
Skeleton with custom ARIA label.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfSkeleton.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that indicates the CSS class string to customize the appearance of Skeleton.
member.value: Accepts a CSS class string separated by space to customize the appearance of Skeleton. The default value is string.Empty.
member.remarks: Multiple CSS classes can be applied by separating them with spaces. These classes are appended to the default Skeleton classes. Custom styles can be used to modify colors, animations, borders, and other visual aspects of the Skeleton component. The CSS classes should target the root element with the .e-skeleton class for proper styling override. Custom styling allows developers to match the skeleton's appearance with their application's design system.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SkeletonType.Rectangle

member.remarks: Creates a rectangular placeholder with custom dimensions. Both Width and Height properties are used for precise dimensioning.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ShimmerEffect
member.summary: Defines the animation effect of the Skeleton.
member.remarks: Animation effects provide visual feedback to users indicating that content is loading. Different effects can be chosen based on the desired user experience and design requirements.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ShimmerEffect.Wave

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationSettings
member.summary: Specifies the show and hide animation settings for the component.
member.remarks: The class allows you to configure custom animations for both showing and hiding toast notifications. You can specify different animation effects, durations, and easing functions to enhance the user experience when toasts appear or disappear. This component provides a declarative way to define animation behaviors through the and properties.

<SfToast> <ToastAnimationSettings> <ToastShowAnimationSettings Effect="ToastAnimationEffect.FadeIn" Duration="600" /> <ToastHideAnimationSettings Effect="ToastAnimationEffect.FadeOut" Duration="400" /> </ToastAnimationSettings> </SfToast>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationSettings.HideSettings

member.value: A instance that defines the animation properties for hiding the toast.

Common hide effects include FadeOut, SlideUp, SlideLeft, SlideRight, and ZoomOut animations.
member.example:
Setting custom hide animation settings:
<ToastAnimationSettings> <ToastHideAnimationSettings Effect="ToastAnimationEffect.SlideUp" Duration="500" /> </ToastAnimationSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationSettings.ShowSettings
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation settings applied when showing the toast notification.
member.value: A instance that defines the animation properties for showing the toast.
member.remarks: The property allows you to customize how the toast appears on screen. You can configure properties such as animation effect, duration, delay, and easing to create engaging show transitions. If not specified, default show animation settings will be applied automatically. Common show effects include FadeIn, SlideDown, SlideLeft, SlideRight, and ZoomIn animations. The show animation plays immediately when the toast is triggered to appear.
member.example:
Setting custom show animation settings:
<ToastAnimationSettings> <ToastShowAnimationSettings Effect="ToastAnimationEffect.SlideDown" Duration="600" /> </ToastAnimationSettings>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastHideAnimationSettings.Easing
member.summary: Gets or sets the easing function that controls the acceleration and deceleration of the hide animation.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies the timing function for the animation. The default value depends on the toast component's default settings.

This property works together with to create the desired animation experience.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastHideAnimationSettings.Effect
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation effect to be applied when hiding the toast notification.
member.value: A enumeration value that specifies the type of animation effect. The default value depends on the toast component's default settings.
member.remarks:
This property determines the visual style of the hide animation. When a toast is dismissed, the specified effect controls how the toast disappears from view. The available animation effects include:
Fade - Creates a fade-out effect where the toast gradually becomes transparent
FadeZoom - Combines fade and zoom effects for a more dynamic transition
FlipLeftDown - Rotates the toast down and to the left
FlipLeftUp - Rotates the toast up and to the left
FlipRightDown - Rotates the toast down and to the right
FlipRightUp - Rotates the toast up and to the right
FlipXDown - Flips the toast horizontally downward
FlipXUp - Flips the toast horizontally upward
FlipYLeft - Flips the toast vertically to the left
FlipYRight - Flips the toast vertically to the right
SlideBottom - Slides the toast toward the bottom of the screen
SlideLeft - Slides the toast toward the left side of the screen
SlideRight - Slides the toast toward the right side of the screen
SlideTop - Slides the toast toward the top of the screen
Zoom - Scales the toast down while hiding it
None - No animation effect is applied
The effect works in combination with and to create the complete animation experience.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastShowAnimationSettings.Effect
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation effect that should be applied when showing the toast notification.
member.value: A ToastEffect enumeration value that specifies the type of animation effect to use during the show animation.
member.remarks:
This property determines the visual style of the show animation. Each effect provides a different visual experience when the Toast appears on screen. The available animation effects include:
Fade - Simple fade-in transparency effect
FadeZoom - Combined fade and scaling effect
FlipLeftDown - 3D flip animation from left to down
FlipLeftUp - 3D flip animation from left to up
FlipRightDown - 3D flip animation from right to down
FlipRightUp - 3D flip animation from right to up
FlipXDown - Horizontal flip animation downward
FlipXUp - Horizontal flip animation upward
FlipYLeft - Vertical flip animation leftward
FlipYRight - Vertical flip animation rightward
SlideBottom - Slide animation from bottom
SlideLeft - Slide animation from left
SlideRight - Slide animation from right
SlideTop - Slide animation from top
Zoom - Scaling effect from center
None - No animation effect (immediate display)
The selected effect applies only to the show animation; hide animation effects are configured separately.

Setting different animation effects.
<!-- Fade effect --> <ToastShowAnimationSettings Effect="ToastEffect.Fade" Duration="400" />
<!-- Slide from right effect --> <ToastShowAnimationSettings Effect="ToastEffect.SlideRight" Duration="600" />

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.SlideRightOut
member.summary: Specifies a slide animation effect that moves the Toast notification toward the right edge out of view.
member.remarks: This effect makes the Toast notification disappear by sliding rightward toward the right edge of its container. It creates a smooth sliding exit animation that is commonly used for right-positioned notifications.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.SlideTopIn
member.summary: Specifies a slide animation effect that moves the Toast notification from the top edge into view.
member.remarks: This effect makes the Toast notification appear by sliding downward from the top edge of its container. It creates a smooth sliding entrance animation that is commonly used for top-positioned notifications.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.SlideTopOut
member.summary: Specifies a slide animation effect that moves the Toast notification toward the top edge out of view.
member.remarks: This effect makes the Toast notification disappear by sliding upward toward the top edge of its container. It creates a smooth sliding exit animation that is commonly used for top-positioned notifications.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.SlideUp
member.summary: Specifies a slide animation effect that moves the Toast notification upward.
member.remarks: This effect creates an upward sliding motion for the Toast notification. It can be used for both entrance and exit animations depending on the context and implementation.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.ZoomIn
member.summary: Specifies a zoom animation effect that scales the Toast notification from small to normal size during entrance.
member.remarks: This effect makes the Toast notification appear by scaling it from a smaller size to its normal size. It creates a smooth scaling entrance animation that draws attention to the notification.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.ZoomOut
member.summary: Specifies a zoom animation effect that scales the Toast notification from normal to small size during exit.
member.remarks: This effect makes the Toast notification disappear by scaling it from its normal size to a smaller size. It creates a smooth scaling exit animation that provides a clean disappearing effect.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastEffect.None
member.summary: Specifies no animation effect for the Toast notification.
member.remarks: This option disables all animation effects, causing the Toast notification to appear and disappear instantly without any transition. This is useful when immediate display is required or when performance is a concern and animations are not desired.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ProgressDirection
member.summary: Specifies the direction types for progress bar animations in Toast notifications.
member.remarks: This enumeration defines the direction in which the progress bar animation moves within Toast notifications. The direction affects how the progress indicator visually represents the remaining time before the Toast automatically closes.
member.example:
Configuring progress bar direction:
<SfToast ShowProgressBar="true"> <ToastAnimationSettings> <ToastProgressBarSettings Direction="ProgressDirection.LTR" /> </ToastAnimationSettings> </SfToast>

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ProgressDirection.RTL
member.summary: Specifies right-to-left (RTL) direction for the progress bar animation.
member.remarks: In RTL direction, the progress bar starts from the right side and moves toward the left as time progresses. This direction is typically used in right-to-left language environments or when the design requires the progress indicator to move from right to left.

member.name: F:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ProgressDirection.LTR
member.summary: Specifies left-to-right (LTR) direction for the progress bar animation.
member.remarks: In LTR direction, the progress bar starts from the left side and moves toward the right as time progresses. This is the default and most common direction, typically used in left-to-right language environments and standard UI designs where progress naturally flows from left to right.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeOpenArgs
member.summary: Specifies the event arguments for the Toast before open event.
member.remarks: This class provides data for the event that is raised before a Toast notification is displayed. It allows you to cancel the opening of the Toast or modify its options programmatically.

example.code:
<SfToast @ref="ToastRef">
                <ToastEvents TValue="ToastModel" OnOpen="@OnBeforeOpen"></ToastEvents>
            </SfToast>
            
            private void OnBeforeOpen(ToastBeforeOpenArgs args)
            {
                // Cancel opening based on some condition
                if (SomeCondition)
                {
                    args.Cancel = true;
                }
                
                // Modify toast options
                if (args.Options != null)
                {
                    args.Options.Content = "Modified content";
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeOpenArgs.Cancel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Toast opening should be cancelled.
member.value: true if the Toast should be prevented from opening; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Setting this property to true prevents the Toast from being displayed to the user. This is useful for implementing conditional logic where certain Toast notifications should not appear based on application state or user preferences.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeOpenArgs.Options
member.summary: Gets or sets the current Toast model properties as options.
member.value: An instance of representing the configuration options for the Toast notification. Can be null.
member.remarks: This property provides access to the Toast configuration that will be used when the Toast is displayed. You can modify these options programmatically before the Toast opens to customize its appearance, content, or behavior. Common modifications include changing the content, title, timeout duration, or CSS classes.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeCloseArgs
member.summary: Specifies the event arguments for the Toast before close event.
member.remarks: This class provides data for the event that is raised before a Toast notification is closed. It allows you to cancel the closing of the Toast, identify which Toast is being closed, and understand how the close action was triggered.

example.code:
<SfToast @ref="ToastRef">
                <ToastEvents TValue="ToastModel" BeforeClose="@OnBeforeClose"></ToastEvents>
            </SfToast>
            
            private void OnBeforeClose(ToastBeforeCloseArgs args)
            {
                // Prevent closing if user interaction is required
                if (args.RequestType == "User")
                {
                    args.Cancel = true;
                }
                
                // Log which toast is closing
                Console.WriteLine($"Toast with Key {args.Key} is closing");
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeCloseArgs.Cancel
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Toast closing should be cancelled.
member.value: true if the Toast should be prevented from closing; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Setting this property to true prevents the Toast from being closed and removed from the display. This is useful for implementing confirmation dialogs or preventing accidental closure of important notifications.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeCloseArgs.Key
member.summary: Gets or sets the unique identifier of the Toast being closed.
member.value: An integer value representing the unique key of the Toast notification. Each Toast is assigned a unique key when created.
member.remarks: The Key property helps identify which specific Toast notification is being closed when multiple Toast messages are displayed. This is particularly useful in scenarios where you need to track or perform specific actions based on which Toast is closing.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeCloseArgs.RequestType
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of request that triggered the Toast close action.
member.value: A string value indicating how the Toast close was initiated. Can be null.
member.remarks: This property provides information about what caused the Toast to close, such as user interaction, timeout expiration, or programmatic closure. Common values might include "User" for user-initiated closures, "Timeout" for automatic closures, or "Programmatic" for code-initiated closures. Understanding the request type helps in implementing different behaviors based on how the Toast was closed.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastBeforeCloseArgs.Options
member.summary: Gets or sets the current Toast model properties as options.
member.value: An instance of representing the configuration options for the Toast notification being closed. Can be null.
member.remarks: This property provides access to the complete configuration of the Toast that is being closed. You can use this information to log details about the Toast, perform cleanup operations, or make decisions about subsequent actions.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastClickEventArgs
member.summary: Specifies the event arguments for the Toast click event.
member.remarks: This class provides data for the event that is raised when a Toast notification is clicked or receives keyboard focus. It allows you to control the click behavior, prevent the default action, and determine whether the Toast should be closed on interaction.

example.code:
<SfToast @ref="ToastRef">
                <ToastEvents TValue="ToastModel" OnClick="@OnToastClick"></ToastEvents>
            </SfToast>
            
            private void OnToastClick(ToastClickEventArgs args)
            {
                // Prevent default click behavior
                args.Cancel = true;
                
                // Control whether Toast closes on click
                args.ClickToClose = false;
                
                // Custom action based on toast content
                if (args.Options?.Title == "Warning")
                {
                    // Handle warning toast click
                    ShowDetailedWarning();
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastClickEventArgs.Cancel

member.value: true if the click event should be prevented; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: Setting this property to true prevents the default click behavior from executing. This is useful when you want to implement custom click handling logic without triggering the Toast's built-in click responses.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastClickEventArgs.ClickToClose

member.value: true if the Toast should be closed when clicked or tabbed; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property controls the auto-close behavior of the Toast when user interacts with it through clicking or keyboard navigation. When set to true, the Toast will automatically close after the click event is processed. This is commonly used for acknowledgment-type notifications where user interaction indicates the message has been read.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastCloseArgs
member.summary: Specifies the event arguments for the Toast close event.
member.remarks: This class provides data for the event that is raised after a Toast notification has been closed and removed from display. It contains information about the closed Toast, including its configuration and unique identifier.

example.code:
<SfToast @ref="ToastRef">
                <ToastEvents TValue="ToastModel" Closed="@OnToastClosed"></ToastEvents>
            </SfToast>
            
            private void OnToastClosed(ToastCloseArgs args)
            {
                // Log the closed toast information
                Console.WriteLine($"Toast with Key {args.Key} has been closed");
                
                // Perform cleanup or follow-up actions
                if (args.Options?.Title == "Error")
                {
                    LogErrorDismissal();
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastCloseArgs.Options

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastOpenArgs
member.summary: Specifies the event arguments for the Toast open event.
member.remarks: This class provides data for the event that is raised after a Toast notification has been successfully opened and displayed to the user. It contains information about the opened Toast, including its configuration and unique identifier.

example.code:
<SfToast @ref="ToastRef">
                <ToastEvents TValue="ToastModel" Opened="@OnToastOpened"></ToastEvents>
            </SfToast>
            
            private void OnToastOpened(ToastOpenArgs args)
            {
                // Log when toast is displayed
                Console.WriteLine($"Toast with Key {args.Key} is now visible");
                
                // Start tracking or analytics
                if (args.Options?.Title == "Welcome")
                {
                    TrackWelcomeMessageShown();
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationSettingsModel.Hide

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationSettingsModel.Show
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation configuration to be applied while showing the Toast.
member.value: A instance that defines the show animation properties. Can be null.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationsModel
member.summary: Represents the animation configuration model for Toast notifications.
member.remarks: This class defines the specific animation properties including effect type, duration, and easing function. It provides fine-grained control over how Toast notifications appear and disappear with various visual effects.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationsModel.Duration
member.summary: Gets or sets the duration for the Toast animation in milliseconds.
member.value: An integer value representing the animation duration in milliseconds. The default value is typically 300ms.
member.remarks: This property controls how long the animation takes to complete. Shorter durations create quick transitions, while longer durations create more gradual, slower animations. Common values range from 200ms to 800ms.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationsModel.Easing
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation timing function for the Toast transition.
member.value: A enumeration value that determines the animation timing curve.
member.remarks: This property controls the acceleration and deceleration of the animation over time. Different easing functions create different visual feels, such as smooth, bouncy, or abrupt transitions. Common options include EaseIn, EaseOut, EaseInOut, and Linear.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastAnimationsModel.Effect
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation effect to be applied during Toast transitions.
member.value: A enumeration value representing the visual animation effect.
member.remarks:
This property specifies the type of visual transition effect for the Toast notification. When an effect like Fade is selected, the Toast will use FadeIn for showing and FadeOut for hiding. The available animation effects include:
Fade - Simple opacity transition
FadeZoom - Combines fading with scaling effect
FlipLeftDown, FlipLeftUp, FlipRightDown, FlipRightUp - 3D flip animations
FlipXDown, FlipXUp, FlipYLeft, FlipYRight - Axis-specific flip effects
SlideBottom, SlideLeft, SlideRight, SlideTop - Directional slide transitions
Zoom - Scaling effect without opacity change
None - No animation effect

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel
member.summary: Represents the configuration model for Toast notifications.
member.remarks: This class defines all the properties and settings that control the appearance, behavior, and content of Toast notifications. It provides comprehensive customization options including animation, positioning, timing, and visual styling.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Animation
member.summary: Gets or sets the animation configuration settings for showing and hiding the Toast.
member.value: A instance that defines the animation behavior. Can be null.
member.remarks: This property controls the visual transition effects when the Toast appears and disappears. You can configure separate animations for show and hide operations, including effect types, durations, and easing functions. If not specified, the Toast will use default animation settings.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Content
member.summary: Gets or sets the content to be displayed in the Toast notification.
member.value: A string representing the Toast content. Accepts plain text, HTML markup, CSS selectors, or element references. Can be null.
member.remarks: This property defines the main message or content that will be displayed in the Toast notification. It supports HTML markup for rich content formatting, and can reference DOM elements or CSS selectors. For complex content layouts, consider using the property instead.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.CssClass
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS classes for customizing the Toast appearance.
member.value: A string containing one or more CSS class names separated by spaces. Can be null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to apply custom styling to the Toast notification by specifying CSS classes. Multiple classes can be applied by separating them with spaces. These classes can be used to customize colors, fonts, borders, shadows, and other visual aspects of the Toast.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the component's state should persist between page reloads.
member.value: true if the component state should be persisted; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When enabled, the Toast component will save its current state (such as active Toast messages) to browser storage and restore it when the page is reloaded. This ensures continuity of Toast notifications across page refreshes.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.EnableRtl
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the Toast should be rendered in right-to-left direction.
member.value: true if the Toast should be rendered in RTL mode; otherwise, false. The default value is false.
member.remarks: This property enables right-to-left text direction and layout for the Toast component, which is essential for proper display of RTL languages like Arabic, Hebrew, or Persian. When enabled, text alignment, icon positioning, and progress bar direction are adjusted accordingly.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.ExtendedTimeout
member.summary: Gets or sets the extended timeout duration for Toast display after user interaction.
member.value: An integer value representing the extended timeout in milliseconds. The default value is 1000ms.
member.remarks: This property specifies how long the Toast should remain visible after the user interacts with it (hover, focus, etc.). When a user hovers over or focuses on a Toast, the normal timeout is paused, and this extended timeout is used instead. This ensures users have adequate time to read or interact with the Toast content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the Toast notification.
member.value: A string representing the height in pixels, percentage, or other CSS units. Can be null for auto height.
member.remarks:
This property controls the vertical size of the Toast notification. You can specify the height using:
Pixels: "200px"
Percentage: "50%"
Other CSS units: "2em", "10vh"
If not specified, the Toast will automatically size based on its content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Icon
member.summary: Gets or sets the CSS classes for the Toast icon.
member.value: A string containing CSS class names for the icon. Can be null for no icon.

Common icon libraries like Font Awesome, Material Icons, or Syncfusion's built-in icons can be used. Example values: "e-icons e-success", "fas fa-check", "material-icons check_circle".

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.NewestOnTop
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether newly created Toast messages should appear on top of existing ones.
member.value: true if new Toast messages should appear on top; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: This property controls the stacking order of multiple Toast notifications. When set to true, new Toast messages are displayed above existing ones. When set to false, new messages appear below existing ones. This affects the visual hierarchy and user attention flow when multiple Toast notifications are active.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Position

member.value: A instance specifying the X and Y coordinates. Can be null for default positioning.

X values: "Left", "Right", "Center"

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.ProgressDirection

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.ShowCloseButton

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.ShowProgressBar

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Target

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.ContentTemplate

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Timeout

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Title

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastModel.Width

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.ToastPositionModel

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.Internal.ToastContent

member.remarks: The class represents the internal content renderer for toast notifications in the Blazor Toast component. It handles the rendering, positioning, timing, and lifecycle management of individual toast messages including progress bars, close buttons, icons, and animation effects. This class manages the display duration, user interactions, and automatic dismissal of toast notifications.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.Internal.ToastContent.OnInitialized

Registers script modules and handles static rendering scenarios

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.GetInstance
member.summary: Creates and returns a dictionary containing the Toast component instance data required for JavaScript interop initialization.
member.returns: A Dictionary<string, object> containing all necessary component configuration data for client-side initialization.

item.description: Component identification (dataId, ID)
.NET object reference for callbacks
Target element and DOM element references
Display behavior settings (NewestOnTop)
Animation configurations for show and hide operations

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.CheckAnimation(System.Object,System.String)
member.summary: Validates and resolves the appropriate animation effect based on component settings and global animation configuration.
member.param: The dynamic animation settings object containing effect configuration.
The fallback animation type to use when no specific effect is defined.
member.returns: A string representing the resolved animation effect name, or "None" if animations are globally disabled.

remarks.para: This method implements the animation resolution logic that respects both component-level and global animation settings:

item.description: When global animation is Default or Enable: Uses the component's specified effect if available
When global animation is Disable: Always returns "None" regardless of component settings
When component effect is "None" but global animation is Enable: Uses the fallback animationType
Falls back to the provided animationType when no specific effect is configured

remarks.para: This ensures consistent animation behavior across the application while respecting user preferences and accessibility requirements.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.GetShowAnimation
member.summary: Creates and returns a dictionary containing the show animation configuration for the Toast component.
member.returns: A Dictionary<string, object> containing the complete show animation settings including effect, duration, and easing.

remarks.para: This method constructs the show animation configuration that will be used when displaying the Toast notification. The configuration includes:

item.description: Effect: Resolved using CheckAnimation with FADE_IN as the default fallback
Duration: Uses the configured duration or falls back to DEFAULT_ANIMATION_TIME
Easing: Uses the configured easing function or defaults to EASE

remarks.para: The returned dictionary is formatted for direct consumption by the JavaScript animation engine, ensuring smooth integration between the .NET configuration and client-side animation execution.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.GetHideAnimation
member.summary: Creates and returns a dictionary containing the hide animation configuration for the Toast component.
member.returns: A Dictionary<string, object> containing the complete hide animation settings including effect, duration, and easing.

remarks.para: This method constructs the hide animation configuration that will be used when dismissing the Toast notification. The configuration includes:

item.description: Effect: Resolved using CheckAnimation with FADE_OUT as the default fallback
Duration: Uses the configured duration or falls back to DEFAULT_ANIMATION_TIME
Easing: Uses the configured easing function or defaults to EASE

remarks.para: The returned dictionary is formatted for direct consumption by the JavaScript animation engine, ensuring smooth integration between the .NET configuration and client-side animation execution. Note: The duration logic includes redundant checks which may be addressed in future optimizations.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.ComponentDispose
member.summary: Performs comprehensive cleanup of the Toast component, releasing all resources and disposing of client-side instances.

remarks.para: This method handles the complete disposal process for the Toast component, including:

item.description: Invoking JavaScript destroy method to clean up client-side resources
Triggering Destroyed event delegates if configured
Clearing and nullifying all collection properties (ShowModels, ProgressObj, TimeoutTimer, etc.)
Resetting template references and component identifiers
Disposing ElementReference instances
Clearing delegate references to prevent memory leaks

remarks.para: The method includes comprehensive exception handling for common disposal scenarios:

item.description: ObjectDisposedException: When the component has already been disposed
TaskCanceledException: When async operations are cancelled during disposal
InvalidOperationException: When operations are performed on an invalid component state

remarks.para: All caught exceptions are passed to the Destroyed event delegate if available, allowing consumers to handle disposal errors appropriately. The method concludes by disposing the window instance to ensure complete cleanup of JavaScript resources.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.EnableRtl

The RTL mode also influences the placement of icons, close buttons, and action buttons within the toast layout.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.ExtendedTimeout
member.summary: Gets or sets the Toast display time duration after interacting with the Toast.
member.value: An int value representing the extended timeout duration in milliseconds. The default value is 1000.
member.remarks: This property defines how long the toast remains visible after user interaction (such as hovering or focusing). When a user interacts with the toast, the normal timeout is extended by this duration, allowing users more time to read or interact with the toast content. This enhances accessibility and user experience by preventing premature dismissal during user engagement. Setting this to 0 disables the extended timeout behavior. The interaction events that trigger this extension include mouse hover, keyboard focus, and touch interactions.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.Height
member.summary: Gets or sets the height of the Toast in pixels/number/percentage. Number value is considered as pixels.
member.value: A string value representing the height. The default value is "auto".

The height can be specified in various units:
Pixels: "100px" or "100" (numeric value treated as pixels)
Percentage: "50%" (relative to the container height)
Auto: "auto" (automatically adjusts based on content size)
When set to "auto", the toast height will be determined by its content size, providing optimal space utilization. Fixed heights may cause content overflow if insufficient space is provided.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.Icon
member.summary: Gets or sets CSS classes to specify an icon for the Toast which is to be displayed at top left corner of the Toast.
member.value: A string containing CSS icon class names. The default value is null.
member.remarks:
The icon is displayed at the top-left corner of the toast and helps users quickly identify the type of notification. You can use icon fonts like Font Awesome, Material Icons, or Syncfusion's built-in icon library. Common built-in Syncfusion icon classes include:
"e-success" for success messages
"e-error" for error messages
"e-warning" for warning messages
"e-info" for information messages
When null, no icon is displayed, providing more space for the content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.NewestOnTop
member.summary: Gets or sets a value that specifies the newly created Toast message display order while multiple toasts are added to page one after another.
member.value: true if new toasts should be displayed on top of existing toasts; otherwise, false. The default value is true.
member.remarks: When set to true, newer toast notifications will appear above existing ones, creating a stack where the most recent toast is most visible to users. When set to false, new toasts will be added below existing ones, maintaining chronological order from top to bottom. This property is particularly useful when managing multiple simultaneous notifications and determining which messages should receive priority in user attention. The stacking behavior affects the visual z-index ordering and animation sequence of multiple toasts.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.ProgressDirection
member.summary: Gets or sets the direction for the Toast progress bar.

This property controls the direction in which the progress bar fills as the toast timeout progresses. The progress bar provides visual feedback to users about how much time remains before the toast automatically disappears. Available options include:
- Progress fills from right to left
- Progress fills from left to right
This property only takes effect when is set to true. The direction may be automatically adjusted based on the setting for proper localization.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.ShowCloseButton

member.value: true if the close button should be shown; otherwise, false. The default value is false.

This improves user control and accessibility by providing an explicit way to dismiss notifications. The close button appearance can be customized using CSS styling. The close button supports keyboard navigation and screen reader accessibility. When clicked, it triggers the close event before removing the toast from the DOM.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.ShowProgressBar

The progress bar direction is controlled by the property. This feature helps users understand how much time they have to read or interact with the notification, improving the overall user experience by providing clear visual feedback about the toast's lifecycle. The progress bar animation smoothly decreases as the timeout approaches, and pauses during user interactions when is configured.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.Target
member.summary: Gets or sets the target container where the Toast to be displayed. Based on the target, the positions such as `Left`, `Top` will be applied to the Toast.
member.value: A string representing the CSS selector or element ID of the target container. The default value is null.
member.remarks: When null or not specified, the toast will be positioned relative to the document body, allowing full-page positioning. When a specific target is provided (e.g., "#myContainer" or ".toast-container"), the toast will be positioned relative to that element's boundaries. This is useful for constraining toasts to specific areas of the page or creating context-specific notifications within particular sections of the UI. The target element must have CSS positioning (relative, absolute, or fixed) for proper toast positioning. Supported selector formats include element IDs (#elementId), class names (.className), and element tags (div).

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.ContentTemplate
member.summary: Gets or sets the HTML template that can be displayed as Toast content.

The template provides significantly more flexibility than the simple string-based property, enabling interactive elements and dynamic content rendering. When both and are provided, the template takes precedence and the string content is ignored. member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.Timeout
member.summary: Gets or sets the Toast display time duration on the page in milliseconds. Once the time expires, Toast message will be removed. Setting 0 as a timeout value displays the Toast on the page until the user closes it manually.
member.value: An int value representing the timeout duration in milliseconds. The default value is 5000.
member.remarks:
This property controls how long the toast remains visible before automatically disappearing. Common timeout values and their use cases:
0 - Toast persists until manually closed (useful for critical messages)
3000 - 3 seconds (good for simple success/confirmation messages)
5000 - 5 seconds (default, suitable for most informational content)
10000 - 10 seconds (for longer messages requiring more reading time)
The timeout can be extended when users interact with the toast, based on the property. During user interactions (hover, focus), the timeout timer is paused and resumes after the interaction ends.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.Title

When null or empty, no title section is rendered in the toast, providing more space for the main content. The title supports plain text only and does not render HTML markup. For complex title formatting, consider using custom CSS classes via the property.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Notifications.SfToast.Width

The responsive behavior can be customized using CSS media queries in conjunction with the property.

member.remarks: This method displays a Toast notification on the screen with the specified or default configuration. When a is provided, the Toast will be displayed with the properties defined in that model. If no model is provided (null), the Toast will use the default configuration settings. The Toast will appear with the configured animation effects and will trigger the appropriate show events. The position of the Toast is determined by the relative positioning settings configured in the component or model.

example.code:
<SfToast @ref="toastObj">
                <ToastPosition X="Right" Y="Top"></ToastPosition>
            </SfToast>
