example.para: A simple Query Builder component.
example.code:
<SfQueryBuilder TValue="EmployeeData" @ref="QueryBuilderObj">
                 <QueryBuilderColumns>
                     <QueryBuilderColumn Field="EmployeeID" Label="Employee ID" Type="ColumnType.Number"></QueryBuilderColumn>
                     <QueryBuilderColumn Field="FirstName" Label="First Name" Type="ColumnType.String"></QueryBuilderColumn>
                     <QueryBuilderColumn Field="City" Label="City" Type="ColumnType.String"></QueryBuilderColumn>
                 </QueryBuilderColumns>
             </SfQueryBuilder>
            
             @code {
                 SfQueryBuilder<EmployeeData> QueryBuilderObj;
            
                 public class EmployeeData
                 {
                     public int EmployeeID { get; set; }
                     public string FirstName { get; set; }
                     public string City { get; set; }
                 }
             }

member.summary: The Query Builder is a graphical user interface that allows users to create and edit conditions for filtering data.
member.remarks: The component provides an intuitive way to build complex queries by adding, grouping, and deleting conditions. It supports various data types and operators, enabling users to filter data from a data source. Key features include data binding, customizable columns, and template support for custom UI.
member.summary: The Query Builder is a graphical user interface that allows users to create and edit complex data filters by combining multiple conditions.
member.remarks: The component provides an intuitive way to construct and manage filter queries, which can be applied to data grids, charts, or other data-bound components.
member.summary: A graphical user interface that is used for filtering large amounts of data by creating or editing conditions.

member.remarks: The allows you to define properties for each column, such as its data type, display label, format, and custom templates. These columns are then used to construct rules and conditions in the Query Builder.
member.example:
The following example demonstrates how to define columns in a .
<SfQueryBuilder> <QueryBuilderColumns> <QueryBuilderColumn Field="EmployeeID" Label="Employee ID" Type="ColumnType.Number"></QueryBuilderColumn> <QueryBuilderColumn Field="FirstName" Label="First Name" Type="ColumnType.String"></QueryBuilderColumn> </QueryBuilderColumns> </SfQueryBuilder>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.QueryBuilderColumn.ChildContent

member.value: A representing the child content. The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property is used to define nested components that provide additional configuration for the column.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.QueryBuilderColumn.Category
member.summary: Gets or sets the category for the column, which helps in grouping columns in the UI.
member.value: A string that specifies the category name. The default value is "OtherFields".
member.remarks: Columns with the same category will be grouped together in the field selection dropdown, improving usability.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.QueryBuilderColumn.Field
member.summary: Gets or sets the data field name that this column is bound to.
member.value: A string representing the field name from the data source.
member.remarks: This property is mandatory and must match a field in the data source for the Query Builder to function correctly.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.QueryBuilderColumn.Format

member.value: A string that specifies the format. The default value is null.
member.remarks: For date columns, you can use standard date format strings (e.g., "d", "M"). For numeric columns, you can use standard numeric format strings (e.g., "n2", "c").

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.QueryBuilderColumn.Label

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.QueryBuilderTemplates

<SfQueryBuilder TValue="Employee" Rule="rule"> <QueryBuilderColumns> <QueryBuilderColumn Field="EmployeeID" Label="Employee ID" Type="ColumnType.Number" /> <QueryBuilderColumn Field="FirstName" Label="First Name" Type="ColumnType.String" /> <QueryBuilderColumn Field="LastName" Label="Last Name" Type="ColumnType.String"> <QueryBuilderTemplates> <ValueTemplate Context="rule"> @{ var templateRule = rule as RuleModel; <SfTextBox @bind-Value="@templateRule.Value"></SfTextBox> } </ValueTemplate> </QueryBuilderTemplates> </QueryBuilderColumn> </QueryBuilderColumns> </SfQueryBuilder>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.ParameterSql
member.summary: Represents a parameterized SQL query, encapsulating both the SQL command and its associated parameters.
member.remarks: This class plays a crucial role in preventing SQL injection attacks by separating the SQL logic from the data. Implementations should ensure that user-provided values are passed as parameters rather than being concatenated directly into the SQL string. This is achieved by using the property for the query string with placeholders and the property for the corresponding values.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.ParameterSql.Sql
member.summary: Gets or sets the SQL statement, which may contain parameter placeholders.
member.value: A string representing the SQL query. The default is null.
member.remarks: The format of parameter placeholders (e.g., ? for positional or @name for named) depends on the specific database provider being used. An example with named parameters: "SELECT * FROM products WHERE ProductID = @ID".

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.QueryBuilder.ParameterSql.Params
member.summary: Gets or sets an array of parameter values that correspond to the placeholders in the query string.
member.value: An array of objects (object[]) containing the parameter values. The default is null.
member.remarks: For positional placeholders, the order of values in this array must match the order of the placeholders in the string. For named parameters, the mapping is typically handled by the database provider, but the order should still be maintained for clarity.

member.value: A collection of contextual tabs in the . The default value is an empty collection.
member.remarks: This property allows you to define and manage contextual tabs in the ribbon control, enabling users to interact with specific tabs based on certain actions or conditions. Contextual tabs are designed to appear only when they are relevant to the current task, enhancing the user experience by reducing clutter and providing context-sensitive options. You can include both built-in and custom ribbon items in these tabs, similar to standard ribbon tabs, offering a consistent and flexible design.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.RibbonFileMenuSettings
member.summary: Gets or sets the settings for the File Menu of the .
member.value: The settings for the File Menu of the . The default value is null.
member.remarks: This property allows you to customize the appearance and behavior of the File Menu in the ribbon control. You can use this property to define items such as "New," "Open," "Save," and other menu commands that are typically found in a file menu.
member.example:
Ribbon component with filemenu enabled.
<SfRibbon ID="default"> <ChildContent> <RibbonFileMenuSettings Visible=true MenuItems="@fileMenuItems"></RibbonFileMenuSettings> <RibbonTabs> <RibbonTab Header="Home"> <RibbonGroups> <RibbonGroup HeaderText="Clip"> <RibbonCollections> <RibbonCollection> <RibbonItems> <RibbonItem Type=RibbonItemType.Button> <RibbonButtonSettings Content="Copy" IconCss="e-icons e-copy"></RibbonButtonSettings> </RibbonItem> </RibbonItems> </RibbonCollection> </RibbonCollections> </RibbonGroup> </RibbonGroups> </RibbonTab> </RibbonTabs> </ChildContent> </SfRibbon> @code { List<MenuItem> fileMenuItems = new List<MenuItem>() { new MenuItem { Text = "New", IconCss = "e-icons e-file-new", Id = "new" }, new MenuItem { Text = "Open", IconCss = "e-icons e-folder-open", Id = "open" }, new MenuItem { Text = "Rename", IconCss = "e-icons e-rename", Id = "rename" }, }; }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.SfRibbon.EnablePersistence
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the state of the modes and built-in items are persisted.
member.value: A boolean value that determines whether the current state of the is persisted. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, the will save its current state of (built-in items and ribbon modes) and restore it when the application is restarted. This feature is useful for maintaining a consistent user experience across sessions. If set to false, the ribbon will not persist its state between application sessions and will reset to its default configuration upon startup.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.SfRibbon.Width
member.summary: Gets or sets the width of the .
member.value: The width of the . The default value is "100%".
member.remarks: This property specifies the width of the component. You can set this property to a specific pixel value (e.g., "800px") or a percentage value (e.g., "100%") to control the width of the Ribbon relative to its container. A value of "100%" makes the Ribbon occupy the full width of its parent container, adapting to the container's width.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.SfRibbon.HideLayoutSwitcher
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the layout switcher button of the is hidden.
member.value: A boolean value that determines whether the layout switcher button of the is hidden. The default value is false, means the button is visible by default.
member.remarks: This property controls the visibility of the layout switcher button, which allows users to toggle between different Ribbon layout styles. When set to true, the button is hidden, preventing users from changing the Ribbon layout. When set to false, the button is visible and allows users to switch between available layout options.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.SfRibbon.IsMinimized
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether the is minimized.
member.value: A boolean value that determines whether the is minimized. The default value is false.
member.remarks: When set to true, the component is minimized, typically hiding its content to provide more screen space for other parts of the application. When set to false, the is fully visible, displaying all of its tabs and content. This is the default state where the Ribbon is fully expanded and accessible to the user.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.SfRibbon.EnableKeyTips
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to enable the key tips for the component.
member.value: A boolean value that specifies whether key tips are enabled. Defaults to false.
member.remarks: When set to true, key tips are displayed when the user presses the "Alt" + "Windows/Command" key combination. Key tips provide a way for users to quickly navigate and access Ribbon items such as tabs, menus (including file and backstage menus), and buttons using keyboard shortcuts. If the same keytip is assigned to multiple Ribbon elements (such as buttons or tabs), the keytip for the first element in the Ribbon's visual hierarchy will be prioritized and triggered when the user presses the assigned keyboard shortcut. This behavior ensures that the most accessible or first defined item responds to the keytip, preventing ambiguity or conflicts when users interact with the Ribbon. Enabling key tips improves the usability of the by providing an efficient method of navigation for users who prefer using the keyboard.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Ribbon.SfRibbon.LayoutSwitcherKeyTip
member.summary: Gets or sets the key tip text for the layout switcher icon in the component.
member.value: A string representing the key tip text for the layout switcher icon. Defaults to an empty string.
member.remarks: The LayoutSwitcherKeyTip property allows you to assign a key tip to the layout switcher icon which facilitates quick keyboard access to the layout switcher through shortcuts.

member.summary: Gets or sets the color picker default rendering palette or picker mode.
member.value: A value from the enumeration. The default value is
member.remarks:
This property controls how the color picker popup is displayed:
If the value is ColorPickerMode.Palette, the color picker will be displayed as a color palette, allowing users to select colors from a predefined set of colors.
If the value is ColorPickerMode.Picker, the color picker will be displayed as a color selection panel, where users can interactively select a color using a more customizable interface (e.g., RGB, HSL sliders, etc.).
This setting provides flexibility for the user interface, allowing developers to choose the most suitable mode based on their application's design and user experience needs.

member.remarks: When set to true, the color picker will display a button that enables the user to switch between different display modes (such as a palette and picker). When set to false, the display mode switcher is hidden or inactive, and the user cannot change the mode interactively.

member.value: A indicating if the recent colors are displayed. The default value is .

</SfRichTextEditor> <SfRichTextEditor> <RichTextEditorBackgroundColor ShowRecentColors = "true" /> <RichTextEditorFontColor ShowRecentColors =" true" /> </SfRichTextEditor >

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.RichTextEditorImportWord
member.summary: A class used for configuring the import of Word documents into the . This class enables the integration of Word document content within the Rich Text Editor.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.RichTextEditorImportWord.ServiceUrl
member.summary: Gets or sets the service URL for uploading a document to the server, which will then be imported into the Rich Text Editor.
member.value: The service URL as a for uploading documents to the server. The default value is String.Empty.
member.remarks: The ServiceUrl should point to a server endpoint capable of processing Word document uploads intended for import. This setup ensures that Word documents can be seamlessly integrated into the Rich Text Editor interface.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.RichTextEditorImportWord.MaxFileSize
member.summary: Gets or sets the maximum allowed file size, in bytes, for Word documents imported in the component.
member.value: A representing the maximum permitted file size, in bytes. The default value is 30000000 (30 MB).
member.remarks: This property restricts the size of Word documents that users can import via the dialog and uploader UI built into the . Files exceeding this size limit will be automatically rejected and an error message will be displayed to the user. Typical usage is to prevent performance or memory issues in client and server processing. To allow larger documents, increase the value of this property as needed. To enforce a stricter size limit, set a lower value (minimum is 0). Negative values are not permitted and will be treated as 0.

example.code: <SfRichTextEditor> <RichTextEditorImportWord MaxFileSize="10485760" /> </SfRichTextEditor>

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.FormatPainterAction
member.summary: Defines the actions supported by the Format Painter in the .
member.remarks: These actions specify the behavior for copying, applying, and canceling formatting in the . They help ensure consistent formatting operations within the editor's content.

example.code:
<SfRichTextEditor>
            <RichTextEditorFormatPainterSettings>
            var options = new FormatPainterParams
            {
            Action = FormatPainterAction.CopyFormat,
            Options = new FormatPainterOptions
            {
            AllowedFormats = "b; em; strong",
            DeniedFormats = "img; a",
            }
            };
            </RichTextEditorFormatPainterSettings>
            </SfRichTextEditor>

This property indicates how the image was added to the editor. The value can be one of the following:
- The image was uploaded through the editor's interface.
- The image was dragged and dropped into the editor.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.FormatPainterOptions
member.summary: Provides configuration options for the Format Painter feature.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.FormatPainterOptions.AllowedFormats
member.summary: Specifies the element selectors from which formats can be copied.
member.value: A string of allowed format selectors, defaulting to a comprehensive list of HTML tags and attributes.
member.remarks: The AllowedFormats property defines a semicolon-separated string of HTML element selectors (e.g., b, i, span) from which the Format Painter copies formatting. This includes common formatting tags, structural elements, and inline styles or attributes such as style or class. Wildcards (e.g., (*)[*]{*}) allow matching all elements with specific attributes. Customizing this property ensures consistent formatting behavior by restricting the feature to specified elements. Only valid HTML selectors should be used to avoid runtime errors. Example: "b; i; span[style]" restricts formatting to bold, italic, and styled span elements.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.RichTextEditor.FormatPainterOptions.DeniedFormats
member.summary: Specifies the element selectors from which formats cannot be copied.
member.value: A string of denied format selectors, defaulting to null (no restrictions).
member.remarks: The DeniedFormats property specifies a semicolon-separated list of HTML element selectors (e.g., b, i, span) that the Format Painter must exclude from copying. This includes elements with inline styles or attributes like class. By default, this property is null, meaning no restrictions are applied. Wildcards such as (*)[*]{*} may be used to target elements with specific attributes. Only valid HTML selectors should be included to prevent runtime errors. Example: "b; i" blocks bold and italic formatting from being copied.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Sankey.SankeyLegendMargin
member.summary: Gets or sets the options for customizing the bottom, left, right, top margin of the legend in the Sankey Chart.
member.value: Accepts the instance of the class. The default value is 0 for top, bottom, left, and right.
member.remarks: Use this class to customize the margin of the legend in the SankeyChart to enhance the visual appearance.

example.code:
<SfSankey Width="600px" Height="400px" Nodes=@Nodes Links=@Links Title="Device Usage" SubTitle="-2023">
                <SankeyLegendSettings Visible="true" Position="SankeyLegendPosition.Bottom" Height="10" Width="10">
                    <SankeyLegendMargin Left="10" Right="10" Top="10" Bottom="10"> </SankeyLegendMargin>
                    <SankeyLegendTextStyle FontSize="10px" FontFamily="Roboto" FontWeight="600" Color="Black" FontStyle="italic">
                    </SankeyLegendTextStyle>
                    <SankeyLegendTitleStyle FontSize="14px" FontFamily="Roboto" FontWeight="800" Color="Black" FontStyle="italic">
                    </SankeyLegendTitleStyle>
                </SankeyLegendSettings>
            </SfSankey>
            @code {
            
                public List<SankeyDataNode> Nodes = new List<SankeyDataNode>();
                public List<SankeyDataLink> Links = new List<SankeyDataLink>();
            
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    base.OnInitialized();
                    Nodes = new List<SankeyDataNode>()
                    {
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "Female", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "Female (58%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "Male", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "Male (42%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "Tablet", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "Tablet (12%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "Mobile", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "Mobile (40%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "Desktop", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "Desktop (48%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "< 18", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "< 18 years (8%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "18-26", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "18-26 years (35%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "27-40", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "27-40 years (38%)" } },
                        new SankeyDataNode() { Id = "> 40", Label = new SankeyDataLabel() { Text = "> 40 years (19%)" } }
                    };
                    Links = new List<SankeyDataLink>()
                    {
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Female", TargetId = "Tablet", Value = 12 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Female", TargetId = "Mobile", Value = 14 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Female", TargetId = "Desktop", Value = 32 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Male", TargetId = "Mobile", Value = 26 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Male", TargetId = "Desktop", Value = 16 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Tablet", TargetId = "< 18", Value = 4 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Tablet", TargetId = "> 40", Value = 8 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Mobile", TargetId = "< 18", Value = 4 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Mobile", TargetId = "18-26", Value = 24 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Mobile", TargetId = "27-40", Value = 10 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Mobile", TargetId = "> 40", Value = 2 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Desktop", TargetId = "18-26", Value = 11 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Desktop", TargetId = "27-40", Value = 28 },
                        new SankeyDataLink() { SourceId = "Desktop", TargetId = "> 40", Value = 9 }
                    };
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Sankey.SankeyLegendSettings.Position
member.summary: Gets or sets the position of the legend in the .
member.value:
One of the enumerations that specifies the position of the legend. Options include:
: Places the legend based on the width and height of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the top of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the left of the chart.
: Displays the legend at the bottom of the chart.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Sankey.SankeyTooltipSettings.NodeFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the format for the node tooltip content.
member.value: A string that defines the format for the tooltip content. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks:
The property allows customization of the node tooltip content. By default, the tooltip displays information for the name and value of a node. Additional information can be included in the tooltip using a format string.
For example, the format "{name} : {value}" displays the name and value of the node in the tooltip.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Sankey.SankeyTooltipSettings.LinkFormat
member.summary: Gets or sets the format for the link tooltip content.
member.value: A string that defines the format for the tooltip content. The default value is an empty string.
member.remarks:
The property allows customization of the link tooltip content. By default, the tooltip displays information for the start and destination name and values of a link. Additional information can be included in the tooltip using a format string.
For example, the format "{source} {source-value} : {target} {target-value}" displays the start and destination name and values of the link in the tooltip.

It's recommended to use clear and concise titles that summarize the main purpose or focus of the sankey chart. Adding a title can significantly enhance the overall readability and understanding of the sankey chart, especially in scenarios with complex or diverse data sets.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.Sankey.SfSankey.PrintAsync(Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ElementReference)
member.summary: Asynchronously prints the specified element referenced by the optional parameter. If no element reference is provided, the chart will print.
member.param: Optional reference to the element to be printed. If not provided, the chart is printed.
member.returns: A task representing the asynchronous printing operation.

example.code:
<SfSankeyChart @ref="sankeychartObj" Width="600px" Height="400px" DataSource="@SankeyData">
                <SankeyChartNodes Width="30" Alignment="SankeyNodeAlign.Left" OffsetX="10" OffsetY="10" Padding="10">
                </SankeyChartNodes>
                <SankeyChartLinks Color="blue" ColorType="ColorType.Static" HighlightOpacity="1" InactiveOpacity="0.3" Opacity="0.7"> </SankeyChartLinks>
            </SfSankeyChart>
            <button @onclick="PrintSankeyChart">PrintSankeyChart</button>
            @code {
               SfSankeyChart sankeychartObj;
            
                public SankeyChartData SankeyData = new SankeyChartData()
                {
                    Nodes = new List<SankeyChartDataNode>(),
                    Links = new List<SankeyChartDataLink>()
                };}
                public async Task PrintSankeyChart()
                {
                   await sankeychartObj.PrintAsync();
                }
            
                protected override void OnInitialized()
                {
                    base.OnInitialized();
                    SankeyData.Nodes = new List<SankeyChartDataNode>()
                    {
                        new SankeyChartDataNode() { Id = "Female", Label = new SankeyChartDataLabel() { Text = "Female (58%)" } },
                        new SankeyChartDataNode() { Id = "Male", Label = new SankeyChartDataLabel() { Text = "Male (42%)" } },
                        new SankeyChartDataNode() { Id = "Tablet", Label = new SankeyChartDataLabel() { Text = "Tablet (12%)" } },
                        new SankeyChartDataNode() { Id = "Mobile", Label = new SankeyChartDataLabel() { Text = "Mobile (40%)" } },

                        new SankeyChartDataNode() { Id = "> 40", Label = new SankeyChartDataLabel() { Text = "> 40 years (19%)" } }
                    };
                    SankeyData.Links = new List<SankeyChartDataLink>()
                    {
                        new SankeyChartDataLink() { SourceId = "Female", TargetId = "Tablet", Value = 12 },

                List<AppointmentData> DataSource = new List<AppointmentData>

                };
                public class AppointmentData
                {
                    public int Id { get; set; }
                    public string Subject { get; set; }
                    public DateTime StartTime { get; set; }
                    public DateTime EndTime { get; set; }
                    public string Notes { get; set; }
                }
            }

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleGroup
member.summary: A class that represents the resource grouping related configurations on component.
member.remarks: You can configure the resource grouping by specifying values for the corresponding properties.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleGroup.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content of schedule group.
member.value: The value used to build the content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleGroup.AllowGroupEdit
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the group editing is enabled in the scheduler.
member.value: Set to `true` to treat multiple resources as a single appointment object in the scheduler's dataSource. The default value is `false`
member.remarks: Group editing is performed on multiple resources based on the value on appointments. It is mandatory to group the resources as an array type and map them to the appointment data's resource field.

example.code:
<SfSchedule TValue="AppointmentData">
                <ScheduleGroup Resources="@Resources" AllowGroupEdit="true"></ScheduleGroup>
                <ScheduleResources>
                    <ScheduleResource TItem="ResourceData" TValue="int[]" DataSource="@OwnersData" Field="OwnerId" Title="Owner" Name="Owners" TextField="Text" IdField="Id" GroupIDField="OwnerGroupId" AllowMultiple="true"></ScheduleResource>
                </ScheduleResources>
            </SfSchedule>
            @code {
                string[] Resources { get; set; } = { "Owners" };
                public List<ResourceData> OwnersData { get; set; } = new List<ResourceData>
                {
                    new ResourceData{ Text = "Nancy", Id = 1 },
                    new ResourceData{ Text = "Steven", Id = 2 }
                };
                public class AppointmentData
                {
                    public int Id { get; set; }
                    public string Subject { get; set; }
                    public DateTime StartTime { get; set; }
                    public DateTime EndTime { get; set; }
                    public int[] OwnerId { get; set; }
                }
                public class ResourceData
                {
                    public int Id { get; set; }
                    public string Text { get; set; }
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleGroup.ByDate

member.value: Set to `true` to group resources by date, where each day will render all the resource names under it. The default value is `false`.
member.remarks: This property is applicable only for Day, Week, WorkWeek, Month and Agenda Views.

member.value: Set to `false` to map all the resources in the child collection to each available parent. The default value is `true`.

member.summary: Gets or sets whether to display the resource grouping layout in normal or compact mode on mobile devices.
member.value: Set to `false` to display the default grouping layout on mobile devices, with scrolling enabled. The default value is `false`.

member.value: A template content that specifies the visualization of resource header tooltip. By default, no tooltip will be displayed on resource header.

example.code:
@{ var resourceData = (context as TemplateContext).ResourceData as ResourceData;
@(resourceData.Text)

member.summary: Gets or sets whether to show/hide the non-working days.
member.value: true, to hide the non-working days. The default value is `false`.
member.remarks: This property is only applicable when is set to `true`, and only affects the Day, Week, WorkWeek, and Month views.

member.value: The collection should be an array of strings. The default value is `null`.

member.summary: It defines the header row type, which accepts either of the following values. Year Month Week Date Hour.
Gets or sets the header row type that needs be rendered on timeline views.
member.value: One of the enumeration.
member.remarks: If the HeaderRowType is Year, renders the year row in timeline view header. If the HeaderRowType is Month, renders the month row in timeline view header. <SfSchedule TValue="AppointmentData">

                {

                    public string Color { get; set; }

member.example:
The following code example shows how to configure the views in scheduler:
<SfSchedule TValue="AppointmentData"> <ScheduleViews> <ScheduleView Option="View.Day"></ScheduleView> <ScheduleView Option="View.Week"></ScheduleView> <ScheduleView Option="View.WorkWeek"></ScheduleView> <ScheduleView Option="View.Month"></ScheduleView> </ScheduleViews> </SfSchedule>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleView.AllowVirtualScrolling
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether to allow the virtual scrolling functionality.
member.value: `true` to enable virtual scrolling. The default value is `false`.
member.remarks: This property is applicable only when resource grouping is enabled, and in agenda view resource grouping should be disabled. It is mandatory to set the property for schedule, when enable AllowVirtualScrolling property.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleView.EnableVirtualMask
member.summary: Gets or sets the virtual mask to the work cells for virtual scrolling actions.
member.value: `true` to enable virtual mask. The default value is `false`.

example.code: <SfSchedule TValue="EventData" Width="100%" Height="600px"> <ScheduleGroup Resources="@GroupData"></ScheduleGroup> <ScheduleResources> <ScheduleResource TItem = "ResourceData" TValue="int[]" DataSource="@ResourceDatasource" Field="ResourceId" Title="Resource" Name="Resources" TextField="Text" IdField="Id" ColorField="Color" AllowMultiple="true"></ScheduleResource> </ScheduleResources> <ScheduleViews> <ScheduleView Option="View.TimelineMonth" AllowVirtualScrolling="true" EnableVirtualMask="true"></ScheduleView> </ScheduleViews> </SfSchedule>

member.remarks: This property is applicable only when property is enabled. The Virtual Mask allows it to render only work cells visible within the view-port without buffering the entire resource collection. Here, same set of DOM elements is re-used to improve the performance. In this feature, a loading placeholder indicator was shown while loading the new data.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleView.AllowOverlap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether overlapping appointments are allowed within the same time slot in the Scheduler. The default value is true.
member.remarks:
When set to false, the Scheduler enforces restrictions to prevent creating or displaying overlapping appointments within the same time duration. This setting is subject to the following limitations:
Initial Loading: The alert for overlapping appointments will not be displayed during the initial load. Overlap events will be ignored during rendering, including their occurrences.
Dynamic Add/Edit: While dynamically adding or editing events, overlapping validation is performed. If an overlap is detected for a normal event, an alert will be shown, and the event will not be saved in the Scheduler. For recurring events, an alert will be displayed, and the event will not be saved in the Scheduler. If users want to save the recurring events while ignoring overlapping occurrences, they must trigger the `PopupOpen` event. The `Data` field will contain the parent recurrence data, and the `OverlapEvents` field will hold the overlap events. Users can then include exceptions in the recurrence events and save the event using the `AddEvent` method.
Out of Date Range Events: The setting only prevents overlaps for events within the current view date range. If users want to consider and prevent overlaps outside the current date range, they must implement their validation in the `ActionBegin` event. If overlapping events are detected, they can cancel the event and show the alert by calling the `OpenOverlapAlertAsync` method if required.
member.value: true if overlapping appointments are allowed (default); otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleView.EnableLazyLoading
member.summary: Gets or sets whether to enable the lazy loading of events for virtual scrolling actions.
member.value: `true` to enable lazy loading of appointments. The default value is `false`.

example.code: <SfSchedule TValue="EventData" Width="100%" Height="600px"> <ScheduleGroup Resources="@GroupData"></ScheduleGroup> <ScheduleResources> <ScheduleResource TItem = "ResourceData" TValue="int[]" DataSource="@ResourceDatasource" Field="ResourceId" Title="Resource" Name="Resources" TextField="Text" IdField="Id" ColorField="Color" AllowMultiple="true"></ScheduleResource> </ScheduleResources> <ScheduleViews> <ScheduleView Option="View.TimelineMonth" AllowVirtualScrolling="true" EnableLazyLoading="true"></ScheduleView> </ScheduleViews> </SfSchedule>

member.remarks: Lazy loading allows the scheduler to fetch the appointments dynamically during scroll actions for the currently rendered resource collection. New data is fetched on-demand as the user scrolls through the schedule content. This helps to improve the scheduler's performance, when loading a large number of appointments.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleView.VirtualResourceCount
member.summary: Gets or sets the number of resources to be renders only in the content viewport.
member.value: Accepts a value of integer type. The default value is `null`.

example.code: <SfSchedule TValue="EventData" Height="550px"> <ScheduleGroup Resources="@GroupData"></ScheduleGroup> <ScheduleResources> <ScheduleResource TItem = "ResourceData" TValue="int[]" DataSource="@ResourceDatasource" Field="ResourceId" Title="Resource" Name="Resources" TextField="Text" IdField="Id" ColorField="Color" AllowMultiple="true"></ScheduleResource> </ScheduleResources> <ScheduleViews> <ScheduleView Option="View.TimelineMonth" AllowVirtualScrolling="true" VirtualResourceCount="20"></ScheduleView> </ScheduleViews> </SfSchedule>

member.remarks: property is only applicable for resources virtual scrolling in timeline views. If this property value is not set, then the number of resources to be displayed in the scheduler is determined implicitly by height of the content area. The provided count must be two times larger than the number of visible resources in the scheduler.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleViewGroup
member.summary: A class that represents the view-specific resource grouping related configurations by rendering ScheduleViewGroup as child content in tag.
member.remarks: You can configure the view wise resource grouping by specifying values for the corresponding properties.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleViewGroup.ChildContent
member.summary: Gets or sets the child content of schedule group.
member.value: The value used to build the content.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.ScheduleViewGroup.AllowGroupEdit
member.summary: Gets or sets whether the group editing is enabled in the scheduler.
member.value: Set to `true` to treat multiple resources as a single appointment object in the scheduler's dataSource. The default value is `false`
member.remarks: Group editing is performed on multiple resources based on the value on appointments. It is mandatory to group the resources as an array type and map them to the appointment data's resource field.

example.code:
<SfSchedule TValue="AppointmentData">
                <ScheduleResources>
                    <ScheduleResource TItem="ResourceData" TValue="int[]" DataSource="@OwnersData" Field="OwnerId" Title="Owner" Name="Owners" TextField="Text" IdField="Id" GroupIDField="OwnerGroupId" AllowMultiple="true"></ScheduleResource>
                </ScheduleResources>
                <ScheduleViews>
                    <ScheduleView Option="View.Week">
                        <ScheduleViewGroup Resources="@Resources" AllowGroupEdit="true"></ScheduleViewGroup>
                    </ScheduleView>
                </ScheduleViews>
            </SfSchedule>
            @code {
                string[] Resources { get; set; } = { "Owners" };
                public List<ResourceData> OwnersData { get; set; } = new List<ResourceData>
                {
                    new ResourceData{ Text = "Nancy", Id = 1 },
                    new ResourceData{ Text = "Steven", Id = 2 }
                };
                public class AppointmentData
                {
                    public int Id { get; set; }
                    public string Subject { get; set; }
                    public DateTime StartTime { get; set; }
                    public DateTime EndTime { get; set; }
                    public int[] OwnerId { get; set; }
                }
                public class ResourceData
                {
                    public int Id { get; set; }
                    public string Text { get; set; }
                }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.SfSchedule`1.WorkDays
member.summary: Gets or sets the working days on the schedule.
member.value: An array of integer values based on the enumeration.
member.example:
In below code example Monday, Wednesday and Friday were set as workdays for week view.

member.remarks: The defined days in the collection will be rendered in the `WorkWeek` view. In other views, all usual days will be displayed, and working days will be highlighted with a different shade.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.SfSchedule`1.AllowOverlap
member.summary: Gets or sets a value indicating whether overlapping appointments are allowed within the same time slot in the Scheduler. The default value is true.
member.remarks:
When set to false, the Scheduler enforces restrictions to prevent creating or displaying overlapping appointments within the same time duration. This setting is subject to the following limitations:
Initial Loading: The alert for overlapping appointments will not be displayed during the initial load. Overlap events will be ignored during rendering, including their occurrences.
Dynamic Add/Edit: While dynamically adding or editing events, overlapping validation is performed. If an overlap is detected for a normal event, an alert will be shown, and the event will not be saved in the Scheduler. For recurring events, an alert will be displayed, and the event will not be saved in the Scheduler. If users want to save the recurring events while ignoring overlapping occurrences, they must trigger the `PopupOpen` event. The `Data` field will contain the parent recurrence data, and the `OverlapEvents` field will hold the overlap events. Users can then include exceptions in the recurrence events and save the event using the `AddEvent` method.
Out of Date Range Events: The setting only prevents overlaps for events within the current view date range. If users want to consider and prevent overlaps outside the current date range, they must implement their validation in the `ActionBegin` event.
member.value: true if overlapping appointments are allowed (default); otherwise, false.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.Schedule.SfSchedule`1.WeekRule
member.summary: Gets or sets the week rule to be applied on the scheduler.
member.value: One of the enumeration values. The default value is .
member.remarks: The available values for the week rule are: - `FirstDay`: The week starts on the first day of the month. - `FirstFullWeek`: The week starts on the first full week of the month. - `FirstFourDayWeek`: The week starts on the first four-day week of the month.

member.remarks: The theme determines the visual appearance of the spinner, including its shape, color, and animation. Each theme corresponds to a different design system, such as Material, Bootstrap, or Fluent. By default, the spinner will inherit the theme from the application.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.SplitButtons.SfSplitButton
member.summary: SplitButton component has primary and secondary button. Primary button is used to select default action and secondary button is used to toggle contextual overlays for displaying list of action items. It can contain both text and images.
member.example:
In the below code example, a basic SplitButton component initialized with and tag directives.
<SfSplitButton> <DropDownMenuItems> <DropDownMenuItem Text="Dashboard"></DropDownMenuItem> <DropDownMenuItem Text="Notifications"></DropDownMenuItem> <DropDownMenuItem Text="User Settings"></DropDownMenuItem> <DropDownMenuItem Text="Log Out"></DropDownMenuItem> </DropDownMenuItems> </SfSplitButton>
member.summary: The SplitButton component features a primary button for a default action and a secondary button that toggles a dropdown with a list of additional action items.
member.remarks: The component can be customized with text, images, or both, providing a flexible and intuitive user interface.
member.example:
In this example, a is configured with several options.
<SfSplitButton Content="Paste"> <SplitButtonItems> <SplitButtonItem Text="Paste" /> <SplitButtonItem Text="Paste Special" /> <SplitButtonItem Text="Paste as Formula" /> <SplitButtonItem Text="Paste as Hyperlink" /> </SplitButtonItems> </SfSplitButton>
member.summary: The SplitButton component contains a primary button and a secondary button. The primary button is used to select a default action, while the secondary button toggles a contextual overlay with a list of action items. The button can display both text and images.
member.remarks: The is a versatile component that combines the functionality of a button with a dropdown menu. It is ideal for scenarios where you need to provide a default action while also offering a set of related options.

example.para: In this example, a is configured with a list of items. When the user clicks the primary button, the default action is triggered. Clicking the dropdown arrow reveals additional options.
example.code: <SfSplitButton Content="Save"> <DropDownMenuItems> <DropDownMenuItem Text="Save as..." /> <DropDownMenuItem Text="Save and close" /> </DropDownMenuItems> </SfSplitButton>

member.summary: A Split Button component that allows users to select a default action from the primary button or choose from a list of additional actions in the dropdown.
member.remarks: The combines the functionality of a button with a dropdown menu. It features a primary button for the main action and a secondary button that reveals a list of related actions. This component is ideal for scenarios where you need to group several related commands under a single element, with one command designated as the default.

member.summary: `ColumnMenuItems` defines both built-in and custom column menu items. The available built-in items are, `AutoFitAll` - Auto fit the size of all columns. `AutoFit` - Auto fit the current column. `SortAscending` - Sort the current column in ascending order. `SortDescending` - Sort the current column in descending order. `Filter` - Filter options will show based on filterSettings property like filterbar, menu filter.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.Internal.ITreeGrid.ColumnQueryMode
member.summary: `ColumnQueryMode` provides options to retrieves data from the data source. Their types are `All`: It retrieves whole data source. `Schema`: retrieves data for all the defined columns in TreeGrid from the data source. `ExcludeHidden`: retrieves data only for visible columns of TreeGrid from the data Source.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.Internal.ITreeGrid.ContextMenuItems
member.summary: `ContextMenuItems` defines both built-in and custom context menu items. The available built-in items are, `AutoFitAll` - Auto fit the size of all columns. `AutoFit` - Auto fit the current column. `Edit` - Edit the current record. `Delete` - Delete the current record. `Save` - Save the edited record. `Cancel` - Cancel the edited state. `PdfExport` - Export the grid as Pdf format. `ExcelExport` - Export the grid as Excel format. `CsvExport` - Export the grid as CSV format. `SortAscending` - Sort the current column in ascending order. `SortDescending` - Sort the current column in descending order. `FirstPage` - Go to the first page. `PrevPage` - Go to the previous page. `LastPage` - Go to the last page. `NextPage` - Go to the next page.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.Internal.ITreeGrid.CopyHierarchyMode

The available built-in items are, `Parent` - Copy the selected data with parent record. `Child` - Copy the selected data with child record. `Both` - Copy the selected data with both parent and child record. `None` - Copy only the selected record.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.Internal.FilterModule`1.BuildHierarchyMaps(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Object})
member.summary: Builds internal hierarchical lookup dictionaries (_itemLookup, _childMap, _parentLookup) for fast parent/child navigation in filtering operations.
member.param: The collection of TreeListItem<T> objects representing the source TreeGrid data, typically after flattening.

remarks.para: This method constructs optimized lookup structures essential for hierarchical filtering in TreeGrid:

item.description: _itemLookup: Maps unique IDs to TreeListItem objects for O(1) item retrieval
_childMap: Groups children by parent ID for efficient parent-to-children navigation
_parentLookup: Maps child IDs to parent objects for child-to-parent traversal
_originalOrderMap: Preserves data source order for consistent result ordering

remarks.para: Performance characteristics: - Time complexity: O(n) where n is the number of records - Space complexity: O(n) for the lookup dictionaries - Includes intelligent caching to avoid rebuilding when data hasn't changed

This method is called automatically before filtering operations and supports both ChildMapping (hierarchical data) and self-referential (ParentId-based) data structures. Essential for TreeGrid filtering modes: Parent, Child, Both, and None.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.Internal.TreeDataItem`1.Level
member.summary: Gets the depth of the record from the root records of the tree.
member.value: The level of the record from the root record of the tree. The default value is 0.
member.remarks: The level determines the depth of the record from the root record of the tree. The 0th level represents the root records, 1st level represents the first child record, and so on. member.summary: Constructs a hierarchical TreeGrid structure from flat data by recursively sorting and organizing Orders the records based on parent-child relationships.
member.param: The collection of raw sorted data(parents and children) from which the dictionary and hierarchy structure are built.
The collection where the hierarchy structure of the tree grid is maintained.

remarks.para: This method uses a recursive strategy to traverse and organize child records under their respective parents. It leverages caching and pre-allocation to improve performance, especially for large datasets.
Recommended for scrollable data in tree grid for better performance during sorting.

member.name: M:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.SfTreeGrid`1.BuildHierarchyMapsAsync(System.Collections.Generic.IEnumerable{System.Object})
member.summary: Asynchronously constructs hierarchical lookup dictionaries (itemLookup and childMap) for TreeGrid records, optimized for parallel execution on large data sets.
member.param: The collection of raw TreeListItem<TValue> items (parents and children) from which to build the hierarchy.

remarks.para: This method leverages parallelization and optimized thread-safe data structures to efficiently precompute parent, child, and order mappings across the TreeGrid. It minimizes reflection and redundant enumeration by caching property accessors, and is designed to be used during or after initial data loading to accelerate later filtering or hierarchy operations.
Invoke this method from initial render or after major data changes to optimize TreeGrid performance for filtering, sorting, or virtualized rendering scenarios.

Gets or sets how to display the text content in the tree grid cell when it overflows.
One of the enumeration values. Default is ClipMode.Ellipsis.
The available modes are:
Clip: Truncates the cell content when it overflows its area.
Ellipsis: Displays ellipsis when the cell content overflows its area.
EllipsisWithTooltip: Displays ellipsis when the cell content overflows its area and also displays a tooltip on mouse hover.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.SfTreeGrid`1.ColumnMenuItems
member.summary: Gets or sets both built-in and custom column menu items. Built-in items are provided as a list of objects, and custom column menu items are provided as a List instance of 'Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ColumnMenuItemModel'.
member.value: The available built-in items include: `AutoFitAll`: Auto fit the size of all columns. `AutoFit`: Auto fit the current column. `SortAscending`: Sort the current column in ascending order. `SortDescending`: Sort the current column in descending order. `Filter`: Filter options will show based on filterSettings property like filterbar, menu filter.
member.remarks: Actions for custom column menu items can be handled through the 'Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridEvents.ColumnMenuItemClicked' event.

example.code: <SfTreeGrid DataSource="@TreeGridData" ColumnMenuItems="@(new List<object>() { "AutoFit", "AutoFitAll", "SortAscending", "SortDescending" })" > </SfTreeGrid>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.SfTreeGrid`1.ColumnQueryMode
member.summary: Gets or sets how to query the column values of the data source.
member.remarks:
The types are:
All: Retrieves the whole data source with all columns.
Schema: Retrieves data only for the defined from the data source.
ExcludeHidden: Retrieves data only for property enabled columns from the data source.
member.value: One of the enumeration values that specifies how the data source fields are retrieved. The default mode is Syncfusion.Blazor.Grids.ColumnQueryModeType.All.

member.summary: Gets or sets a value that determines whether the header remains fixed in position when scrolling the tree grid content vertically.
member.value: A indicating whether the column headers remain sticky at the top while scrolling through tree grid content. The default value is .

remarks.para: When , the header will remain visible at the top of the viewport as users scroll down through tree grid data, improving navigation and context retention.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridAggregateColumn.Type
member.summary:
Defines the aggregate type of a particular column.
Types of aggregate supported in-built are,
- Performs sum aggregation.
- Performs average aggregation.
- Performs count aggregation. - Performs false count aggregation.
- Performs true count aggregation.
- Performs max aggregation.
- Performs min aggregation.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridColumn.Columns
member.summary: Used to render multiple header rows (stacked headers) on TreeGrid header.
member.value: A list of instances.
member.remarks: Stacked headers allow grouping columns under a common header. This feature enables better organization of columns where multiple columns can be grouped to reflect a hierarchy of information. It is useful to represent complex data structures.

example.code:
<SfTreeGrid DataSource="@TreeGridData" IdMapping="TaskId" ParentIdMapping="ParentId">
                <TreeGridColumns>
                    <TreeGridColumn HeaderText="Task Details" Columns="@new List<TreeGridColumn> {
                        new sTreeGridColumn { Field = "TaskName", HeaderText = "Task Name" },
                        new TreeGridColumn { Field = "StartDate", HeaderText = "Start Date", Format = "yyyy-MM-dd" }
                    }">
                    </TreeGridColumn>
                </TreeGridColumns>
            </SfTreeGrid>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridColumn.Commands
member.summary: Commands provides an option to display command buttons in every cell.
member.value: A list of instances.

example.code: <SfTreeGrid DataSource="@TreeGridData" IdMapping="TaskId" ParentIdMapping="ParentId"> <TreeGridColumns> <TreeGridColumn HeaderText="Manage Records" Width="150" Commands="@new List<TreeGridCommandColumn> { new TreeGridCommandColumn { Type = CommandButtonType.Edit, ButtonOption = new CommandButtonOptions { IconCss = "e-icons e-edit", CssClass = "e-flat" } }, new TreeGridCommandColumn { Type = CommandButtonType.Delete, ButtonOption = new CommandButtonOptions { IconCss = "e-icons e-delete", CssClass = "e-flat" } }, new TreeGridCommandColumn { Type = CommandButtonType.Save, ButtonOption = new CommandButtonOptions { IconCss = "e-icons e-save", CssClass = "e-flat" } }, new TreeGridCommandColumn { Type = CommandButtonType.Cancel, ButtonOption = new CommandButtonOptions { IconCss = "e-icons e-cancel-icon", CssClass = "e-flat" } } }"> </TreeGridColumn> </TreeGridColumns> </SfTreeGrid>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridCommandColumn.Type
member.summary: Gets or sets the type of the command button.
member.value:
One of the enumeration values that defines the button type. The default is None. None - Default. A command button with no default action. Use this for custom command actions.
Edit - A edit command button that edit current record.
Delete - A delete command button that delete current record.
Save - A save command button that saves the current edited record.
Cancel - A cancel command button that cancels the edit state.
member.remarks: To use custom command button, set Type as and use event to perform custom action.

            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridEvents`1.BeforeCopyPaste
member.summary: An event that is raised before a copy or paste action in the Grid cells. You can cancel the copy or paste action by cancelling this event.
member.value: An event callback function.
member.remarks: This event triggers before event, so you can cancel the copy or paste operation by using this event. Also, this event handler receives a object which provides the details of the before paste/copy action.

example.code:
<SfTreeGrid DataSource="@TreeData" @ref="TreeGrid" >
               <TreeGridEvents BeforeCopyPaste="CopyPaste"></TreeGridEvents>
             </SfTreeGrid>
             @code{
              public async Task CopyPaste(BeforeCopyPasteEventArgs args)
              {
                    // you can cancel the entire copy action here
                 if(args.Action == "Copy"){
                    args.Cancel = true;
                 }
                    // you can cancel the entire paste action here
                 if(args.Action == "Paste"){
                    args.Cancel = true;
                 }
              }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridEvents`1.BeforeCellPaste
member.summary: An event that is raised before pasting the copied cell value in the corresponding cells. You can cancel the paste on a particular cell by handling this event.
member.value: An event callback function.
member.remarks: This event handler receives a object which provides the details for the before cell paste action. The paste event action can be cancelled by setting the Cancel property of the property.

example.code:
<SfTreeGrid DataSource="@TreeData" @ref="TreeGrid" >
            <TreeGridEvents TValue="BusinessObject" BeforeCellPaste="CellPaste"></TreeGridEvents>
            </SfTreeGrid>
            @code{
             public async Task Paste(BeforeCellPasteEventArgs<BusinessObject> args)
             {
              if(ColumnIndex == 1 && RowIndex == 4){
                  // you can modify the content to be pasted here.
                 args.CellValue = "Modified value";
             }
            }

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridEvents`1.ExcelAggregateTemplateInfo
member.summary: Gets or sets the delegate that is invoked when caption, footer aggregate rows are generated during an Excel export.
member.value: An where T is . The default value is .

remarks.para: This callback is executed only during Excel export (for example, when the user clicks the Excel export toolbar item or when export is triggered programmatically).
The delegate is raised for each applicable aggregate section (caption, footer), allowing customization of text, formatting, and styles in the generated Excel sheet.
If this property is , the export proceeds with default aggregate rendering.

member.name: T:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings
member.summary: Configures Tree Grid key settings.
member.remarks: The properties set to TreeGridKeySettings will handle and/or prevent hot key's default action.

example.code: <SfTreeGrid @ref="TreeGrid" DataSource="@TreeGridData"> <TreeGridKeySettings MoveLeftCell="Shift+Left" MoveRightCell="Tab" MoveUpCell="UpArrow" MoveDownCell=""></TreeGridKeySettings> ........ </SfTreeGrid>

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings.MoveLeftCell
member.summary:
Defines the action keys for the left cell movement.
Shift+Tab Moves to left cell on pressing Shift+Tab key
ArrowLeft Moves to left cell on pressing LeftArrow key
ShiftLeft Moves to left cell on pressing Shift+LeftArrow key
The default value are Shift+Tab,LeftArrow,Shift+LeftArrow.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings.MoveRightCell
member.summary:
Defines the action keys for the right cell movement.
Tab Moves to right cell on pressing Tab key
RightArrow Moves to right cell on pressing RightArrow key
Shift+RightArrow Moves to right cell on pressing Shift+RightArrow key
The default value are Tab,RightArrow,Shift+RightArrow.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings.MoveUpCell
member.summary:
Defines the action keys for the up cell movement.
Shift+Enter Moves to top cell on pressing Shit+Enter key
UpArrow Moves to top cell on pressing UpArrow key
Shift+UpArrow Moves to top cell on pressing Shift+UpArrow key
The default value are Shift+Enter,UpArrow,Shift+UpArrow.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings.MoveDownCell
member.summary:
Defines the action keys for the down cell movement.
Enter Moves to down cell on pressing Enter key
DownArrow Moves to down cell on pressing DownArrow key
Shift+DownArrow Moves to down cell on pressing Shift+DownArrow key
The default value are Enter,DownArrow,Shift+DownArrow.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings.IndentRow
member.summary:
Defines the action keys for indenting the row.
Alt+Shift+RightArrow Indent the row on pressing Alt+Shift+RightArrow keys
The default value is Alt+Shift+RightArrow.

member.name: P:Syncfusion.Blazor.TreeGrid.TreeGridKeySettings.OutdentRow
member.summary:
Defines the action keys for outdenting the row.
Alt+Shift+LeftArrow Indent the row on pressing Alt+Shift+LeftArrow keys
The default value is AltShiftLeft.
